raw_candidates.name: Chain-of-thought prompting
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CoT showed elicited reasoning traces dramatically raise LLM task accuracy; ReAct's thought actions are CoT traces interleaved with environment actions.
raw_candidates.definition: Prompting technique (Wei et al., 2022) in which few-shot exemplars contain step-by-step reasoning, eliciting intermediate reasoning from an LLM before its answer.
raw_candidates.source_title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models

raw_candidates.name: In-context learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ReAct is delivered entirely as few-shot in-context exemplars: the thought-action-observation format exists only as prompt conditioning, the capability ICL established.
raw_candidates.definition: The ability of a pretrained LM (demonstrated at scale by GPT-3, 2020) to perform a new task from examples and instructions in its prompt, with no parameter updates.
raw_candidates.source_title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

raw_candidates.name: Scratchpads
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Scratchpads showed models compute better when allowed to emit intermediate steps into a buffer; ReAct's thought stream is a scratchpad interleaved with actions.
raw_candidates.definition: Technique (Nye et al., 2021) training/prompting models to write intermediate computation into a 'scratchpad' before answering, improving multi-step arithmetic and code execution prediction.
raw_candidates.source_title: Show Your Work: Scratchpads for Intermediate Computation with Language Models

raw_candidates.name: Least-to-most prompting
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Least-to-most decomposed hard problems into sequenced subproblems shortly before ReAct; a sibling prompting strategy for multi-step reasoning.
raw_candidates.definition: Prompting strategy (Zhou et al., 2022) that decomposes a problem into subproblems solved in sequence, each answer feeding the next prompt.
raw_candidates.source_title: Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in Large Language Models

raw_candidates.name: Self-consistency
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Self-consistency improved CoT by sampling and marginalizing over reasoning paths; a decoding-side sibling of ReAct's single-trajectory loop.
raw_candidates.definition: Decoding strategy (Wang et al., 2022) sampling multiple CoT reasoning paths and taking the majority answer, substantially raising reasoning benchmark scores.
raw_candidates.source_title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models

raw_candidates.name: STaR: Self-Taught Reasoner
raw_candidates.causal_claim: STaR bootstrapped rationale generation from few exemplars, showing reasoning traces could be elicited and improved without large rationale datasets.
raw_candidates.definition: Bootstrapping method (Zelikman et al., 2022) in which a model generates rationales for problems, keeps those reaching correct answers, and fine-tunes on them.
raw_candidates.source_title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning

raw_candidates.name: Zero-shot chain-of-thought
raw_candidates.causal_claim: 'Let's think step by step' showed reasoning traces could be elicited with no exemplars at all, sharpening the reasoning/acting contrast ReAct built on.
raw_candidates.definition: Finding (Kojima et al., 2022) that appending 'Let's think step by step' elicits reasoning traces from LLMs zero-shot, large gains on reasoning tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners

raw_candidates.name: Selection-inference
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Selection-inference decomposed reasoning into LLM selection and inference steps over facts, a modular sibling of ReAct's interleaving.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Creswell et al., 2022) alternating an LLM selection module (pick relevant facts) and inference module (derive one step), for faithful multi-step reasoning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Selection-Inference: Exploiting Large Language Models for Interpretable Logical Reasoning

raw_candidates.name: Decomposed prompting
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Decomposed prompting split complex tasks into sub-tasks routed to specialized LLM calls, a modular sibling architecture to ReAct's loop.
raw_candidates.definition: Approach (Khot et al., 2022) decomposing a complex task into sub-tasks, each handled by an LLM prompt or handler, composed by a controller.
raw_candidates.source_title: Decomposed Prompting: A Modular Approach for Solving Complex Tasks

raw_candidates.name: Automatic prompt engineering
raw_candidates.causal_claim: APE automated the search for effective instructions, part of the 2022 prompting-methods wave surrounding ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Zhou et al., 2022) using an LLM to propose and select natural-language instructions automatically, matching human prompt engineering.
raw_candidates.source_title: Large Language Models Are Human-Level Prompt Engineers

raw_candidates.name: Large-scale pretraining (GPT-3)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ReAct's experiments prompt GPT-3 and PaLM; the pretrained model is the substrate whose in-context behavior the ReAct format steers.
raw_candidates.definition: 175B-parameter autoregressive LM (Brown et al., 2020) whose few-shot in-context performance made prompt-based task specification practical at scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

raw_candidates.name: PaLM
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PaLM-540B was ReAct's strongest base model; its scale supplied the emergent reasoning ReAct's exemplars elicited.
raw_candidates.definition: 540B dense decoder LM (Chowdhery et al., 2022) trained with Pathways, showing strong emergent reasoning and few-shot performance.
raw_candidates.source_title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways

raw_candidates.name: Codex code generation model
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ReAct's GPT-3 experiments used the davinci-series API models descended from the GPT-3/Codex line; Codex showed prompted models executing structured action-like outputs.
raw_candidates.definition: GPT-3 fine-tuned on public code (Chen et al., 2021); powered GitHub Copilot and scored 28.8% on HumanEval, showing prompted models producing executable structured output.
raw_candidates.source_title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code

raw_candidates.name: Instruction tuning (FLAN)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: FLAN showed instruction-formatted multitask tuning unlocks zero-shot task following; ReAct instead used base models, but FLAN defined the instruction-following contrast class.
raw_candidates.definition: Fine-tuning a 137B LM on 60+ datasets phrased as instructions (Wei et al., 2021), yielding large zero-shot gains on unseen task types.
raw_candidates.source_title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners

raw_candidates.name: Hosted LLM APIs (OpenAI API)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ReAct was run through hosted API access to GPT-3-class models; API serving made prompt-loop experiments a commodity.
raw_candidates.definition: Commercial API access to GPT-3 (June 2020), which turned large-model prompting into an on-demand service any researcher could loop over.
raw_candidates.source_title: OpenAI API announcement

raw_candidates.name: LaMDA
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LaMDA demonstrated dialog-tuned LLMs at scale in early 2022, part of the model wave ReAct drew on; not used in ReAct's experiments.
raw_candidates.definition: Dialog-specialized LLM family (Thoppilan et al., 2022) fine-tuned for grounded, sensible conversation.
raw_candidates.source_title: LaMDA: Language Models for Dialog Applications

raw_candidates.name: Chinchilla
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Chinchilla reset the compute-optimal scaling recipe in 2022; a scaling-law sibling result, not an input to ReAct's method.
raw_candidates.definition: 70B LM (Hoffmann et al., 2022) establishing compute-optimal parameter/token balance, outperforming much larger models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models

raw_candidates.name: Gopher
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Gopher was a 280B contemporary of the models ReAct used, documenting emergent few-shot abilities at scale.
raw_candidates.definition: 280B LM (Rae et al., 2021) from DeepMind with extensive analysis of scale-driven capability gains and risks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Scaling Language Models: Methods, Analysis & Insights from Training Gopher

raw_candidates.name: T5 text-to-text framework
raw_candidates.causal_claim: T5 unified tasks as text-to-text, an ancestor of the prompt-as-interface idea ReAct exploits; ReAct used decoder LMs, not T5.
raw_candidates.definition: Transfer-learning framework (Raffel et al., 2019) casting every NLP task as text-in/text-out, with an 11B encoder-decoder model.
raw_candidates.source_title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

raw_candidates.name: BERT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BERT established the pretrain-then-adapt paradigm ReAct inherited, but ReAct's generative prompting bypassed encoder fine-tuning entirely.
raw_candidates.definition: Bidirectionally pretrained encoder (Devlin et al., 2018) whose fine-tuned representations reset NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

raw_candidates.name: GPT-2
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-2 first showed conditioning alone elicits tasks zero-shot, the direct empirical precedent for the prompting substrate ReAct builds on.
raw_candidates.definition: 1.5B LM (Radford et al., 2019) demonstrating zero-shot task transfer by text conditioning, improving log-linearly with scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

raw_candidates.name: SayCan
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: SayCan grounded LLM plans in robot affordances months before ReAct; the leading sibling approach to LLM acting, compared against ReAct's setting.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Ahn et al., 2022) pairing an LLM's task knowledge ('Say') with learned affordance values ('Can') to ground plans for a mobile manipulator.
raw_candidates.source_title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances

raw_candidates.name: Inner Monologue
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Inner Monologue fed environment feedback back into an LLM planner in text form, the closest contemporaneous sibling to ReAct's observation loop.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Huang et al., 2022) giving an LLM planner textual environment feedback (success detection, scene description) for closed-loop robotic planning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models

raw_candidates.name: MRKL systems
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MRKL routed LLM calls to external tools and knowledge sources months before ReAct; the verifier already flagged it as ReAct's near-simultaneous multiple.
raw_candidates.definition: Neuro-symbolic architecture (Karpas et al., 2022) in which an LLM router dispatches to expert modules: calculators, APIs, knowledge bases.
raw_candidates.source_title: MRKL Systems: A modular, neuro-symbolic architecture that combines large language models, external knowledge sources and discrete reasoning

raw_candidates.name: Language models as zero-shot planners
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Huang et al. showed LLMs could decompose embodied tasks into executable steps zero-shot, defining the act-only baseline ReAct's reasoning was measured against.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Huang et al., 2022) translating LLM-generated high-level plans into admissible embodied actions via sentence-embedding matching.
raw_candidates.source_title: Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners: Extracting Actionable Knowledge for Embodied Agents

raw_candidates.name: WebGPT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: WebGPT fine-tuned GPT-3 to browse the web with search and citation actions, an early demonstration of an LLM operating a tool interface in a loop.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Nakano et al., 2021) fine-tuning GPT-3 to use a text-based browser (search, click, scroll) and answer questions with citations, preferred over humans on ELI5.
raw_candidates.source_title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback

raw_candidates.name: ProgPrompt
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ProgPrompt generated program-like robot plans with assertion-based recovery, a code-as-policy sibling of ReAct's loop.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Singh et al., 2022) prompting LLMs to emit Pythonic robot action programs with assertions enabling environment feedback and recovery.
raw_candidates.source_title: ProgPrompt: Generating Situated Robot Task Plans using Large Language Models

raw_candidates.name: Gato
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Gato showed a single transformer acting across embodiments and modalities in 2022; a generalist-agent sibling, not an input to ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Multi-modal, multi-task agent (Reed et al., 2022): one 1.2B transformer playing Atari, captioning images, and controlling a robot arm.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Generalist Agent

raw_candidates.name: Decision Transformer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Decision Transformer reframed RL as sequence modeling over trajectories, part of the transformer-meets-acting wave; ReAct's acting is prompt-based, not return-conditioned.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Chen et al., 2021) casting offline RL as conditional sequence modeling, generating actions from desired returns and past trajectories.
raw_candidates.source_title: Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling

raw_candidates.name: Trajectory Transformer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Trajectory Transformer modeled offline RL trajectories for planning by beam search; a sequence-modeling sibling with no channel into ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Janner et al., 2021) modeling distributions over trajectories with a transformer and planning via beam search.
raw_candidates.source_title: Offline Reinforcement Learning as One Big Sequence Modeling Problem

raw_candidates.name: Retrieval-augmented generation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: RAG coupled an LM to a retriever for knowledge tasks; ReAct's Wikipedia actions generalize that retrieve-then-reason pattern into an interactive loop.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Lewis et al., 2020) combining a pretrained retriever with a generator, state of the art on open-domain QA at introduction.
raw_candidates.source_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

raw_candidates.name: Dense passage retrieval
raw_candidates.causal_claim: DPR made neural retrieval the default knowledge-access layer for QA systems of ReAct's era; ReAct used the Wikipedia API's own search instead.
raw_candidates.definition: Dual-encoder retriever (Karpukhin et al., 2020) outperforming BM25 by wide margins on open-domain QA retrieval.
raw_candidates.source_title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

raw_candidates.name: REALM
raw_candidates.causal_claim: REALM pretrained with retrieval in the loop, an ancestor of retrieve-while-reasoning; ReAct's retrieval happens at inference via actions, not in pretraining.
raw_candidates.definition: Pretraining framework (Guu et al., 2020) augmenting an LM with a neural retriever trained end-to-end on a Wikipedia corpus.
raw_candidates.source_title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training

raw_candidates.name: ALFWorld
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ALFWorld was one of ReAct's two headline testbeds (+34 over baselines); its text-game alignment of embodied tasks made the acting loop measurable.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark (Shridhar et al., 2020) aligning the ALFRED embodied instruction dataset with interactive text games, enabling text-agent evaluation of embodied tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: ALFWorld: Aligning Text and Embodied Environments for Interactive Learning

raw_candidates.name: WebShop
raw_candidates.causal_claim: WebShop was ReAct's second headline testbed (+10); a coeval benchmark, built independently of the method.
raw_candidates.definition: Simulated e-commerce environment (Yao et al., 2022) with 1.18M products and 12k instructions for evaluating web-shopping agents.
raw_candidates.source_title: WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents

raw_candidates.name: HotpotQA
raw_candidates.causal_claim: HotpotQA was ReAct's multi-hop QA testbed, where its Wikipedia search actions were exercised; the benchmark predates and did not shape the method.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Yang et al., 2018) of 113k multi-hop questions requiring reasoning over multiple Wikipedia paragraphs, with supporting-fact annotations.
raw_candidates.source_title: HotpotQA: A Dataset for Diverse, Explainable Multi-hop Question Answering

raw_candidates.name: FEVER
raw_candidates.causal_claim: FEVER was ReAct's fact-verification testbed; its retrieve-and-verify task shape matches ReAct's action set but predates the method by four years.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Thorne et al., 2018) of 185k claims labeled Supported/Refuted/NotEnoughInfo against Wikipedia evidence.
raw_candidates.source_title: FEVER: a large-scale dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification

raw_candidates.name: TextWorld
raw_candidates.causal_claim: TextWorld made text-game agent research a commodity platform; ALFWorld's design descends from it, so its channel to ReAct runs through ALFWorld.
raw_candidates.definition: Microsoft learning environment (Cote et al., 2018) for generating and solving text-based games, used to train and evaluate RL language agents.
raw_candidates.source_title: TextWorld: A Learning Environment for Training Reinforcement Learning Agents, Inspired by Text-based Games

raw_candidates.name: BabyAI
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BabyAI studied grounded instruction following in grid worlds; part of the embodied-instruction lineage, with no channel into ReAct's prompting method.
raw_candidates.definition: Platform (Chevalier-Boisvert et al., 2018) for sample-efficient grounded language learning in a procedurally generated grid world.
raw_candidates.source_title: BabyAI: A Platform to Study the Sample Efficiency of Grounded Language Learning

raw_candidates.name: AI2-THOR
raw_candidates.causal_claim: AI2-THOR supplied the simulated rooms ALFRED/ALFWorld were built in; two steps removed from ReAct's text interface.
raw_candidates.definition: Interactive 3D environment framework (Kolve et al., 2017) of simulated indoor scenes for embodied AI research.
raw_candidates.source_title: AI2-THOR: An Interactive 3D Environment for Visual AI

raw_candidates.name: VirtualHome
raw_candidates.causal_claim: VirtualHome represented household activities as programs, an ancestor of program-style action plans; no channel into ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Simulator (Puig et al., 2018) representing household activities as executable program graphs for activity understanding and planning.
raw_candidates.source_title: VirtualHome: Simulating Household Activities via Programs

raw_candidates.name: ScienceWorld
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ScienceWorld evaluated text agents on science experiments in 2022; a coeval sibling benchmark to ReAct's testbeds.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark (Wang et al., 2022) of 30 science-experiment tasks in a text-simulated environment for interactive agents.
raw_candidates.source_title: ScienceWorld: Is your Agent Smarter than a 5th Grader?

raw_candidates.name: SQuAD
raw_candidates.causal_claim: SQuAD defined extractive reading comprehension as the canonical QA task; ReAct's open-domain QA setting descends from this task lineage at several removes.
raw_candidates.definition: Reading-comprehension dataset (Rajpurkar et al., 2016) of 100k questions over Wikipedia paragraphs, which industrialized extractive QA evaluation.
raw_candidates.source_title: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text

raw_candidates.name: Natural Questions
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Natural Questions anchored open-domain QA evaluation on real search queries; part of the QA task lineage, not an input to ReAct's method.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019) of real anonymized Google queries with Wikipedia answers, standardizing open-domain QA.
raw_candidates.source_title: Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research

raw_candidates.name: TriviaQA
raw_candidates.causal_claim: TriviaQA scaled evidence-based QA with distant supervision; an evaluation-lineage ancestor with no method channel into ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Joshi et al., 2017) of 650k question-answer-evidence triples for reading comprehension over web and Wikipedia evidence.
raw_candidates.source_title: TriviaQA: A Large Scale Distantly Supervised Challenge Dataset for Reading Comprehension

raw_candidates.name: STRIPS planning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: STRIPS formalized action preconditions/effects that 'action' still echoes in agent loops; ReAct consumed no planner formalism - the lineage is conceptual only.
raw_candidates.definition: Automated planner (Fikes & Nilsson, 1971) representing actions by preconditions and add/delete lists, the template for classical planning.
raw_candidates.source_title: STRIPS: A New Approach to the Application of Theorem Proving to Problem Solving

raw_candidates.name: Shakey the Robot
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Shakey was the first integrated sense-plan-act robot, the archetype ReAct's loop unknowingly recapitulates; no technical channel connects them.
raw_candidates.definition: SRI robot (1966-72) integrating perception, STRIPS planning, and action execution - the first general-purpose mobile robot agent.
raw_candidates.source_title: Shakey the Robot

raw_candidates.name: A* search
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A* made heuristic search the default planning subroutine of classical agents; ReAct performs no graph search.
raw_candidates.definition: Graph search algorithm (Hart, Nilsson & Raphael, 1968) guaranteeing optimal paths with an admissible heuristic.
raw_candidates.source_title: A* search algorithm

raw_candidates.name: General Problem Solver
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPS introduced means-ends analysis, the ur-form of reason-then-act; a 65-year conceptual ancestor with no consumed channel into ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Program (Newell & Simon, 1957) solving problems by means-ends analysis over difference tables - an early model of human problem solving.
raw_candidates.source_title: General Problem Solver

raw_candidates.name: SOAR cognitive architecture
raw_candidates.causal_claim: SOAR unified reasoning and acting in a production-rule agent for decades of agent research; ReAct's authors did not build on it.
raw_candidates.definition: Cognitive architecture (Laird, Newell & Rosenbloom, 1987) implementing agents as production rules over problem spaces, with chunking as learning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Soar (cognitive architecture)

raw_candidates.name: BDI architecture
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BDI gave agent systems their belief-desire-intention vocabulary; an influential parallel tradition with no channel into LLM prompting.
raw_candidates.definition: Agent architecture (Bratman 1987; Rao & Georgeff 1991) structuring agents by beliefs, desires, and committed intentions (plans).
raw_candidates.source_title: Belief-desire-intention model

raw_candidates.name: Subsumption architecture
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Brooks' subsumption argued for reactive layered control over deliberative planning - the act-side pole of the tension ReAct synthesizes, at 36 years' remove.
raw_candidates.definition: Robot control architecture (Brooks, 1986) of layered reactive behaviors without central world models ('intelligence without representation').
raw_candidates.source_title: Subsumption architecture

raw_candidates.name: ACT-R
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ACT-R modeled human cognition as productions over declarative memory; a cognitive-science parallel with no channel into ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Cognitive architecture (Anderson, 1990s) unifying procedural productions and declarative chunks, widely used to model human task performance.
raw_candidates.source_title: ACT-R

raw_candidates.name: SHRDLU
raw_candidates.causal_claim: SHRDLU coupled language understanding to action in a blocks world, an early language-and-action system; conceptual ancestry only.
raw_candidates.definition: Program (Winograd, 1970) understanding and executing natural-language commands about a simulated blocks world.
raw_candidates.source_title: SHRDLU

raw_candidates.name: PDDL
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PDDL standardized planning-domain description for the classical planning community; ReAct uses free-text actions, not PDDL.
raw_candidates.definition: Planning Domain Definition Language (McDermott et al., 1998), the standard input format for automated planning competitions.
raw_candidates.source_title: PDDL

raw_candidates.name: Graphplan
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Graphplan made classical planning dramatically faster via planning graphs; part of the planning canon ReAct bypasses.
raw_candidates.definition: Planner (Blum & Furst, 1995) building a compact planning graph to extract plans far faster than prior search-based planners.
raw_candidates.source_title: Graphplan

raw_candidates.name: Blackboard architecture
raw_candidates.causal_claim: HEARSAY-II's blackboard coordinated opportunistic knowledge sources - an early multi-component reasoning system; no channel into ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Erman et al., 1975-80) in which independent knowledge sources cooperate through a shared blackboard workspace.
raw_candidates.source_title: Blackboard system

raw_candidates.name: ELIZA
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ELIZA showed pattern-matched text could sustain an illusion of understanding; the remotest conversational ancestor, with no technical channel to ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Program (Weizenbaum, 1966) simulating a Rogerian therapist by pattern matching and reassembly rules.
raw_candidates.source_title: ELIZA

raw_candidates.name: Behavior trees
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Behavior trees became the standard control structure for game NPCs and robotics tasks; ReAct's loop is prompt-driven, not tree-driven.
raw_candidates.definition: Control architecture (popularized in game AI, 2000s) organizing agent behavior as a ticked tree of condition and action nodes.
raw_candidates.source_title: Behavior tree (artificial intelligence, robotics and control)

raw_candidates.name: Procedural Reasoning System
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PRS implemented BDI-style reactive planning in deployed systems; part of the agent-architecture canon with no channel into ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Agent system (Georgeff & Lansky, 1987) executing hierarchical plans reactively in dynamic environments, a BDI implementation ancestor.
raw_candidates.source_title: Procedural reasoning system

raw_candidates.name: Deep Q-Network (DQN)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: DQN's agents were the act-only baselines tradition ReAct's ALFWorld comparisons (imitation/RL) descend from; ReAct replaced policy learning with prompting.
raw_candidates.definition: Agent (Mnih et al., 2013/2015) learning Atari control from pixels by deep Q-learning, founding deep reinforcement learning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning

raw_candidates.name: AlphaGo
raw_candidates.causal_claim: AlphaGo fused search with learned policies - the era's emblem of machine acting; ReAct's loop uses neither search nor learned value functions.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Silver et al., 2016) combining deep policy/value networks with Monte Carlo tree search to defeat the world Go champion.
raw_candidates.source_title: Mastering the game of Go with deep neural networks and tree search

raw_candidates.name: Monte Carlo tree search
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MCTS is the search half of AlphaGo-style acting; ReAct performs a single greedy trajectory with no tree search.
raw_candidates.definition: Search algorithm (Kocsis & Szepesvari, 2006; Coulom, 2006) balancing exploration/exploitation via UCB over simulated rollouts.
raw_candidates.source_title: Monte Carlo tree search

raw_candidates.name: Q-learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Q-learning founded model-free value learning, the RL substrate of the act-only baselines; ReAct learns no values.
raw_candidates.definition: Off-policy temporal-difference algorithm (Watkins, 1989) learning action values from experience without a model of the environment.
raw_candidates.source_title: Q-learning

raw_candidates.name: DAgger imitation learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: DAgger-style imitation was among the ALFWorld baselines ReAct beat by 34 points; the beaten incumbent, not an enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Imitation-learning algorithm (Ross, Gordon & Bagnell, 2011) reducing covariate shift by aggregating expert corrections on the learner's own trajectories.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning

raw_candidates.name: Behavior cloning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Behavior cloning is the simplest imitation baseline tradition in ReAct's comparison set; an incumbent approach, not an input.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Pomerleau, 1989, ALVINN) training a network to copy expert actions from demonstrations, the template for imitation learning.
raw_candidates.source_title: ALVINN: An Autonomous Land Vehicle in a Neural Network

raw_candidates.name: Options framework (hierarchical RL)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The options framework formalized temporally extended actions, the RL analog of plan steps; no channel into ReAct's prompting.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Sutton, Precup & Singh, 1999) for hierarchical RL via temporally extended actions (options) with initiation sets and termination conditions.
raw_candidates.source_title: Between MDPs and semi-MDPs: A framework for temporal abstraction in reinforcement learning

raw_candidates.name: Dyna architecture
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Dyna integrated learning, planning, and acting in one loop - a conceptual RL ancestor of interleaved reason-act cycles; no consumed channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Sutton, 1990) interleaving real experience, model learning, and simulated planning updates in a single agent loop.
raw_candidates.source_title: Dyna (reinforcement learning)

raw_candidates.name: Prompt tuning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Prompt tuning showed soft prompts could steer frozen models, part of the prompt-as-program evidence base; ReAct uses discrete few-shot exemplars, not learned vectors.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Lester et al., 2021) learning continuous prompt embeddings for a frozen LM, matching fine-tuning at scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning

raw_candidates.name: Prefix-tuning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Prefix-tuning steered generation via learned prefixes; a parameter-efficient sibling of prompt conditioning with no channel into ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Li & Liang, 2021) optimizing continuous prefix activations for generation tasks, keeping LM parameters frozen.
raw_candidates.source_title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation

raw_candidates.name: MetaICL
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MetaICL trained models explicitly to learn in context from exemplars, sharpening the ICL capability ReAct's format depends on - at one remove, through ICL itself.
raw_candidates.definition: Meta-training approach (Min et al., 2021) teaching LMs to use in-context examples, improving few-shot generalization to unseen tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: MetaICL: Learning to Learn In Context

raw_candidates.name: Natural Instructions
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Natural Instructions catalogued tasks in instruction form, feeding the FLAN-style tuning wave; ReAct's exemplars were hand-written, not drawn from it.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark (Mishra et al., 2021) of 61 tasks with expert-written definitions and examples, for cross-task instruction generalization.
raw_candidates.source_title: Cross-Task Generalization via Natural Language Instructions

raw_candidates.name: PromptSource
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PromptSource systematized prompt authoring for hundreds of datasets; infrastructure of the prompting era, not an input to ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Toolkit and corpus (Bach et al., 2021) of ~2,000 prompts for 170+ datasets, with an API and prompt-authoring interface.
raw_candidates.source_title: PromptSource: An Integrated System for Prompt Engineering

raw_candidates.name: Self-talk
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Self-talk showed an LM clarifying itself via generated question-answer subdialogues, an early elicited-reasoning precursor at one remove from ReAct's thoughts.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Shwartz et al., 2020) in which an LM asks itself clarifying questions and uses the answers for commonsense QA, prefiguring elicited reasoning traces.
raw_candidates.source_title: Unsupervised Commonsense Question Answering with Self-Talk

raw_candidates.name: UnifiedQA
raw_candidates.causal_claim: UnifiedQA showed one model could span QA formats via text unification; part of the text-interface consolidation ReAct inherited, with no direct channel.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Khashabi et al., 2020) training a single T5-based model across extractive, abstractive, multiple-choice and yes/no QA formats.
raw_candidates.source_title: UnifiedQA: Crossing Format Boundaries With a Single QA System

raw_candidates.name: LoRA
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LoRA made adaptation cheap via low-rank updates; ReAct adapts by prompting alone, so LoRA is an unused sibling technique.
raw_candidates.definition: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning method (Hu et al., 2021) injecting trainable low-rank matrices into frozen weights.
raw_candidates.source_title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

raw_candidates.name: Transformer architecture
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Every model ReAct prompted is a Transformer; the architecture reaches ReAct through the pretrained models built on it, not directly.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017) replacing recurrence with self-attention; the substrate of all modern LLMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Attention Is All You Need

raw_candidates.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Seq2seq established encoder-decoder sequence transduction, the paradigm the Transformer displaced; it reaches ReAct only through that lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Sutskever et al., 2014) mapping input sequences to output sequences with LSTM encoder-decoders, founding neural sequence transduction.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Bahdanau attention
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bahdanau attention introduced the alignment mechanism that became self-attention; it reaches ReAct through the Transformer, two steps removed.
raw_candidates.definition: Mechanism (Bahdanau et al., 2014) letting a decoder attend over encoder states, fixing the fixed-length bottleneck in neural machine translation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

raw_candidates.name: LSTM
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LSTMs were the pre-Transformer sequence substrate; ReAct's models contain none - the lineage runs entirely through the Transformer succession.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent architecture (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) with gated memory cells enabling long-range sequence learning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long short-term memory

raw_candidates.name: Backpropagation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Backpropagation trained every network in ReAct's lineage; it reaches ReAct through the pretrained models, never as a consumed component of the method.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986) computing gradients through layered networks by the chain rule, making deep training practical.
raw_candidates.source_title: Backpropagation

raw_candidates.name: Word2vec
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Word2vec began the learned-embedding era that pretraining scaled; its channel to ReAct runs through the whole pretraining lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Mikolov et al., 2013) learning word embeddings from co-occurrence prediction, founding distributional representation learning at scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

raw_candidates.name: Sentence-BERT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Sentence-BERT supplied the embedding matching used by sibling planners (zero-shot planners) to ground actions; ReAct itself does no embedding matching.
raw_candidates.definition: Modification of BERT (Reimers & Gurevych, 2019) producing sentence embeddings for fast similarity search and clustering.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks

raw_candidates.name: ColBERT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ColBERT made late-interaction retrieval efficient for QA pipelines of the era; ReAct's search actions call the Wikipedia API, not ColBERT.
raw_candidates.definition: Retrieval model (Khattab & Zaharia, 2020) using token-level late interaction over BERT embeddings for fast, accurate passage search.
raw_candidates.source_title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT

raw_candidates.name: Wolfram Alpha
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Wolfram Alpha pioneered computational answers as a callable knowledge service, the product ancestor of tool-augmented answering; no channel into ReAct's research prototype.
raw_candidates.definition: Computational knowledge engine (Wolfram, 2009) answering factual queries by computing over curated structured data.
raw_candidates.source_title: WolframAlpha

raw_candidates.name: Siri
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Siri productized the voice assistant loop (interpret, act, respond) a decade before ReAct; a product-lineage ancestor with no technical channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Voice assistant (Apple, 2011) interpreting natural-language requests and executing actions across phone services.
raw_candidates.source_title: Siri

raw_candidates.name: MediaWiki API
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The MediaWiki API is literally the action interface ReAct's Wikipedia environment wraps (search/lookup actions); commodity infrastructure, not a leap.
raw_candidates.definition: Web API for Wikipedia (2000s) exposing search and page retrieval programmatically - the substrate of ReAct's Wikipedia action space.
raw_candidates.source_title: MediaWiki API

raw_candidates.name: SPARQL and the Semantic Web
raw_candidates.causal_claim: SPARQL standardized querying structured knowledge on the web; ReAct queries unstructured text via search actions instead.
raw_candidates.definition: Query language (W3C, 2008) for RDF data, the Semantic Web's standard interface to structured knowledge.
raw_candidates.source_title: SPARQL

raw_candidates.name: OpenIE
raw_candidates.causal_claim: OpenIE extracted relational tuples from text at web scale, an ancestor of machine-readable web knowledge; no channel into ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Paradigm (Banko et al., 2007, TextRunner) extracting (arg1, relation, arg2) tuples from web text without hand-built extractors.
raw_candidates.source_title: Open information extraction

raw_candidates.name: Rasa open-source dialogue framework
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Rasa industrialized intent-and-action dialogue agents for developers; the commercial dialogue-agent tradition ReAct's research bypassed.
raw_candidates.definition: Open-source framework (2016) for building text/voice assistants with NLU and dialogue policies executing actions.
raw_candidates.source_title: Rasa (software)

raw_candidates.name: Reflexion
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Reflexion extended ReAct with verbal self-reflection memory - a successor, dated after the parent, listed to be dropped by the year bound.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Shinn et al., 2023) in which agents verbally reflect on failures and store the reflections as episodic memory for later trials.
raw_candidates.source_title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning

raw_candidates.name: Toolformer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Toolformer taught models to call APIs by self-supervision - a 2023 successor direction, after the parent.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Schick et al., 2023) trained to decide which APIs to call and how, from self-supervised annotations.
raw_candidates.source_title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

raw_candidates.name: Generative Agents
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Generative Agents built believable agent societies on an LLM loop in 2023 - after the parent; part of the lineage ReAct opened, not its ancestry.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Park et al., 2023) of LLM agents with memory stream, reflection, and planning, simulating a small town's social behavior.
raw_candidates.source_title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior

candidate.name: In-context learning
candidate.causal_claim: ReAct is delivered entirely as few-shot in-context exemplars: the thought-action-observation format exists only as prompt conditioning, the capability ICL established.
candidate.definition: The ability of a pretrained LM (demonstrated at scale by GPT-3, 2020) to perform a new task from examples and instructions in its prompt, with no parameter updates.
candidate.source_title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

candidate.name: Scratchpads
candidate.causal_claim: Scratchpads showed models compute better when allowed to emit intermediate steps into a buffer; ReAct's thought stream is a scratchpad interleaved with actions.

candidate.source_title: Selection-Inference: Exploiting Large Language Models for Interpretable Logical Reasoning

candidate.name: Decomposed prompting
candidate.causal_claim: Decomposed prompting split complex tasks into sub-tasks routed to specialized LLM calls, a modular sibling architecture to ReAct's loop.
candidate.definition: Approach (Khot et al., 2022) decomposing a complex task into sub-tasks, each handled by an LLM prompt or handler, composed by a controller.
candidate.source_title: Decomposed Prompting: A Modular Approach for Solving Complex Tasks

candidate.name: Automatic prompt engineering
candidate.causal_claim: APE automated the search for effective instructions, part of the 2022 prompting-methods wave surrounding ReAct.
candidate.definition: Method (Zhou et al., 2022) using an LLM to propose and select natural-language instructions automatically, matching human prompt engineering.
candidate.source_title: Large Language Models Are Human-Level Prompt Engineers

candidate.name: PaLM
candidate.causal_claim: PaLM-540B was ReAct's strongest base model; its scale supplied the emergent reasoning ReAct's exemplars elicited.
candidate.definition: 540B dense decoder LM (Chowdhery et al., 2022) trained with Pathways, showing strong emergent reasoning and few-shot performance.
candidate.source_title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways

candidate.name: LaMDA
candidate.causal_claim: LaMDA demonstrated dialog-tuned LLMs at scale in early 2022, part of the model wave ReAct drew on; not used in ReAct's experiments.
candidate.definition: Dialog-specialized LLM family (Thoppilan et al., 2022) fine-tuned for grounded, sensible conversation.
candidate.source_title: LaMDA: Language Models for Dialog Applications

candidate.name: Chinchilla
candidate.causal_claim: Chinchilla reset the compute-optimal scaling recipe in 2022; a scaling-law sibling result, not an input to ReAct's method.
candidate.definition: 70B LM (Hoffmann et al., 2022) establishing compute-optimal parameter/token balance, outperforming much larger models.
candidate.source_title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models

candidate.name: SayCan
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: SayCan grounded LLM plans in robot affordances months before ReAct; the leading sibling approach to LLM acting, compared against ReAct's setting.
candidate.definition: System (Ahn et al., 2022) pairing an LLM's task knowledge ('Say') with learned affordance values ('Can') to ground plans for a mobile manipulator.
candidate.source_title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances

candidate.name: Inner Monologue
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Inner Monologue fed environment feedback back into an LLM planner in text form, the closest contemporaneous sibling to ReAct's observation loop.
candidate.definition: Framework (Huang et al., 2022) giving an LLM planner textual environment feedback (success detection, scene description) for closed-loop robotic planning.
candidate.source_title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models

candidate.name: MRKL systems
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: MRKL routed LLM calls to external tools and knowledge sources months before ReAct; the verifier already flagged it as ReAct's near-simultaneous multiple.
candidate.definition: Neuro-symbolic architecture (Karpas et al., 2022) in which an LLM router dispatches to expert modules: calculators, APIs, knowledge bases.
candidate.source_title: MRKL Systems: A modular, neuro-symbolic architecture that combines large language models, external knowledge sources and discrete reasoning

candidate.name: Language models as zero-shot planners
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Huang et al. showed LLMs could decompose embodied tasks into executable steps zero-shot, defining the act-only baseline ReAct's reasoning was measured against.
candidate.definition: Method (Huang et al., 2022) translating LLM-generated high-level plans into admissible embodied actions via sentence-embedding matching.
candidate.source_title: Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners: Extracting Actionable Knowledge for Embodied Agents

candidate.name: ProgPrompt
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: ProgPrompt generated program-like robot plans with assertion-based recovery, a code-as-policy sibling of ReAct's loop.
candidate.definition: Method (Singh et al., 2022) prompting LLMs to emit Pythonic robot action programs with assertions enabling environment feedback and recovery.
candidate.source_title: ProgPrompt: Generating Situated Robot Task Plans using Large Language Models

candidate.name: Gato
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Gato showed a single transformer acting across embodiments and modalities in 2022; a generalist-agent sibling, not an input to ReAct.
candidate.definition: Multi-modal, multi-task agent (Reed et al., 2022): one 1.2B transformer playing Atari, captioning images, and controlling a robot arm.
candidate.source_title: A Generalist Agent

candidate.name: WebShop
candidate.causal_claim: WebShop was ReAct's second headline testbed (+10); a coeval benchmark, built independently of the method.
candidate.definition: Simulated e-commerce environment (Yao et al., 2022) with 1.18M products and 12k instructions for evaluating web-shopping agents.
candidate.source_title: WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents

candidate.name: ScienceWorld
candidate.causal_claim: ScienceWorld evaluated text agents on science experiments in 2022; a coeval sibling benchmark to ReAct's testbeds.
candidate.definition: Benchmark (Wang et al., 2022) of 30 science-experiment tasks in a text-simulated environment for interactive agents.
candidate.source_title: ScienceWorld: Is your Agent Smarter than a 5th Grader?

candidate.name: Reflexion
candidate.causal_claim: Reflexion extended ReAct with verbal self-reflection memory - a successor, dated after the parent, listed to be dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: Framework (Shinn et al., 2023) in which agents verbally reflect on failures and store the reflections as episodic memory for later trials.
candidate.source_title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning

candidate.name: Toolformer
candidate.causal_claim: Toolformer taught models to call APIs by self-supervision - a 2023 successor direction, after the parent.
candidate.definition: Model (Schick et al., 2023) trained to decide which APIs to call and how, from self-supervised annotations.
candidate.source_title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

candidate.name: Generative Agents
candidate.causal_claim: Generative Agents built believable agent societies on an LLM loop in 2023 - after the parent; part of the lineage ReAct opened, not its ancestry.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Park et al., 2023) of LLM agents with memory stream, reflection, and planning, simulating a small town's social behavior.
candidate.source_title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior

raw_candidates.name: Generative pretraining (GPT-1)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-1 is GPT-2's literal predecessor in the same lab: the Transformer-decoder generative-pretraining recipe GPT-2 scaled 10x and pushed from fine-tuning to zero-shot conditioning.
raw_candidates.definition: OpenAI model (Radford et al., 2018): a 117M Transformer decoder pretrained on BooksCorpus, then fine-tuned per task, beating purpose-built models on 9 of 12 language-understanding tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

raw_candidates.name: Transformer architecture
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-2 is a stack of Transformer decoder blocks; the architecture reaches it as part of the GPT-1 recipe it inherited and scaled.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017) replacing recurrence with self-attention; the substrate of all modern LLMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Attention Is All You Need

raw_candidates.name: ULMFiT
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ULMFiT proved pretrain-then-fine-tune for NLP months before GPT-1, defining the transfer paradigm GPT-2's zero-shot move reacted against and extended.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Howard & Ruder, 2018): LM pretraining, LM fine-tuning, classifier fine-tuning with discriminative rates and gradual unfreezing, large gains on text classification.
raw_candidates.source_title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification

raw_candidates.name: ELMo
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ELMo showed contextualized representations from a pretrained LM transfer broadly; part of the 2018 pretraining wave GPT-2's lineage runs through GPT-1, not ELMo's biLSTM design.
raw_candidates.definition: Representation model (Peters et al., 2018): deep contextualized word vectors from a bidirectional LSTM LM, improving six NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep contextualized word representations

raw_candidates.name: BERT
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BERT is the encoder sibling of the 2018 pretraining wave - the alternative branch (masked, fine-tuned) to GPT-2's decoder, zero-shot branch; not consumed by GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Bidirectionally pretrained encoder (Devlin et al., 2018) whose fine-tuned representations reset NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

raw_candidates.name: Neural probabilistic language model
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bengio's NPLM founded neural language modeling - distributed word representations learned jointly with the LM; the deep ancestor of the pretraining lineage, reaching GPT-2 through GPT-1 and the Transformer succession.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Bengio et al., 2003) learning distributed word embeddings jointly with a neural LM, beating n-gram models on perplexity.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

raw_candidates.name: Word2vec
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Word2vec industrialized learned embeddings, the representation premise pretraining scaled; it reaches GPT-2 through the whole pretraining tradition.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Mikolov et al., 2013) learning word embeddings from co-occurrence prediction at scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

raw_candidates.name: RNN language modeling (Mikolov)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Mikolov's RNNLM showed neural LMs decisively beating n-gram baselines, restarting LM research as a neural discipline; an ancestor at several removes.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent neural LM (Mikolov et al., 2010) reducing perplexity and WER substantially over backoff n-gram models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Recurrent neural network based language model

raw_candidates.name: Byte-pair encoding for NMT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BPE subword segmentation is GPT-2's tokenization family (byte-level BPE); the segmentation scheme was inherited as part of the GPT-1 recipe and tooling.
raw_candidates.definition: Segmentation method (Sennrich et al., 2016) applying byte-pair encoding to learn subword units, fixing rare-word handling in neural MT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

raw_candidates.name: Layer normalization
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LayerNorm stabilizes the Transformer blocks GPT-2 stacks (moved to pre-norm in GPT-2); it arrives inside the inherited GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
raw_candidates.definition: Normalization method (Ba, Kiros & Hinton, 2016) normalizing layer activations per example, stabilizing recurrent and deep training.
raw_candidates.source_title: Layer Normalization

raw_candidates.name: Adam optimizer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Adam is the optimizer family the GPT line trained with; a commodity component of the inherited training recipe, not a GPT-2-specific enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Optimizer (Kingma & Ba, 2014) with adaptive per-parameter rates from first/second moment estimates; became deep learning's default.
raw_candidates.source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

raw_candidates.name: GELU activation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GELU is the activation the GPT line adopted from GPT-1 onward; it reaches GPT-2 inside the inherited architecture.
raw_candidates.definition: Activation (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016) weighting inputs by their Gaussian CDF, adopted across Transformer models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)

raw_candidates.name: BooksCorpus
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BooksCorpus was GPT-1's pretraining corpus - the data half of the recipe GPT-2 replaced with WebText; its channel runs through GPT-1.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Zhu et al., 2015) of 11,038 unpublished books (~74M sentences) used to train the original GPT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Aligning Books and Movies: Towards Story-like Visual Explanations by Watching Movies and Reading Books

raw_candidates.name: Common Crawl
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Common Crawl is the web-scale corpus infrastructure of the era; GPT-2's WebText was deliberately NOT Common Crawl (Reddit-linked pages instead), so the channel is weak.
raw_candidates.definition: Nonprofit web archive (founded 2007-08) providing petabytes of crawled web pages used to train many LMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Common Crawl

raw_candidates.name: Deep learning scaling predictability (Hestness)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Hestness et al. showed learning curves follow predictable power laws with scale - the empirical backdrop for GPT-2's log-linear scaling bet, though GPT-2's paper derives its claim from its own runs.
raw_candidates.definition: Study (Hestness et al., 2017) demonstrating predictable power-law scaling of model performance with data and model size across applications.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically

raw_candidates.name: AlexNet
raw_candidates.causal_claim: AlexNet opened the deep-learning era whose scaling logic GPT-2 extends to language; it reaches GPT-2 through the entire deep-learning succession, not directly.
raw_candidates.definition: CNN (Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, 2012) winning ImageNet by a wide margin with GPU training, founding the deep-learning era.
raw_candidates.source_title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: CUDA GPU computing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CUDA made the GPU training of every model in this lineage practical; it reaches GPT-2 as inherited infrastructure, two successions removed.
raw_candidates.definition: Platform (NVIDIA, 2007) exposing GPU parallelism to general computation, the substrate of deep-learning training economics.
raw_candidates.source_title: CUDA

raw_candidates.name: Backpropagation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Backpropagation trained every network in the lineage; it reaches GPT-2 through the models and recipes that embody it.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986) computing gradients through layered networks by the chain rule.
raw_candidates.source_title: Backpropagation

raw_candidates.name: LSTM
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LSTMs were the pre-Transformer LM substrate (ELMo, ULMFiT); GPT-2's lineage displaced them via the Transformer, which is the channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent architecture (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) with gated memory cells for long-range sequence learning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long short-term memory

raw_candidates.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Seq2seq founded neural sequence transduction; it reaches GPT-2 through the Transformer that displaced it.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Sutskever et al., 2014) mapping sequences to sequences with LSTM encoder-decoders.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Bahdanau attention
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bahdanau attention is the Transformer's own predecessor; it reaches GPT-2 inside self-attention, via the Transformer.
raw_candidates.definition: Mechanism (Bahdanau et al., 2014) letting a decoder attend over encoder states in neural MT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

raw_candidates.name: MAML meta-learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MAML learns initializations for fast few-shot adaptation by gradient steps - the meta-learning paradigm GPT-2's conditioning-based few-shot bypassed entirely; no channel, as with ICL's expansion.
raw_candidates.definition: Meta-learning algorithm (Finn, Abbeel & Levine, 2017) learning parameter initializations adaptable to new tasks in a few gradient steps.
raw_candidates.source_title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks

raw_candidates.name: Matching Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Matching Networks did one-shot classification by attention over support examples - a conditioning-flavored few-shot method, but embedding-based and never consumed by the GPT line.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Vinyals et al., 2016) for one-shot learning via attention over a support set in embedding space.
raw_candidates.source_title: Matching Networks for One Shot Learning

raw_candidates.name: Prototypical Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Prototypical Networks learn metric spaces for few-shot classification; part of the meta-learning paradigm with no channel into GPT-2's demonstration.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Snell, Swersky & Zemel, 2017) classifying by distance to class prototypes in a learned embedding space.
raw_candidates.source_title: Prototypical Networks for Few-shot Learning

raw_candidates.name: Zero-shot learning via attributes
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Attribute-based zero-shot classification in vision showed category transfer without examples a decade earlier - a conceptual sibling in another modality, with no channel into GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Lampert, Nickisch & Harmeling, 2009) classifying unseen animal classes via human-specified attribute vectors.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to detect unseen object classes by between-class attribute transfer

raw_candidates.name: Kneser-Ney smoothing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Kneser-Ney was the statistical-LM state of the art the neural lineage displaced; ancestry of the task, not of the method.
raw_candidates.definition: Smoothing technique (Kneser & Ney, 1995) for n-gram LMs, the best-performing backoff scheme of the statistical era.
raw_candidates.source_title: Kneser-Ney smoothing

raw_candidates.name: Perplexity as LM metric
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Perplexity (Jelinek-era) is the yardstick GPT-2's log-linear scaling claim is stated in; a measurement convention, not an enabler of the capability.
raw_candidates.definition: Metric from speech-recognition LM evaluation (Jelinek, 1970s): exponentiated cross-entropy of a test set under the model.
raw_candidates.source_title: Perplexity

raw_candidates.name: One Billion Word Benchmark
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The 1B Word Benchmark standardized neural LM comparison in the pre-Transformer years; part of the evaluation lineage, not an input to GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark (Chelba et al., 2013) for statistical language modeling at billion-word scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: One Billion Word Benchmark for Measuring Progress in Statistical Language Modeling

raw_candidates.name: Penn Treebank LM benchmark
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PTB was the small-data LM testbed of the neural-LM era (Mikolov's RNNLM results); evaluation ancestry only.
raw_candidates.definition: Corpus (Marcus et al., 1993) whose LM split became the standard small benchmark for neural language models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Penn Treebank

raw_candidates.name: TensorFlow
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-1/GPT-2 were implemented in TensorFlow; commodity tooling any equivalent framework replaces, not a milestone in the method's causal chain.
raw_candidates.definition: Google's open-source deep-learning framework (2015) for dataflow graph computation.
raw_candidates.source_title: TensorFlow

raw_candidates.name: PyTorch
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PyTorch was the era's other framework; the GPT line's public code was TensorFlow-based, so even the tooling channel points elsewhere.
raw_candidates.definition: Facebook's open-source deep-learning framework (2016) with dynamic computation graphs.
raw_candidates.source_title: PyTorch

raw_candidates.name: Distributed training (parameter servers)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Large-scale distributed training patterns underpin all big-model runs of the era; GPT-2's 1.5B training was modest by later standards and consumed no specific distributed-training milestone.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture pattern (Li et al., 2014) scaling ML training across clusters via parameter servers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Scaling Distributed Machine Learning with the Parameter Server

raw_candidates.name: Curriculum learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Curriculum learning orders training examples easy-to-hard; GPT-2's training used no curriculum - a named idea in the training-methods space with no channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Strategy (Bengio et al., 2009) presenting training examples in a meaningful order to improve generalization and speed.
raw_candidates.source_title: Curriculum Learning

raw_candidates.name: Generating sequences with RNNs (Graves)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Graves 2013 showed RNNs generating convincing text and handwriting sample-by-sample - the generative-LM demonstration tradition GPT-2 scales; ancestry through the neural-LM lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Work (Graves, 2013) using LSTMs with mixture-density outputs to generate handwriting and text sequences.
raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: CoVe contextual vectors
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CoVe transferred MT-encoder representations to downstream tasks, an early transfer-representation result in the run-up to ELMo/GPT-1; its channel runs through that 2018 wave.
raw_candidates.definition: Representations (McCann et al., 2017) from a machine-translation encoder, improving classification and QA when concatenated with GloVe.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learned in Translation: Contextualized Word Vectors

raw_candidates.name: GloVe
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GloVe was the other embedding standard of the word2vec era; the embedding premise reaches GPT-2 through the pretraining tradition, and GPT-2 learns its embeddings end-to-end regardless.
raw_candidates.definition: Embedding method (Pennington, Socher & Manning, 2014) factorizing global co-occurrence statistics.
raw_candidates.source_title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

raw_candidates.name: Fast weights (Schmidhuber)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Schmidhuber's fast-weight programmers proposed one network programming another via weight changes - a conceptual ancestor of conditioning, cited by later meta-learning, with no channel into GPT-2's work.
raw_candidates.definition: Proposal (Schmidhuber, 1992) in which a slow network generates fast weights for another network, an early form of learned adaptation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to Control Fast-Weight Memories: An Alternative to Dynamic Recurrent Networks

raw_candidates.name: Learning to learn (Thrun & Pratt)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The learning-to-learn literature framed transfer as meta-knowledge decades before; framing ancestry for few-shot claims, not a consumed component.
raw_candidates.definition: Research programme (Thrun & Pratt, eds., 1998) on learning inductive bias from task families.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to Learn

raw_candidates.name: Neural Turing Machines
raw_candidates.causal_claim: NTMs coupled networks to external memory; an alternative augmentation direction that the GPT lineage did not take.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2014) giving a neural controller differentiable read/write access to an external memory bank.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Turing Machines

raw_candidates.name: Memory Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Memory Networks answered questions over an explicit memory store; a sibling QA architecture with no channel into GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Weston, Chopra & Bordes, 2014) combining learned representations with a long-term memory component for QA.
raw_candidates.source_title: Memory Networks

raw_candidates.name: End-to-End Memory Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MemN2N made memory attention end-to-end differentiable; part of the attention-era QA landscape, not GPT-2's lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Sukhbaatar et al., 2015) reading memory with multiple attention hops, trained end-to-end.
raw_candidates.source_title: End-To-End Memory Networks

raw_candidates.name: Differentiable Neural Computer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The DNC was DeepMind's flagship memory-augmented architecture; a parallel direction with no channel into the GPT line.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2016) coupling a neural controller to an external memory matrix with differentiable addressing.
raw_candidates.source_title: Hybrid computing using a neural network with dynamic external memory

raw_candidates.name: Transformer-XL
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Transformer-XL extended context via recurrence in Jan 2019 - coeval with GPT-2 (same year), listed to be dropped by the year bound.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Dai et al., 2019) adding segment-level recurrence and relative positions to the Transformer for longer contexts.
raw_candidates.source_title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context

raw_candidates.name: XLNet
raw_candidates.causal_claim: XLNet's permutation LM was 2019's alternative pretraining objective - coeval with GPT-2, dropped by the year bound.
raw_candidates.definition: Pretraining method (Yang et al., 2019) maximizing likelihood over permutation orders, combining autoregressive and autoencoding advantages.
raw_candidates.source_title: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding

raw_candidates.name: RoBERTa
raw_candidates.causal_claim: RoBERTa showed BERT was undertrained - a coeval 2019 replication study, dropped by the year bound.
raw_candidates.definition: Study (Liu et al., 2019) optimizing BERT's training recipe for substantially better results.
raw_candidates.source_title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach

raw_candidates.name: ERNIE
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Baidu's ERNIE added knowledge masking to pretraining in 2019 - coeval, dropped by the year bound.
raw_candidates.definition: Pretraining model (Sun et al., 2019) masking entities and phrases to inject knowledge into representations.
raw_candidates.source_title: ERNIE: Enhanced Representation through Knowledge Integration

raw_candidates.name: GPT-2 staged release and 'too dangerous to release' debate
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The staged-release controversy is part of GPT-2's own 2019 story, not a predecessor - coeval, dropped by the year bound.
raw_candidates.definition: OpenAI's staged release of GPT-2 (Feb-Nov 2019) over misuse concerns, a landmark in release-policy debates.
raw_candidates.source_title: GPT-2

raw_candidates.name: Residual networks (ResNet)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Residual connections are inside every Transformer block GPT-2 stacks; they arrive as part of the Transformer/GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (He et al., 2015) with skip connections enabling training of 100+ layer networks, winning ImageNet 2015.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

raw_candidates.name: Dropout
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Dropout is a standard regularizer inside the inherited training recipe; commodity component, not a GPT-2 enabler in the milestone sense.
raw_candidates.definition: Regularization technique (Srivastava et al., 2014) randomly dropping units during training to prevent co-adaptation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting

raw_candidates.name: Batch normalization
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BatchNorm normalized activations across batches; the Transformer line standardized on LayerNorm instead, so even the component channel points to its sibling.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Ioffe & Szegedy, 2015) normalizing layer inputs per mini-batch, accelerating deep training.
raw_candidates.source_title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift

raw_candidates.name: Weight initialization (Xavier/He)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Principled initialization is inside every training run of the era; background technique, not a milestone GPT-2 distinctively consumed (GPT-2's scaled residual init is its own tweak).
raw_candidates.definition: Initialization schemes (Glorot & Bengio, 2010; He et al., 2015) keeping activation/gradient scales stable across layers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks

raw_candidates.name: Stochastic gradient descent with momentum
raw_candidates.causal_claim: SGD is the optimization substrate of all of it; it reaches GPT-2 through every intervening training run and belongs many levels deeper in the trace.
raw_candidates.definition: Optimization method (stochastic approximation, Robbins-Monro 1951; momentum, Polyak 1964) training models by noisy gradient steps.
raw_candidates.source_title: Stochastic gradient descent

raw_candidates.name: Automatic differentiation (autodiff)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Autodiff (Linnainmaa 1970; framework-era reverse mode) is how gradients are computed in practice; deep infrastructure ancestry, mediated by every framework and model above it.
raw_candidates.definition: Technique (Linnainmaa, 1970) computing derivatives of composite functions by the chain rule in reverse accumulation order.
raw_candidates.source_title: Automatic differentiation

raw_candidates.name: Theano
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Theano pioneered symbolic autodiff frameworks for research; GPT-2's stack was TensorFlow, so even the tooling lineage is a sibling.
raw_candidates.definition: Python library (Bergstra et al., 2007-2010) for symbolic tensor computation and GPU code generation, from MILA.

raw_candidates.name: cuDNN

raw_candidates.name: WikiText

raw_candidates.causal_claim: RACE was part of the reading-comprehension evaluation landscape GPT-2's zero-shot claims were situated in; not an input.

raw_candidates.name: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling

raw_candidates.causal_claim: WaveNet showed autoregressive generation at unprecedented fidelity in audio - the generative-modeling era's emblem, in another modality; no channel into GPT-2's text result.

raw_candidates.name: QRNN
raw_candidates.causal_claim: QRNNs were the efficiency-focused RNN alternative of the PTB era; part of the displaced RNN-LM landscape, no channel into GPT-2.

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Cache/dynamic-evaluation tricks squeezed RNN LMs by exploiting recency at test time; test-time adaptation ideas the GPT-2 demonstration did not use.

candidate.name: Penn Treebank LM benchmark

candidate.name: PyTorch

raw_candidates.name: Byte-pair encoding for NMT

raw_candidates.name: Adam optimizer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Adam is the optimizer family the GPT line trained with; a commodity component of the inherited training recipe, not a GPT-2-specific enabler.
