raw_candidates.name: Fast weights (Schmidhuber)

raw_candidates.name: Learning to learn (Thrun & Pratt)

raw_candidates.name: Neural Turing Machines

raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Turing Machines

raw_candidates.name: Memory Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Memory Networks answered questions over an explicit memory store; a sibling QA architecture with no channel into GPT-2.

raw_candidates.source_title: Memory Networks

raw_candidates.name: End-to-End Memory Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MemN2N made memory attention end-to-end differentiable; part of the attention-era QA landscape, not GPT-2's lineage.

raw_candidates.source_title: End-To-End Memory Networks

raw_candidates.name: Differentiable Neural Computer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The DNC was DeepMind's flagship memory-augmented architecture; a parallel direction with no channel into the GPT line.

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Transformer-XL extended context via recurrence in Jan 2019 - coeval with GPT-2 (same year), listed to be dropped by the year bound.

raw_candidates.name: RoBERTa

raw_candidates.name: ERNIE

raw_candidates.name: Dropout

raw_candidates.name: Batch normalization
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BatchNorm normalized activations across batches; the Transformer line standardized on LayerNorm instead, so even the component channel points to its sibling.

raw_candidates.name: Weight initialization (Xavier/He)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Principled initialization is inside every training run of the era; background technique, not a milestone GPT-2 distinctively consumed (GPT-2's scaled residual init is its own tweak).

raw_candidates.source_title: Automatic differentiation

raw_candidates.source_title: Theano (software)

raw_candidates.name: cuDNN

raw_candidates.source_title: cuDNN

raw_candidates.definition: Model/framework (Raffel et al., 2019, Google): unified text-to-text format with encoder-decoder Transformer pretrained on C4.
raw_candidates.source_title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

raw_candidates.name: SuperGLUE benchmark
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-3 was evaluated on SuperGLUE few-shot; an evaluation target, not an enabler of the leap.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark suite (Wang et al., 2019) of hard language-understanding tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: SuperGLUE: A Stickier Benchmark for General-Purpose Language Understanding Systems

raw_candidates.name: Natural Questions dataset
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A GPT-3 few-shot evaluation set, not an enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019, Google): real search queries with Wikipedia answers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research

raw_candidates.name: Winogrande dataset
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A GPT-3 evaluation set, not an enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Sakaguchi et al., 2019): large-scale Winograd-style commonsense benchmark.
raw_candidates.source_title: Winogrande: An Adversarial Winograd Schema Challenge at Scale

raw_candidates.name: WebText corpus
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-3 trained on WebText2, an expanded version of GPT-2's WebText - the channel runs through GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (OpenAI, 2019): web pages from outbound Reddit links, built for GPT-2.
raw_candidates.source_title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

raw_candidates.name: Microsoft-OpenAI Azure supercomputing partnership
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-3's training run executed on the Microsoft-built cluster - an institutional/compute precondition rather than a technical milestone in the lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Partnership (announced Jul 2019): Microsoft invested $1B in OpenAI to build Azure AI supercomputing for large-model training.
raw_candidates.source_title: Microsoft invests in OpenAI (2019 announcement)

raw_candidates.name: DeepSpeed ZeRO optimizer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with GPT-3 (2020); not part of GPT-3's training stack on the record.
raw_candidates.definition: Library (Rajbhandari et al., 2020, Microsoft): memory-optimization for distributed training.
raw_candidates.source_title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models

raw_candidates.name: ELECTRA
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with GPT-3 (2020) and a parallel paradigm.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Clark et al., 2020, Google): replaced-token-detection pretraining.
raw_candidates.source_title: ELECTRA: Pre-training Text Encoders as Discriminators Rather Than Generators

raw_candidates.name: Reformer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with GPT-3 (2020); not consumed by it.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Kitaev et al., 2020): LSH attention and reversible layers for efficient Transformers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Reformer: The Efficient Transformer

raw_candidates.name: Deep RL from human preferences (Christiano et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Christiano-style preference learning directly enabled the agent's leap as the first demonstration that human comparisons could train a reward model guiding behavior — the seed of RLHF.
raw_candidates.source_title: Why is ChatGPT so good? (Scale AI)
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Christiano et al., 2017) learning a reward model from human preferences over trajectory segments and optimizing it with RL.

raw_candidates.name: PPO (proximal policy optimization)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PPO directly enabled the agent's leap as the optimization algorithm that ran the RLHF stage aligning the agent's engine.
raw_candidates.source_title: The Day We Stopped Predicting the Next Word: How ChatGPT Was Actually Built
raw_candidates.definition: Policy-gradient RL algorithm (Schulman et al., 2017) with clipped surrogate objective; the standard optimizer for RLHF.

raw_candidates.name: Large-scale pretraining (GPT-3)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-3-scale pretraining directly enabled the agent's leap by producing a single model with enough world knowledge and few-shot adaptability to serve as a general task engine.
raw_candidates.source_title: AI Paper Review: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
raw_candidates.definition: Training very large autoregressive language models on web-scale text; GPT-3 (175B) showed few-shot in-context task performance without fine-tuning.

raw_candidates.name: Fine-tuning language models from human preferences (Ziegler et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The first application of preference-based reward learning to language models - the direct methodological bridge between Christiano et al. 2017 and Stiennon et al. 2020 / InstructGPT.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Ziegler et al., 2019, OpenAI): train a reward model from human comparisons and fine-tune a pretrained LM (GPT-2) with PPO under a KL penalty.
raw_candidates.source_title: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences - ADS

raw_candidates.name: Learning to summarize from human feedback (Stiennon et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The immediate predecessor of InstructGPT: same recipe, same lab, six shared authors; proved RLHF beats supervised baselines and human reference summaries.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Stiennon et al., 2020, OpenAI): full RLHF recipe - human comparisons, Bradley-Terry reward model, PPO with reference-KL penalty - applied to summarization at 1.3B-6.7B scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to summarize from human feedback

raw_candidates.name: TRPO (trust region policy optimization)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PPO's direct predecessor; the RLHF lineage consumed the simplified PPO, not TRPO itself.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Schulman et al., 2015): policy updates constrained to a trust region via KL bound, with monotonic-improvement guarantees.
raw_candidates.source_title: Trust Region Policy Optimization

raw_candidates.name: Bradley-Terry model of paired comparisons
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The preference-model form inside every RLHF reward model - but it reached RLHF packaged inside Christiano et al.'s reward-learning method.
raw_candidates.definition: Statistical model (Bradley & Terry, 1952): probability that one item beats another is a logistic function of latent scores.
raw_candidates.source_title: Rank Analysis of Incomplete Block Designs

raw_candidates.name: Inverse reinforcement learning (Ng & Russell)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The intellectual ancestor of reward learning; RLHF's channel runs through preference-based reward learning (Christiano), not demonstration-based IRL.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Ng & Russell, 2000): recover a reward function from an expert's observed behavior.
raw_candidates.source_title: Algorithms for Inverse Reinforcement Learning

raw_candidates.name: Apprenticeship learning via inverse RL (Abbeel & Ng)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A demonstration-based precursor; not the channel into preference-based RLHF.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Abbeel & Ng, 2004): match an expert's feature expectations to learn near-expert policies without a reward function.
raw_candidates.source_title: Apprenticeship Learning via Inverse Reinforcement Learning

raw_candidates.name: TAMER framework (Knox & Stone)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: An early human-feedback RL channel, but evaluative rather than preference-comparison based; the InstructGPT lineage runs through Christiano/Ziegler/Stiennon.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Knox & Stone, 2009): agents learn from human evaluative feedback (+/-) treated as reward.
raw_candidates.source_title: Interactively Shaping Agents via Human Reinforcement

raw_candidates.name: Preference-based reinforcement learning (Wirth et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The formal backdrop Christiano et al. operationalized at deep-RL scale in the same year; the consumed artifact in the lineage is Christiano's method.
raw_candidates.definition: Survey/formalization (Wirth et al., 2017) of RL from trajectory preferences rather than numeric rewards.
raw_candidates.source_title: Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning: A Formal Framework and a Survey

raw_candidates.name: WebGPT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A sibling application of human-feedback fine-tuning, not an enabler of the RLHF recipe itself.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Nakano et al., 2021, OpenAI): GPT-3 fine-tuned with human feedback to answer questions using a text browser.
raw_candidates.source_title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback

raw_candidates.name: InstructGPT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with the RLHF node itself (same year, same work) - cannot be its predecessor at year granularity.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Ouyang et al., 2022, OpenAI): SFT + RLHF on GPT-3 - the very system this graph's RLHF node is drawn from.
raw_candidates.source_title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

raw_candidates.name: Constitutional AI
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with RLHF (2022) and a parallel branch, not a predecessor.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Bai et al., 2022, Anthropic): RL from AI feedback (RLAIF) using a written constitution.
raw_candidates.source_title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

raw_candidates.name: Sparrow dialogue agent
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with RLHF (2022); a parallel application.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Glaese et al., 2022, DeepMind): dialogue agent trained with human judgements and rule-based rewards.
raw_candidates.source_title: Improving alignment of dialogue agents via targeted human judgements

raw_candidates.name: Direct preference optimization (DPO)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Postdates the RLHF node (2022) - a successor/simplification, not a predecessor.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Rafailov et al., 2023): optimize policies directly on preference data, bypassing an explicit reward model.
raw_candidates.source_title: Direct Preference Optimization

raw_candidates.name: TL;DR summarization dataset
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The task substrate for Stiennon et al.'s demonstration - its channel into RLHF runs through that paper.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Reddit TL;DR posts with author-written summaries), used by Ziegler and Stiennon for RLHF summarization experiments.
raw_candidates.source_title: TL;DR dataset (Reddit summarization corpus)

candidate.name: Generative pretraining (GPT-1)
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-1 is GPT-2's literal predecessor in the same lab: the Transformer-decoder generative-pretraining recipe GPT-2 scaled 10x and pushed from fine-tuning to zero-shot conditioning.
candidate.definition: OpenAI model (Radford et al., 2018): a 117M Transformer decoder pretrained on BooksCorpus, then fine-tuned per task, beating purpose-built models on 9 of 12 language-understanding tasks.
candidate.source_title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

candidate.name: Transformer architecture
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-2 is a stack of Transformer decoder blocks; the architecture reaches it as part of the GPT-1 recipe it inherited and scaled.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017) replacing recurrence with self-attention; the substrate of all modern LLMs.
candidate.source_title: Attention Is All You Need

candidate.name: ULMFiT
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: ULMFiT proved pretrain-then-fine-tune for NLP months before GPT-1, defining the transfer paradigm GPT-2's zero-shot move reacted against and extended.
candidate.definition: Method (Howard & Ruder, 2018): LM pretraining, LM fine-tuning, classifier fine-tuning with discriminative rates and gradual unfreezing, large gains on text classification.
candidate.source_title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification

candidate.name: ELMo
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: ELMo showed contextualized representations from a pretrained LM transfer broadly; part of the 2018 pretraining wave GPT-2's lineage runs through GPT-1, not ELMo's biLSTM design.
candidate.definition: Representation model (Peters et al., 2018): deep contextualized word vectors from a bidirectional LSTM LM, improving six NLP benchmarks.
candidate.source_title: Deep contextualized word representations

candidate.name: BERT
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: BERT is the encoder sibling of the 2018 pretraining wave - the alternative branch (masked, fine-tuned) to GPT-2's decoder, zero-shot branch; not consumed by GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Bidirectionally pretrained encoder (Devlin et al., 2018) whose fine-tuned representations reset NLP benchmarks.
candidate.source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

candidate.name: Neural probabilistic language model
candidate.causal_claim: Bengio's NPLM founded neural language modeling - distributed word representations learned jointly with the LM; the deep ancestor of the pretraining lineage, reaching GPT-2 through GPT-1 and the Transformer succession.
candidate.definition: Model (Bengio et al., 2003) learning distributed word embeddings jointly with a neural LM, beating n-gram models on perplexity.
candidate.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

candidate.name: Word2vec
candidate.causal_claim: Word2vec industrialized learned embeddings, the representation premise pretraining scaled; it reaches GPT-2 through the whole pretraining tradition.
candidate.definition: Method (Mikolov et al., 2013) learning word embeddings from co-occurrence prediction at scale.
candidate.source_title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

candidate.name: RNN language modeling (Mikolov)
candidate.causal_claim: Mikolov's RNNLM showed neural LMs decisively beating n-gram baselines, restarting LM research as a neural discipline; an ancestor at several removes.
candidate.definition: Recurrent neural LM (Mikolov et al., 2010) reducing perplexity and WER substantially over backoff n-gram models.
candidate.source_title: Recurrent neural network based language model

candidate.name: Byte-pair encoding for NMT
candidate.causal_claim: BPE subword segmentation is GPT-2's tokenization family (byte-level BPE); the segmentation scheme was inherited as part of the GPT-1 recipe and tooling.
candidate.definition: Segmentation method (Sennrich et al., 2016) applying byte-pair encoding to learn subword units, fixing rare-word handling in neural MT.
candidate.source_title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

candidate.name: Layer normalization
candidate.causal_claim: LayerNorm stabilizes the Transformer blocks GPT-2 stacks (moved to pre-norm in GPT-2); it arrives inside the inherited GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
candidate.definition: Normalization method (Ba, Kiros & Hinton, 2016) normalizing layer activations per example, stabilizing recurrent and deep training.
candidate.source_title: Layer Normalization

candidate.name: Adam optimizer
candidate.causal_claim: Adam is the optimizer family the GPT line trained with; a commodity component of the inherited training recipe, not a GPT-2-specific enabler.
candidate.definition: Optimizer (Kingma & Ba, 2014) with adaptive per-parameter rates from first/second moment estimates; became deep learning's default.
candidate.source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

candidate.name: GELU activation
candidate.causal_claim: GELU is the activation the GPT line adopted from GPT-1 onward; it reaches GPT-2 inside the inherited architecture.
candidate.definition: Activation (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016) weighting inputs by their Gaussian CDF, adopted across Transformer models.
candidate.source_title: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)

candidate.name: BooksCorpus
candidate.causal_claim: BooksCorpus was GPT-1's pretraining corpus - the data half of the recipe GPT-2 replaced with WebText; its channel runs through GPT-1.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Zhu et al., 2015) of 11,038 unpublished books (~74M sentences) used to train the original GPT.
candidate.source_title: Aligning Books and Movies: Towards Story-like Visual Explanations by Watching Movies and Reading Books

candidate.name: Common Crawl
candidate.causal_claim: Common Crawl is the web-scale corpus infrastructure of the era; GPT-2's WebText was deliberately NOT Common Crawl (Reddit-linked pages instead), so the channel is weak.
candidate.definition: Nonprofit web archive (founded 2007-08) providing petabytes of crawled web pages used to train many LMs.
candidate.source_title: Common Crawl

candidate.name: Deep learning scaling predictability (Hestness)
candidate.causal_claim: Hestness et al. showed learning curves follow predictable power laws with scale - the empirical backdrop for GPT-2's log-linear scaling bet, though GPT-2's paper derives its claim from its own runs.
candidate.definition: Study (Hestness et al., 2017) demonstrating predictable power-law scaling of model performance with data and model size across applications.
candidate.source_title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically

candidate.name: AlexNet
candidate.causal_claim: AlexNet opened the deep-learning era whose scaling logic GPT-2 extends to language; it reaches GPT-2 through the entire deep-learning succession, not directly.
candidate.definition: CNN (Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, 2012) winning ImageNet by a wide margin with GPU training, founding the deep-learning era.
candidate.source_title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

candidate.name: CUDA GPU computing
candidate.causal_claim: CUDA made the GPU training of every model in this lineage practical; it reaches GPT-2 as inherited infrastructure, two successions removed.
candidate.definition: Platform (NVIDIA, 2007) exposing GPU parallelism to general computation, the substrate of deep-learning training economics.
candidate.source_title: CUDA

candidate.name: Backpropagation
candidate.causal_claim: Backpropagation trained every network in the lineage; it reaches GPT-2 through the models and recipes that embody it.
candidate.definition: Algorithm (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986) computing gradients through layered networks by the chain rule.
candidate.source_title: Backpropagation

candidate.name: LSTM
candidate.causal_claim: LSTMs were the pre-Transformer LM substrate (ELMo, ULMFiT); GPT-2's lineage displaced them via the Transformer, which is the channel.
candidate.definition: Recurrent architecture (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) with gated memory cells for long-range sequence learning.
candidate.source_title: Long short-term memory

candidate.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
candidate.causal_claim: Seq2seq founded neural sequence transduction; it reaches GPT-2 through the Transformer that displaced it.
candidate.definition: Framework (Sutskever et al., 2014) mapping sequences to sequences with LSTM encoder-decoders.
candidate.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

candidate.name: Bahdanau attention
candidate.causal_claim: Bahdanau attention is the Transformer's own predecessor; it reaches GPT-2 inside self-attention, via the Transformer.
candidate.definition: Mechanism (Bahdanau et al., 2014) letting a decoder attend over encoder states in neural MT.
candidate.source_title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

candidate.name: MAML meta-learning
candidate.causal_claim: MAML learns initializations for fast few-shot adaptation by gradient steps - the meta-learning paradigm GPT-2's conditioning-based few-shot bypassed entirely; no channel, as with ICL's expansion.
candidate.definition: Meta-learning algorithm (Finn, Abbeel & Levine, 2017) learning parameter initializations adaptable to new tasks in a few gradient steps.
candidate.source_title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks

candidate.name: Matching Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Matching Networks did one-shot classification by attention over support examples - a conditioning-flavored few-shot method, but embedding-based and never consumed by the GPT line.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Vinyals et al., 2016) for one-shot learning via attention over a support set in embedding space.
candidate.source_title: Matching Networks for One Shot Learning

candidate.name: Prototypical Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Prototypical Networks learn metric spaces for few-shot classification; part of the meta-learning paradigm with no channel into GPT-2's demonstration.
candidate.definition: Method (Snell, Swersky & Zemel, 2017) classifying by distance to class prototypes in a learned embedding space.
candidate.source_title: Prototypical Networks for Few-shot Learning

candidate.name: Zero-shot learning via attributes
candidate.causal_claim: Attribute-based zero-shot classification in vision showed category transfer without examples a decade earlier - a conceptual sibling in another modality, with no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Method (Lampert, Nickisch & Harmeling, 2009) classifying unseen animal classes via human-specified attribute vectors.
candidate.source_title: Learning to detect unseen object classes by between-class attribute transfer

candidate.name: Kneser-Ney smoothing
candidate.causal_claim: Kneser-Ney was the statistical-LM state of the art the neural lineage displaced; ancestry of the task, not of the method.
candidate.definition: Smoothing technique (Kneser & Ney, 1995) for n-gram LMs, the best-performing backoff scheme of the statistical era.
candidate.source_title: Kneser-Ney smoothing

candidate.name: Perplexity as LM metric
candidate.causal_claim: Perplexity (Jelinek-era) is the yardstick GPT-2's log-linear scaling claim is stated in; a measurement convention, not an enabler of the capability.
candidate.definition: Metric from speech-recognition LM evaluation (Jelinek, 1970s): exponentiated cross-entropy of a test set under the model.
candidate.source_title: Perplexity

candidate.name: One Billion Word Benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: The 1B Word Benchmark standardized neural LM comparison in the pre-Transformer years; part of the evaluation lineage, not an input to GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Benchmark (Chelba et al., 2013) for statistical language modeling at billion-word scale.
candidate.source_title: One Billion Word Benchmark for Measuring Progress in Statistical Language Modeling

candidate.name: Penn Treebank LM benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: PTB was the small-data LM testbed of the neural-LM era (Mikolov's RNNLM results); evaluation ancestry only.
candidate.definition: Corpus (Marcus et al., 1993) whose LM split became the standard small benchmark for neural language models.
candidate.source_title: Penn Treebank

candidate.name: TensorFlow
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-1/GPT-2 were implemented in TensorFlow; commodity tooling any equivalent framework replaces, not a milestone in the method's causal chain.
candidate.definition: Google's open-source deep-learning framework (2015) for dataflow graph computation.
candidate.source_title: TensorFlow

candidate.name: PyTorch
candidate.causal_claim: PyTorch was the era's other framework; the GPT line's public code was TensorFlow-based, so even the tooling channel points elsewhere.
candidate.definition: Facebook's open-source deep-learning framework (2016) with dynamic computation graphs.
candidate.source_title: PyTorch

candidate.name: Distributed training (parameter servers)
candidate.causal_claim: Large-scale distributed training patterns underpin all big-model runs of the era; GPT-2's 1.5B training was modest by later standards and consumed no specific distributed-training milestone.
candidate.definition: Architecture pattern (Li et al., 2014) scaling ML training across clusters via parameter servers.
candidate.source_title: Scaling Distributed Machine Learning with the Parameter Server

candidate.name: Curriculum learning
candidate.causal_claim: Curriculum learning orders training examples easy-to-hard; GPT-2's training used no curriculum - a named idea in the training-methods space with no channel.
candidate.definition: Strategy (Bengio et al., 2009) presenting training examples in a meaningful order to improve generalization and speed.
candidate.source_title: Curriculum Learning

candidate.name: Generating sequences with RNNs (Graves)
candidate.causal_claim: Graves 2013 showed RNNs generating convincing text and handwriting sample-by-sample - the generative-LM demonstration tradition GPT-2 scales; ancestry through the neural-LM lineage.
candidate.definition: Work (Graves, 2013) using LSTMs with mixture-density outputs to generate handwriting and text sequences.
candidate.source_title: Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks

candidate.name: CoVe contextual vectors
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: CoVe transferred MT-encoder representations to downstream tasks, an early transfer-representation result in the run-up to ELMo/GPT-1; its channel runs through that 2018 wave.
candidate.definition: Representations (McCann et al., 2017) from a machine-translation encoder, improving classification and QA when concatenated with GloVe.
candidate.source_title: Learned in Translation: Contextualized Word Vectors

candidate.name: GloVe
candidate.causal_claim: GloVe was the other embedding standard of the word2vec era; the embedding premise reaches GPT-2 through the pretraining tradition, and GPT-2 learns its embeddings end-to-end regardless.
candidate.definition: Embedding method (Pennington, Socher & Manning, 2014) factorizing global co-occurrence statistics.
candidate.source_title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

candidate.name: Fast weights (Schmidhuber)
candidate.causal_claim: Schmidhuber's fast-weight programmers proposed one network programming another via weight changes - a conceptual ancestor of conditioning, cited by later meta-learning, with no channel into GPT-2's work.
candidate.definition: Proposal (Schmidhuber, 1992) in which a slow network generates fast weights for another network, an early form of learned adaptation.
candidate.source_title: Learning to Control Fast-Weight Memories: An Alternative to Dynamic Recurrent Networks

candidate.name: Learning to learn (Thrun & Pratt)
candidate.causal_claim: The learning-to-learn literature framed transfer as meta-knowledge decades before; framing ancestry for few-shot claims, not a consumed component.
candidate.definition: Research programme (Thrun & Pratt, eds., 1998) on learning inductive bias from task families.
candidate.source_title: Learning to Learn

candidate.name: Neural Turing Machines
candidate.causal_claim: NTMs coupled networks to external memory; an alternative augmentation direction that the GPT lineage did not take.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2014) giving a neural controller differentiable read/write access to an external memory bank.
candidate.source_title: Neural Turing Machines

candidate.name: Memory Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Memory Networks answered questions over an explicit memory store; a sibling QA architecture with no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Weston, Chopra & Bordes, 2014) combining learned representations with a long-term memory component for QA.
candidate.source_title: Memory Networks

candidate.causal_claim: MemN2N made memory attention end-to-end differentiable; part of the attention-era QA landscape, not GPT-2's lineage.
candidate.definition: Model (Sukhbaatar et al., 2015) reading memory with multiple attention hops, trained end-to-end.
candidate.source_title: End-To-End Memory Networks

candidate.causal_claim: The DNC was DeepMind's flagship memory-augmented architecture; a parallel direction with no channel into the GPT line.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2016) coupling a neural controller to an external memory matrix with differentiable addressing.
candidate.source_title: Hybrid computing using a neural network with dynamic external memory

candidate.name: Transformer-XL
candidate.causal_claim: Transformer-XL extended context via recurrence in Jan 2019 - coeval with GPT-2 (same year), listed to be dropped by the year bound.

candidate.source_title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context

candidate.name: XLNet
candidate.causal_claim: XLNet's permutation LM was 2019's alternative pretraining objective - coeval with GPT-2, dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: Pretraining method (Yang et al., 2019) maximizing likelihood over permutation orders, combining autoregressive and autoencoding advantages.
candidate.source_title: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding

candidate.name: RoBERTa
candidate.causal_claim: RoBERTa showed BERT was undertrained - a coeval 2019 replication study, dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: Study (Liu et al., 2019) optimizing BERT's training recipe for substantially better results.
candidate.source_title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach

candidate.name: ERNIE
candidate.causal_claim: Baidu's ERNIE added knowledge masking to pretraining in 2019 - coeval, dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: Pretraining model (Sun et al., 2019) masking entities and phrases to inject knowledge into representations.
candidate.source_title: ERNIE: Enhanced Representation through Knowledge Integration

candidate.name: GPT-2 staged release and 'too dangerous to release' debate
candidate.causal_claim: The staged-release controversy is part of GPT-2's own 2019 story, not a predecessor - coeval, dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: OpenAI's staged release of GPT-2 (Feb-Nov 2019) over misuse concerns, a landmark in release-policy debates.

candidate.name: Residual networks (ResNet)

candidate.definition: Architecture (He et al., 2015) with skip connections enabling training of 100+ layer networks, winning ImageNet 2015.
candidate.source_title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

candidate.name: Dropout
candidate.causal_claim: Dropout is a standard regularizer inside the inherited training recipe; commodity component, not a GPT-2 enabler in the milestone sense.
candidate.definition: Regularization technique (Srivastava et al., 2014) randomly dropping units during training to prevent co-adaptation.
candidate.source_title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting

candidate.name: Batch normalization
candidate.causal_claim: BatchNorm normalized activations across batches; the Transformer line standardized on LayerNorm instead, so even the component channel points to its sibling.
candidate.definition: Method (Ioffe & Szegedy, 2015) normalizing layer inputs per mini-batch, accelerating deep training.
candidate.source_title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift

candidate.name: Weight initialization (Xavier/He)
candidate.causal_claim: Principled initialization is inside every training run of the era; background technique, not a milestone GPT-2 distinctively consumed (GPT-2's scaled residual init is its own tweak).
candidate.definition: Initialization schemes (Glorot & Bengio, 2010; He et al., 2015) keeping activation/gradient scales stable across layers.
candidate.source_title: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks

candidate.name: Stochastic gradient descent with momentum
candidate.causal_claim: SGD is the optimization substrate of all of it; it reaches GPT-2 through every intervening training run and belongs many levels deeper in the trace.
candidate.definition: Optimization method (stochastic approximation, Robbins-Monro 1951; momentum, Polyak 1964) training models by noisy gradient steps.
candidate.source_title: Stochastic gradient descent

candidate.name: Automatic differentiation (autodiff)
candidate.causal_claim: Autodiff (Linnainmaa 1970; framework-era reverse mode) is how gradients are computed in practice; deep infrastructure ancestry, mediated by every framework and model above it.
candidate.definition: Technique (Linnainmaa, 1970) computing derivatives of composite functions by the chain rule in reverse accumulation order.
candidate.source_title: Automatic differentiation

candidate.name: Theano
candidate.causal_claim: Theano pioneered symbolic autodiff frameworks for research; GPT-2's stack was TensorFlow, so even the tooling lineage is a sibling.
candidate.definition: Python library (Bergstra et al., 2007-2010) for symbolic tensor computation and GPU code generation, from MILA.
candidate.source_title: Theano (software)

candidate.name: cuDNN
candidate.causal_claim: cuDNN's GPU kernels underlie all framework training of the era; commodity plumbing beneath the recipe, not a consumed milestone.
candidate.definition: NVIDIA library (2014) of GPU-accelerated primitives for deep neural networks.
candidate.source_title: cuDNN

candidate.name: Data parallelism and model parallelism practice
candidate.causal_claim: Multi-GPU training practice (from AlexNet's two-GPU split onward) is the era's background capability; GPT-2's 1.5B run consumed the practice generically, not a named milestone.
candidate.definition: Practice of splitting training across GPUs (Krizhevsky, 2012 onward), scaling to data/model parallelism in large runs.

candidate.causal_claim: Wikipedia text trained half the models of the era; GPT-2's WebText notably drew on Reddit-linked pages broadly - corpus plumbing, not a milestone in the method's chain.

candidate.name: Shannon's n-gram entropy studies
candidate.causal_claim: Shannon's prediction-and-entropy work founded language modeling as a measurable science; the remotest task ancestry, mediated by the entire statistical and neural LM succession.
candidate.definition: Studies (Shannon, 1951) estimating the entropy of English via human prediction experiments, founding statistical language modeling.
candidate.source_title: Prediction and Entropy of Printed English

candidate.name: Markov chains for text
candidate.causal_claim: Markov's letter-sequence analysis of Pushkin is the first statistical text model; ancestry of the task across a century of intermediaries.

candidate.name: Feedforward neural LM (Bengio follow-ups)
candidate.causal_claim: Duplicate-angle variant of the NPLM line (already scouted as the neural probabilistic LM); dedupe is expected to merge or drop it.

candidate.name: Hierarchical softmax and NCE
candidate.causal_claim: Output-layer approximations made large-vocabulary neural LMs trainable in the Mikolov era; GPT-2's full softmax at 50k vocab on modern hardware no longer needed them - a displaced enabling trick of the prior era.

candidate.name: Character-aware LM (Kim et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: Character-CNN word models addressed open vocabularies compositionally; the GPT line solved the same problem with BPE instead - a sibling solution, not a channel.
candidate.definition: Model (Kim et al., 2015) composing word representations from character CNNs for language modeling.
candidate.source_title: Character-Aware Neural Language Models

candidate.name: Pointer-sentinel and variational LM advances
candidate.causal_claim: Mid-2010s PTB-era LM refinements (pointer sentinel, variational dropout) mark the RNN-LM era's ceiling that the Transformer succession displaced; no channel into GPT-2.

candidate.name: Semi-supervised sequence learning
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Dai & Le's sequence-autoencoding pretraining anticipated LM pretraining for classification in 2015; an early paradigm ancestor whose channel runs through the 2018 wave.
candidate.definition: Method (Dai & Le, 2015) pretraining sequence models by LM/autoencoding before supervised fine-tuning, improving classification.

candidate.name: Contextual pre-training via language modeling (Peters 2017 NAACL)

candidate.name: WikiText
candidate.causal_claim: WikiText-103 was a standard LM benchmark in GPT-2's zero-shot perplexity tables; a yardstick, not an enabler.

candidate.source_title: Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models

candidate.name: CNN/Daily Mail summarization dataset
candidate.causal_claim: CNN/Daily Mail was the corpus for GPT-2's zero-shot summarization probe (TL;DR prompting); evaluation lineage only.

candidate.name: RACE reading comprehension
candidate.causal_claim: RACE was part of the reading-comprehension evaluation landscape GPT-2's zero-shot claims were situated in; not an input.

candidate.source_title: RACE: Large-scale ReAding Comprehension Dataset From Examinations

candidate.name: GLUE benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: GLUE defined the fine-tuning era's scoreboard that GPT-2's zero-shot stance implicitly argued against; the incumbent measurement regime, not an enabler.

candidate.source_title: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark and Analysis Platform for Natural Language Understanding

candidate.name: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling
candidate.causal_claim: Jozefowicz et al. pushed LSTM LMs to their limits and catalogued what scale bought before Transformers - the immediate pre-history of the scaling question GPT-2 answered differently.

candidate.name: ConvS2S

candidate.name: WaveNet

candidate.name: QRNN
candidate.causal_claim: QRNNs were the efficiency-focused RNN alternative of the PTB era; part of the displaced RNN-LM landscape, no channel into GPT-2.
