raw_candidates.name: Transformer architecture
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-2 is a stack of Transformer decoder blocks; the architecture reaches it as part of the GPT-1 recipe it inherited and scaled.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017) replacing recurrence with self-attention; the substrate of all modern LLMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Attention Is All You Need

raw_candidates.name: ULMFiT
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ULMFiT proved pretrain-then-fine-tune for NLP months before GPT-1, defining the transfer paradigm GPT-2's zero-shot move reacted against and extended.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Howard & Ruder, 2018): LM pretraining, LM fine-tuning, classifier fine-tuning with discriminative rates and gradual unfreezing, large gains on text classification.
raw_candidates.source_title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification

raw_candidates.name: ELMo
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ELMo showed contextualized representations from a pretrained LM transfer broadly; part of the 2018 pretraining wave GPT-2's lineage runs through GPT-1, not ELMo's biLSTM design.
raw_candidates.definition: Representation model (Peters et al., 2018): deep contextualized word vectors from a bidirectional LSTM LM, improving six NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep contextualized word representations

raw_candidates.name: BERT
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BERT is the encoder sibling of the 2018 pretraining wave - the alternative branch (masked, fine-tuned) to GPT-2's decoder, zero-shot branch; not consumed by GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Bidirectionally pretrained encoder (Devlin et al., 2018) whose fine-tuned representations reset NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

raw_candidates.name: Neural probabilistic language model
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bengio's NPLM founded neural language modeling - distributed word representations learned jointly with the LM; the deep ancestor of the pretraining lineage, reaching GPT-2 through GPT-1 and the Transformer succession.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Bengio et al., 2003) learning distributed word embeddings jointly with a neural LM, beating n-gram models on perplexity.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

raw_candidates.name: Word2vec
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Word2vec industrialized learned embeddings, the representation premise pretraining scaled; it reaches GPT-2 through the whole pretraining tradition.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Mikolov et al., 2013) learning word embeddings from co-occurrence prediction at scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

raw_candidates.name: RNN language modeling (Mikolov)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Mikolov's RNNLM showed neural LMs decisively beating n-gram baselines, restarting LM research as a neural discipline; an ancestor at several removes.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent neural LM (Mikolov et al., 2010) reducing perplexity and WER substantially over backoff n-gram models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Recurrent neural network based language model

raw_candidates.name: Byte-pair encoding for NMT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BPE subword segmentation is GPT-2's tokenization family (byte-level BPE); the segmentation scheme was inherited as part of the GPT-1 recipe and tooling.
raw_candidates.definition: Segmentation method (Sennrich et al., 2016) applying byte-pair encoding to learn subword units, fixing rare-word handling in neural MT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

raw_candidates.name: Layer normalization
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LayerNorm stabilizes the Transformer blocks GPT-2 stacks (moved to pre-norm in GPT-2); it arrives inside the inherited GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
raw_candidates.definition: Normalization method (Ba, Kiros & Hinton, 2016) normalizing layer activations per example, stabilizing recurrent and deep training.
raw_candidates.source_title: Layer Normalization

raw_candidates.name: Adam optimizer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Adam is the optimizer family the GPT line trained with; a commodity component of the inherited training recipe, not a GPT-2-specific enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Optimizer (Kingma & Ba, 2014) with adaptive per-parameter rates from first/second moment estimates; became deep learning's default.
raw_candidates.source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

raw_candidates.name: GELU activation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GELU is the activation the GPT line adopted from GPT-1 onward; it reaches GPT-2 inside the inherited architecture.
raw_candidates.definition: Activation (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016) weighting inputs by their Gaussian CDF, adopted across Transformer models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)

raw_candidates.name: BooksCorpus
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BooksCorpus was GPT-1's pretraining corpus - the data half of the recipe GPT-2 replaced with WebText; its channel runs through GPT-1.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Zhu et al., 2015) of 11,038 unpublished books (~74M sentences) used to train the original GPT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Aligning Books and Movies: Towards Story-like Visual Explanations by Watching Movies and Reading Books

raw_candidates.name: Common Crawl
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Common Crawl is the web-scale corpus infrastructure of the era; GPT-2's WebText was deliberately NOT Common Crawl (Reddit-linked pages instead), so the channel is weak.
raw_candidates.definition: Nonprofit web archive (founded 2007-08) providing petabytes of crawled web pages used to train many LMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Common Crawl

raw_candidates.name: Deep learning scaling predictability (Hestness)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Hestness et al. showed learning curves follow predictable power laws with scale - the empirical backdrop for GPT-2's log-linear scaling bet, though GPT-2's paper derives its claim from its own runs.
raw_candidates.definition: Study (Hestness et al., 2017) demonstrating predictable power-law scaling of model performance with data and model size across applications.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically

raw_candidates.name: AlexNet
raw_candidates.causal_claim: AlexNet opened the deep-learning era whose scaling logic GPT-2 extends to language; it reaches GPT-2 through the entire deep-learning succession, not directly.
raw_candidates.definition: CNN (Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, 2012) winning ImageNet by a wide margin with GPU training, founding the deep-learning era.
raw_candidates.source_title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: CUDA GPU computing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CUDA made the GPU training of every model in this lineage practical; it reaches GPT-2 as inherited infrastructure, two successions removed.
raw_candidates.definition: Platform (NVIDIA, 2007) exposing GPU parallelism to general computation, the substrate of deep-learning training economics.
raw_candidates.source_title: CUDA

raw_candidates.name: Backpropagation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Backpropagation trained every network in the lineage; it reaches GPT-2 through the models and recipes that embody it.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986) computing gradients through layered networks by the chain rule.
raw_candidates.source_title: Backpropagation

raw_candidates.name: LSTM
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LSTMs were the pre-Transformer LM substrate (ELMo, ULMFiT); GPT-2's lineage displaced them via the Transformer, which is the channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent architecture (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) with gated memory cells for long-range sequence learning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long short-term memory

raw_candidates.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Seq2seq founded neural sequence transduction; it reaches GPT-2 through the Transformer that displaced it.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Sutskever et al., 2014) mapping sequences to sequences with LSTM encoder-decoders.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Bahdanau attention
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bahdanau attention is the Transformer's own predecessor; it reaches GPT-2 inside self-attention, via the Transformer.
raw_candidates.definition: Mechanism (Bahdanau et al., 2014) letting a decoder attend over encoder states in neural MT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

raw_candidates.name: MAML meta-learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MAML learns initializations for fast few-shot adaptation by gradient steps - the meta-learning paradigm GPT-2's conditioning-based few-shot bypassed entirely; no channel, as with ICL's expansion.
raw_candidates.definition: Meta-learning algorithm (Finn, Abbeel & Levine, 2017) learning parameter initializations adaptable to new tasks in a few gradient steps.
raw_candidates.source_title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks

raw_candidates.name: Matching Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Matching Networks did one-shot classification by attention over support examples - a conditioning-flavored few-shot method, but embedding-based and never consumed by the GPT line.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Vinyals et al., 2016) for one-shot learning via attention over a support set in embedding space.
raw_candidates.source_title: Matching Networks for One Shot Learning

raw_candidates.name: Prototypical Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Prototypical Networks learn metric spaces for few-shot classification; part of the meta-learning paradigm with no channel into GPT-2's demonstration.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Snell, Swersky & Zemel, 2017) classifying by distance to class prototypes in a learned embedding space.
raw_candidates.source_title: Prototypical Networks for Few-shot Learning

raw_candidates.name: Zero-shot learning via attributes
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Attribute-based zero-shot classification in vision showed category transfer without examples a decade earlier - a conceptual sibling in another modality, with no channel into GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Lampert, Nickisch & Harmeling, 2009) classifying unseen animal classes via human-specified attribute vectors.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to detect unseen object classes by between-class attribute transfer

raw_candidates.name: Kneser-Ney smoothing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Kneser-Ney was the statistical-LM state of the art the neural lineage displaced; ancestry of the task, not of the method.
raw_candidates.definition: Smoothing technique (Kneser & Ney, 1995) for n-gram LMs, the best-performing backoff scheme of the statistical era.
raw_candidates.source_title: Kneser-Ney smoothing

raw_candidates.name: Perplexity as LM metric
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Perplexity (Jelinek-era) is the yardstick GPT-2's log-linear scaling claim is stated in; a measurement convention, not an enabler of the capability.
raw_candidates.definition: Metric from speech-recognition LM evaluation (Jelinek, 1970s): exponentiated cross-entropy of a test set under the model.
raw_candidates.source_title: Perplexity

raw_candidates.name: One Billion Word Benchmark
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The 1B Word Benchmark standardized neural LM comparison in the pre-Transformer years; part of the evaluation lineage, not an input to GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark (Chelba et al., 2013) for statistical language modeling at billion-word scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: One Billion Word Benchmark for Measuring Progress in Statistical Language Modeling

raw_candidates.name: Penn Treebank LM benchmark
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PTB was the small-data LM testbed of the neural-LM era (Mikolov's RNNLM results); evaluation ancestry only.
raw_candidates.definition: Corpus (Marcus et al., 1993) whose LM split became the standard small benchmark for neural language models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Penn Treebank

raw_candidates.name: TensorFlow
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-1/GPT-2 were implemented in TensorFlow; commodity tooling any equivalent framework replaces, not a milestone in the method's causal chain.
raw_candidates.definition: Google's open-source deep-learning framework (2015) for dataflow graph computation.
raw_candidates.source_title: TensorFlow

raw_candidates.name: PyTorch
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PyTorch was the era's other framework; the GPT line's public code was TensorFlow-based, so even the tooling channel points elsewhere.
raw_candidates.definition: Facebook's open-source deep-learning framework (2016) with dynamic computation graphs.
raw_candidates.source_title: PyTorch

raw_candidates.name: Distributed training (parameter servers)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Large-scale distributed training patterns underpin all big-model runs of the era; GPT-2's 1.5B training was modest by later standards and consumed no specific distributed-training milestone.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture pattern (Li et al., 2014) scaling ML training across clusters via parameter servers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Scaling Distributed Machine Learning with the Parameter Server

raw_candidates.name: Curriculum learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Curriculum learning orders training examples easy-to-hard; GPT-2's training used no curriculum - a named idea in the training-methods space with no channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Strategy (Bengio et al., 2009) presenting training examples in a meaningful order to improve generalization and speed.
raw_candidates.source_title: Curriculum Learning

raw_candidates.name: Generating sequences with RNNs (Graves)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Graves 2013 showed RNNs generating convincing text and handwriting sample-by-sample - the generative-LM demonstration tradition GPT-2 scales; ancestry through the neural-LM lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Work (Graves, 2013) using LSTMs with mixture-density outputs to generate handwriting and text sequences.
raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: CoVe contextual vectors
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CoVe transferred MT-encoder representations to downstream tasks, an early transfer-representation result in the run-up to ELMo/GPT-1; its channel runs through that 2018 wave.
raw_candidates.definition: Representations (McCann et al., 2017) from a machine-translation encoder, improving classification and QA when concatenated with GloVe.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learned in Translation: Contextualized Word Vectors

raw_candidates.name: GloVe
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GloVe was the other embedding standard of the word2vec era; the embedding premise reaches GPT-2 through the pretraining tradition, and GPT-2 learns its embeddings end-to-end regardless.
raw_candidates.definition: Embedding method (Pennington, Socher & Manning, 2014) factorizing global co-occurrence statistics.
raw_candidates.source_title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

raw_candidates.name: Fast weights (Schmidhuber)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Schmidhuber's fast-weight programmers proposed one network programming another via weight changes - a conceptual ancestor of conditioning, cited by later meta-learning, with no channel into GPT-2's work.
raw_candidates.definition: Proposal (Schmidhuber, 1992) in which a slow network generates fast weights for another network, an early form of learned adaptation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to Control Fast-Weight Memories: An Alternative to Dynamic Recurrent Networks

raw_candidates.name: Learning to learn (Thrun & Pratt)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The learning-to-learn literature framed transfer as meta-knowledge decades before; framing ancestry for few-shot claims, not a consumed component.
raw_candidates.definition: Research programme (Thrun & Pratt, eds., 1998) on learning inductive bias from task families.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to Learn

raw_candidates.name: Neural Turing Machines
raw_candidates.causal_claim: NTMs coupled networks to external memory; an alternative augmentation direction that the GPT lineage did not take.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2014) giving a neural controller differentiable read/write access to an external memory bank.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Turing Machines

raw_candidates.name: Memory Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Memory Networks answered questions over an explicit memory store; a sibling QA architecture with no channel into GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Weston, Chopra & Bordes, 2014) combining learned representations with a long-term memory component for QA.
raw_candidates.source_title: Memory Networks

raw_candidates.name: End-to-End Memory Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MemN2N made memory attention end-to-end differentiable; part of the attention-era QA landscape, not GPT-2's lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Sukhbaatar et al., 2015) reading memory with multiple attention hops, trained end-to-end.
raw_candidates.source_title: End-To-End Memory Networks

raw_candidates.name: Differentiable Neural Computer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The DNC was DeepMind's flagship memory-augmented architecture; a parallel direction with no channel into the GPT line.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2016) coupling a neural controller to an external memory matrix with differentiable addressing.
raw_candidates.source_title: Hybrid computing using a neural network with dynamic external memory

raw_candidates.name: Residual networks (ResNet)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Residual connections are inside every Transformer block GPT-2 stacks; they arrive as part of the Transformer/GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (He et al., 2015) with skip connections enabling training of 100+ layer networks, winning ImageNet 2015.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

raw_candidates.name: Dropout
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Dropout is a standard regularizer inside the inherited training recipe; commodity component, not a GPT-2 enabler in the milestone sense.
raw_candidates.definition: Regularization technique (Srivastava et al., 2014) randomly dropping units during training to prevent co-adaptation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting

raw_candidates.name: Batch normalization
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BatchNorm normalized activations across batches; the Transformer line standardized on LayerNorm instead, so even the component channel points to its sibling.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Ioffe & Szegedy, 2015) normalizing layer inputs per mini-batch, accelerating deep training.
raw_candidates.source_title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift

raw_candidates.name: Weight initialization (Xavier/He)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Principled initialization is inside every training run of the era; background technique, not a milestone GPT-2 distinctively consumed (GPT-2's scaled residual init is its own tweak).
raw_candidates.definition: Initialization schemes (Glorot & Bengio, 2010; He et al., 2015) keeping activation/gradient scales stable across layers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks

raw_candidates.name: Stochastic gradient descent with momentum
raw_candidates.causal_claim: SGD is the optimization substrate of all of it; it reaches GPT-2 through every intervening training run and belongs many levels deeper in the trace.
raw_candidates.definition: Optimization method (stochastic approximation, Robbins-Monro 1951; momentum, Polyak 1964) training models by noisy gradient steps.
raw_candidates.source_title: Stochastic gradient descent

raw_candidates.name: Automatic differentiation (autodiff)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Autodiff (Linnainmaa 1970; framework-era reverse mode) is how gradients are computed in practice; deep infrastructure ancestry, mediated by every framework and model above it.
raw_candidates.definition: Technique (Linnainmaa, 1970) computing derivatives of composite functions by the chain rule in reverse accumulation order.
raw_candidates.source_title: Automatic differentiation

raw_candidates.name: Theano
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Theano pioneered symbolic autodiff frameworks for research; GPT-2's stack was TensorFlow, so even the tooling lineage is a sibling.
raw_candidates.definition: Python library (Bergstra et al., 2007-2010) for symbolic tensor computation and GPU code generation, from MILA.
raw_candidates.source_title: Theano (software)

raw_candidates.name: cuDNN
raw_candidates.causal_claim: cuDNN's GPU kernels underlie all framework training of the era; commodity plumbing beneath the recipe, not a consumed milestone.
raw_candidates.definition: NVIDIA library (2014) of GPU-accelerated primitives for deep neural networks.
raw_candidates.source_title: cuDNN

raw_candidates.name: Data parallelism and model parallelism practice
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Multi-GPU training practice (from AlexNet's two-GPU split onward) is the era's background capability; GPT-2's 1.5B run consumed the practice generically, not a named milestone.
raw_candidates.definition: Practice of splitting training across GPUs (Krizhevsky, 2012 onward), scaling to data/model parallelism in large runs.
raw_candidates.source_title: One weird trick for parallelizing convolutional neural networks

raw_candidates.name: Reddit as a curated data source
raw_candidates.causal_claim: WebText's curation trick was scraping pages linked from Reddit with karma>=3 - a data choice inside GPT-2's own contribution, using a commodity platform; the platform is not a milestone predecessor.
raw_candidates.definition: Social news platform (founded 2005) whose outbound links and karma scores OpenAI used as a quality filter for WebText.
raw_candidates.source_title: Reddit

raw_candidates.name: Wikipedia as training corpus
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Wikipedia text trained half the models of the era; GPT-2's WebText notably drew on Reddit-linked pages broadly - corpus plumbing, not a milestone in the method's chain.
raw_candidates.definition: Free encyclopedia (founded 2001) whose text became a standard LM training and evaluation corpus.
raw_candidates.source_title: Wikipedia

raw_candidates.name: Shannon's n-gram entropy studies
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Shannon's prediction-and-entropy work founded language modeling as a measurable science; the remotest task ancestry, mediated by the entire statistical and neural LM succession.
raw_candidates.definition: Studies (Shannon, 1951) estimating the entropy of English via human prediction experiments, founding statistical language modeling.
raw_candidates.source_title: Prediction and Entropy of Printed English

raw_candidates.name: Markov chains for text
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Markov's letter-sequence analysis of Pushkin is the first statistical text model; ancestry of the task across a century of intermediaries.
raw_candidates.definition: Analysis (Markov, 1913) of vowel/consonant sequences in Eugene Onegin, the first application of Markov chains to text.
raw_candidates.source_title: Markov chain

raw_candidates.name: Feedforward neural LM (Bengio follow-ups)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Duplicate-angle variant of the NPLM line (already scouted as the neural probabilistic LM); dedupe is expected to merge or drop it.
raw_candidates.definition: The 2003 JMLR neural LM and its immediate follow-up literature establishing feedforward neural language modeling.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

raw_candidates.name: Hierarchical softmax and NCE
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Output-layer approximations made large-vocabulary neural LMs trainable in the Mikolov era; GPT-2's full softmax at 50k vocab on modern hardware no longer needed them - a displaced enabling trick of the prior era.
raw_candidates.definition: Techniques (Morin & Bengio, 2005; Mnih & Teh, 2012; Gutmann & Hyvarinen, 2010) approximating the softmax partition function for large vocabularies.
raw_candidates.source_title: Noise-contrastive estimation

raw_candidates.name: Character-aware LM (Kim et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Character-CNN word models addressed open vocabularies compositionally; the GPT line solved the same problem with BPE instead - a sibling solution, not a channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Kim et al., 2015) composing word representations from character CNNs for language modeling.
raw_candidates.source_title: Character-Aware Neural Language Models

raw_candidates.name: Pointer-sentinel and variational LM advances
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Mid-2010s PTB-era LM refinements (pointer sentinel, variational dropout) mark the RNN-LM era's ceiling that the Transformer succession displaced; no channel into GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Models (Merity et al., 2016; Gal & Ghahramani, 2016) pushing RNN LM perplexity via pointer mechanisms and variational dropout.
raw_candidates.source_title: Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models

raw_candidates.name: AWD-LSTM
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: AWD-LSTM was the strongest RNN LM recipe ULMFiT built on; it reaches GPT-2 through the ULMFiT/GPT-1 paradigm succession, as a SUBTYPE-relative of the LSTM line.
raw_candidates.definition: Regularized LSTM LM (Merity, Keskar & Socher, 2017) whose recipe powered ULMFiT's transfer results.
raw_candidates.source_title: Regularizing and Optimizing LSTM Language Models

raw_candidates.name: Semi-supervised sequence learning
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Dai & Le's sequence-autoencoding pretraining anticipated LM pretraining for classification in 2015; an early paradigm ancestor whose channel runs through the 2018 wave.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Dai & Le, 2015) pretraining sequence models by LM/autoencoding before supervised fine-tuning, improving classification.
raw_candidates.source_title: Semi-supervised Sequence Learning

raw_candidates.name: Contextual pre-training via language modeling (Peters 2017 NAACL)
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The tagLM work preceding ELMo showed LM states helping sequence labelers; ancestry inside the ELMo branch of the 2018 wave.
raw_candidates.definition: Work (Peters et al., 2017) augmenting sequence labelers with pretrained LM representations (tagLM), the direct run-up to ELMo.
raw_candidates.source_title: Semi-supervised sequence tagging with bidirectional language models

raw_candidates.name: LAMBADA
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LAMBADA was a headline zero-shot test in GPT-2's paper (accuracy jumping with scale); a testbed the result was measured on, not a component of the method.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Paperno et al., 2016) of narrative passages whose final word requires broad discourse context, designed to defeat local-context models.
raw_candidates.source_title: The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context

raw_candidates.name: CoQA
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CoQA supplied GPT-2's flagship zero-shot number (55 F1 without task training); the stage for the demonstration, not an input to it.
raw_candidates.definition: Conversational QA dataset (Reddy, Chen & Manning, 2018) of 127k questions over dialogues about passages, with rationale spans.
raw_candidates.source_title: CoQA: A Conversational Question Answering Challenge

raw_candidates.name: Children's Book Test
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CBT was among GPT-2's zero-shot evaluation suites; evaluation ancestry only.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Hill et al., 2015/2016) of children's-book sentences with a missing word to predict from context, for evaluating reading models.
raw_candidates.source_title: The Goldilocks Principle: Reading Children's Books with Explicit Memory Representations

raw_candidates.name: WikiText
raw_candidates.causal_claim: WikiText-103 was a standard LM benchmark in GPT-2's zero-shot perplexity tables; a yardstick, not an enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark (Merity et al., 2016) of 103M tokens from verified Wikipedia articles for long-term LM evaluation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models

raw_candidates.name: CNN/Daily Mail summarization dataset
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CNN/Daily Mail was the corpus for GPT-2's zero-shot summarization probe (TL;DR prompting); evaluation lineage only.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Hermann et al., 2015) of news articles with bullet summaries, repurposed as the standard abstractive summarization benchmark.
raw_candidates.source_title: Teaching Machines to Read and Comprehend

raw_candidates.name: RACE reading comprehension
raw_candidates.causal_claim: RACE was part of the reading-comprehension evaluation landscape GPT-2's zero-shot claims were situated in; not an input.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Lai et al., 2017) of 100k English-exam questions for middle/high school students, for reading comprehension.
raw_candidates.source_title: RACE: Large-scale ReAding Comprehension Dataset From Examinations

raw_candidates.name: GLUE benchmark
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GLUE defined the fine-tuning era's scoreboard that GPT-2's zero-shot stance implicitly argued against; the incumbent measurement regime, not an enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark (Wang et al., 2018) of nine sentence-level understanding tasks that standardized transfer evaluation for BERT-era models.
raw_candidates.source_title: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark and Analysis Platform for Natural Language Understanding

raw_candidates.name: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Jozefowicz et al. pushed LSTM LMs to their limits and catalogued what scale bought before Transformers - the immediate pre-history of the scaling question GPT-2 answered differently.
raw_candidates.definition: Study (Jozefowicz et al., 2016) training very large LSTM LMs on the 1B Word Benchmark, analyzing architectures and output layers at scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling

raw_candidates.name: ConvS2S
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Convolutional seq2seq was Facebook's parallel bet to the Transformer in 2017 - the sibling architecture line that lost; no channel into GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Gehring et al., 2017) using gated convolutions with attention for sequence-to-sequence tasks, matching RNN quality faster.
raw_candidates.source_title: Convolutional Sequence to Sequence Learning

raw_candidates.name: WaveNet
raw_candidates.causal_claim: WaveNet showed autoregressive generation at unprecedented fidelity in audio - the generative-modeling era's emblem, in another modality; no channel into GPT-2's text result.
raw_candidates.definition: Generative model (van den Oord et al., 2016) of raw audio by dilated causal convolutions, transforming text-to-speech quality.
raw_candidates.source_title: WaveNet: A Generative Model for Raw Audio

raw_candidates.name: Sparsely-Gated MoE
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Shazeer's MoE scaled capacity via conditional computation - the road GPT-2 did not take (dense scaling); a sibling scaling philosophy with no channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Shazeer et al., 2017) inserting sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layers to reach 137B parameters with conditional compute.
raw_candidates.source_title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer

raw_candidates.name: Relative position encodings
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Shaw et al.'s relative positions improved Transformer self-attention; GPT-2 used learned absolute positions from the GPT-1 design, so the component channel does not reach it.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Shaw, Uszkoreit & Vaswani, 2018) representing relative positions in self-attention, improving translation quality.
raw_candidates.source_title: Self-Attention with Relative Position Representations

raw_candidates.name: Mixed-precision training
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Mixed precision became standard large-training practice in this era; a generic technique GPT-2's run may have used but which no milestone claim attaches to.
raw_candidates.definition: Technique (Micikevicius et al., 2017) training in FP16 with FP32 master weights, halving memory and speeding large runs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Mixed Precision Training

raw_candidates.name: AdamW and decoupled weight decay
raw_candidates.causal_claim: AdamW fixed weight decay in adaptive optimizers; the GPT line's runs used Adam-family training generically - a sibling refinement, not a consumed milestone.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Loshchilov & Hutter, 2017) decoupling weight decay from gradient-based updates in Adam, improving generalization.
raw_candidates.source_title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization

raw_candidates.name: QRNN
raw_candidates.causal_claim: QRNNs were the efficiency-focused RNN alternative of the PTB era; part of the displaced RNN-LM landscape, no channel into GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Bradbury et al., 2016) quasi-recurrent networks pooling convolutions across time for faster sequence modeling.
raw_candidates.source_title: Quasi-Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Continuous cache and dynamic evaluation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Cache/dynamic-evaluation tricks squeezed RNN LMs by exploiting recency at test time; test-time adaptation ideas the GPT-2 demonstration did not use.
raw_candidates.definition: Methods (Grave et al., 2016; Krause et al., 2017) improving LM perplexity via cache models and test-time gradient adaptation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Improving Neural Language Models with a Continuous Cache

raw_candidates.name: On the State of the Art of Evaluation in Neural Language Models
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Melis et al. showed tuned LSTMs rivaling newer architectures - the evaluation-hygiene debate framing GPT-2's era; commentary, not a component.
raw_candidates.definition: Study (Melis, Dyer & Blunsom, 2017) demonstrating standard LSTM LMs with tuned hyperparameters match or beat newer architectures.
raw_candidates.source_title: On the State of the Art of Evaluation in Neural Language Models

raw_candidates.name: Winograd Schemas
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Winograd schemas defined the commonsense coreference challenge used to probe LM understanding of the era; evaluation ancestry for GPT-2's claims.
raw_candidates.definition: Challenge set (Levesque, 2011) of pronoun-resolution problems designed to require commonsense reasoning.
raw_candidates.source_title: The Winograd Schema Challenge

raw_candidates.name: Story Cloze and ROCStories
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Story Cloze probed narrative understanding in the GPT-1-era evaluation suite; part of the task landscape, not an input to GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark (Mostafazadeh et al., 2016) choosing the right ending for five-sentence stories, over the ROCStories corpus.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Corpus and Cloze Evaluation for Deeper Understanding of Commonsense Stories

raw_candidates.name: MultiNLI
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MultiNLI was a flagship transfer task of the GPT-1 fine-tuning demonstration; GPT-2's zero-shot stance bypassed the fine-tune eval regime it belongs to.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Williams, Nangia & Bowman, 2017) of 433k sentence pairs for natural language inference across genres.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Broad-Coverage Challenge Corpus for Sentence Understanding through Inference

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Parameters move in the direction of steepest decrease of the loss.
raw_candidates.lineage: Optimization substrate of all neural training.
raw_candidates.name: Gradient descent
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Optimizes a function iteratively by stepping against its gradient.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: The optimization primitive under nearly all ML training.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Shared hidden layers are trained on multiple task losses, biasing toward reusable structure.
raw_candidates.lineage: Conceptual frame for ICL as implicit multi-task learning.
raw_candidates.name: Multi-task learning
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Improved generalization by training related tasks together with shared representations.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: The framework GPT-2's paper invoked for zero-shot transfer.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: 14M WordNet-organized images labeled via crowdsourcing.
raw_candidates.lineage: Vision transfer precedent for NLP transfer learning.
raw_candidates.name: ImageNet
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Gave vision a million-scale labeled dataset that made pretraining transfer practical.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Pretrain-then-fine-tune in vision became the template NLP imported.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A relation module scores query-support pairs instead of using a fixed distance.
raw_candidates.name: Relation Networks
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Learned the comparison metric itself for few-shot classification.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Extended metric-based few-shot learning.

aliases: Siamese Neural Networks for One-shot Image Recognition
raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Twin networks embed two inputs; a distance over embeddings scores sameness.
raw_candidates.name: Siamese networks for one-shot learning
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Recognized new classes from a single example via learned similarity.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Early deep one-shot learning result.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A sequence model reads labeled examples and predicts for queries using attention to history.
raw_candidates.name: SNAIL
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Meta-learned with temporal convolutions and attention over past experience.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Strong few-shot results with a model-based meta-learner.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Move the initialization toward weights obtained after training on a sampled task.
raw_candidates.name: Reptile
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Simplified first-order meta-learning for fast adaptation.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Widely used simple meta-learning baseline.

aliases: Optimization as a Model for Few-Shot Learning
raw_candidates.key_mechanism: An LSTM meta-learner ingests gradients and updates the learner's parameters cell-state style.
raw_candidates.name: LSTM meta-learner
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Learned an optimizer that adapts a learner to few-shot tasks.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Optimization-based meta-learning milestone.

aliases: Learning to learn by gradient descent by gradient descent
raw_candidates.key_mechanism: An LSTM optimizer is meta-trained by backpropagating through optimization runs.
raw_candidates.name: Learning to learn by gradient descent
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Replaced hand-designed optimizers with a learned recurrent optimizer.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Founded learned-optimizer research.

aliases: One-shot Learning with Memory-Augmented Neural Networks
raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A controller writes labeled examples to memory and reads them back for later queries.
raw_candidates.name: Memory-Augmented Neural Networks
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Learned from a single example by binding it to external memory in one shot.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Model-based meta-learning milestone for one-shot tasks.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A meta network produces fast weights for a base learner conditioned on support examples.
raw_candidates.name: Meta Networks
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Adapted rapidly by generating fast weights from task context.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Fast-weight meta-learning milestone.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Context points are encoded and aggregated into a representation conditioning the decoder.
raw_candidates.name: Conditional Neural Processes
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Predicted functions from a few context points in one forward pass.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Founded the neural-process family of conditional meta-learning.

aliases: Human-level concept learning through probabilistic program induction
raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Probabilistic programs compose primitives into concepts, inferred by Bayesian sampling.
raw_candidates.name: Bayesian program learning
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Matched human one-shot concept learning on handwritten characters.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Set the human-level one-shot benchmark (Omniglot).

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A small hypernetwork outputs the weights of a larger main network.
raw_candidates.name: Hypernetworks
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Generated one network's weights with another network conditioned on context.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Established weight-generation as a conditioning mechanism.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A Fisher-information penalty protects weights important to earlier tasks.
raw_candidates.lineage: Continual-learning fix for the paradigm ICL sidesteps.
raw_candidates.name: Elastic weight consolidation
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Reduced catastrophic forgetting when learning sequential tasks.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Standard continual-learning baseline.

aliases: Google's Multilingual Neural Machine Translation System
raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A single NMT model with a target-language token transfers across pairs zero-shot.
raw_candidates.name: Multilingual zero-shot translation
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Translated between language pairs never seen together in training.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: First large-scale zero-shot transfer phenomenon in production NNs.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A shared leaderboard of sentence and sentence-pair tasks.
raw_candidates.lineage: Measurement of the paradigm ICL displaced.
raw_candidates.name: GLUE
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Measured general language understanding across nine tasks in one benchmark.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: The scoreboard of the fine-tune era.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Questions whose answers are spans in Wikipedia paragraphs, crowdsourced.
raw_candidates.name: SQuAD
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Gave reading comprehension a 100k-question benchmark.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Drove the transfer-era QA race.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: An encoder-decoder is trained to predict surrounding sentences.
raw_candidates.name: Skip-thought vectors
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Learned generic sentence representations without labels.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Early unsupervised sentence-representation milestone.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Transformer or deep-averaging encoders trained on multi-task data.
raw_candidates.name: Universal Sentence Encoder
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Provided off-the-shelf sentence embeddings for transfer tasks.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Widely used transfer embeddings.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Entropy and n-gram statistics measure the predictability of symbol sequences.
raw_candidates.name: Shannon information theory
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Quantified information and prediction, founding statistical language modeling.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Foundation of information theory and LM evaluation.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Conditional probabilities over word histories with smoothing and backoff.
raw_candidates.name: N-gram language models
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Predicted words from fixed-order Markov statistics for speech recognition.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Standard LM technology for three decades.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Hebbian traces modulated by learned coefficients, trained by gradient descent.
raw_candidates.name: Differentiable plasticity
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Learned per-connection plasticity rules for fast within-lifetime adaptation.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Fast-adaptation mechanism research line.

raw_candidates.name: TRPO (trust region policy optimization)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PPO's direct predecessor - PPO is explicitly 'a first-order approximation of TRPO' that keeps its stability without second-order machinery.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Schulman et al., 2015): policy updates constrained to a trust region via a KL bound, with monotonic-improvement guarantees.
raw_candidates.source_title: Trust Region Policy Optimization

raw_candidates.name: REINFORCE (Williams)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The founding policy-gradient method; the entire lineage PPO belongs to descends from it.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Williams, 1992): gradient ascent on expected reward using sampled returns - the original policy-gradient estimator.
raw_candidates.source_title: Simple statistical gradient-following algorithms for connectionist reinforcement learning

raw_candidates.name: Policy gradient theorem (Sutton et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The mathematical foundation that makes policy-gradient methods (REINFORCE, actor-critic, TRPO, PPO) well-defined.
raw_candidates.definition: Theorem (Sutton, McAllester, Singh & Mansour, 2000): the gradient of expected return can be written without differentiating the state distribution.
raw_candidates.source_title: Policy Gradient Methods for Reinforcement Learning with Function Approximation

raw_candidates.name: Actor-critic methods (Konda & Tsitsiklis)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The variance-reduction architecture inside TRPO/PPO practice - but consumed packaged in those methods, not directly.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Konda & Tsitsiklis, 2000-2003): a critic estimates values to reduce the variance of an actor's policy-gradient updates.
raw_candidates.source_title: Actor-Critic Algorithms

raw_candidates.name: Natural policy gradient (Kakade)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The intellectual parent of trust-region methods; its channel into PPO runs through TRPO.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Kakade, 2002): follow the gradient in the Fisher-information metric rather than raw parameter space.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Natural Policy Gradient

raw_candidates.name: Conservative policy iteration (Kakade & Langford)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: An early improvement-guarantee method whose lineage runs into TRPO.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Kakade & Langford, 2002): conservative mixture updates with approximate monotonic improvement guarantees.
raw_candidates.source_title: Approximately Optimal Approximate Reinforcement Learning

raw_candidates.name: Generalized advantage estimation (GAE)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PPO's companion estimator - the advantage signal PPO's clipped objective consumes in standard implementations (and in all RLHF codebases).
raw_candidates.definition: Estimator (Schulman et al., 2016): exponentially-weighted advantage estimates trading bias against variance via a lambda parameter.
raw_candidates.source_title: High-Dimensional Continuous Control Using Generalized Advantage Estimation

raw_candidates.name: Deep Q-Network (DQN)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A parallel value-based lineage; PPO's policy-gradient family does not consume it.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Mnih et al., 2015): value-based deep RL with experience replay and target networks, reaching human-level Atari play.
raw_candidates.source_title: Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning

raw_candidates.name: A3C asynchronous actor-critic
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A contemporary baseline PPO was compared against, not an input to it.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Mnih et al., 2016): asynchronous parallel actor-learners for actor-critic RL.
raw_candidates.source_title: Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning

raw_candidates.name: OpenAI Gym
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Infrastructure the RL community used, but not a causal input to PPO's algorithm.
raw_candidates.definition: Toolkit (Brockman et al., 2016): standardized RL environments and evaluation protocol.
raw_candidates.source_title: OpenAI Gym

raw_candidates.name: Importance sampling for off-policy evaluation (Precup et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PPO's probability-ratio objective is importance-sampling-flavored, but the consumed formulation arrives via TRPO's surrogate objective.
raw_candidates.definition: Technique (Precup, Sutton & Dasgupta, 2000): reweight trajectories from a behavior policy to evaluate a target policy.
raw_candidates.source_title: Eligibility Traces for Off-Policy Policy Evaluation

raw_candidates.name: DDPG (deep deterministic policy gradient)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A parallel off-policy lineage; not consumed by PPO.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Lillicrap et al., 2016): off-policy deterministic actor-critic for continuous control.
raw_candidates.source_title: Continuous control with deep reinforcement learning

raw_candidates.name: Soft actor-critic (SAC)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Postdates PPO (2017) - a successor branch, not a predecessor.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Haarnoja et al., 2018): maximum-entropy off-policy actor-critic.
raw_candidates.source_title: Soft Actor-Critic

raw_candidates.name: Evolution strategies (Salimans et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with PPO (2017) and a rival approach, not a predecessor.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Salimans et al., 2017, OpenAI): black-box evolution strategies as a scalable RL alternative.
raw_candidates.source_title: Evolution Strategies as a Scalable Alternative to Reinforcement Learning

candidate.name: Neural probabilistic language model
candidate.causal_claim: Bengio's NPLM founded neural language modeling - distributed word representations learned jointly with the LM; the deep ancestor of the pretraining lineage, reaching GPT-2 through GPT-1 and the Transformer succession.
candidate.definition: Model (Bengio et al., 2003) learning distributed word embeddings jointly with a neural LM, beating n-gram models on perplexity.
candidate.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

candidate.name: Word2vec
candidate.causal_claim: Word2vec industrialized learned embeddings, the representation premise pretraining scaled; it reaches GPT-2 through the whole pretraining tradition.
candidate.definition: Method (Mikolov et al., 2013) learning word embeddings from co-occurrence prediction at scale.
candidate.source_title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

candidate.name: RNN language modeling (Mikolov)
candidate.causal_claim: Mikolov's RNNLM showed neural LMs decisively beating n-gram baselines, restarting LM research as a neural discipline; an ancestor at several removes.
candidate.definition: Recurrent neural LM (Mikolov et al., 2010) reducing perplexity and WER substantially over backoff n-gram models.
candidate.source_title: Recurrent neural network based language model

candidate.name: Byte-pair encoding for NMT
candidate.causal_claim: BPE subword segmentation is GPT-2's tokenization family (byte-level BPE); the segmentation scheme was inherited as part of the GPT-1 recipe and tooling.
candidate.definition: Segmentation method (Sennrich et al., 2016) applying byte-pair encoding to learn subword units, fixing rare-word handling in neural MT.
candidate.source_title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

candidate.name: Layer normalization
candidate.causal_claim: LayerNorm stabilizes the Transformer blocks GPT-2 stacks (moved to pre-norm in GPT-2); it arrives inside the inherited GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
candidate.definition: Normalization method (Ba, Kiros & Hinton, 2016) normalizing layer activations per example, stabilizing recurrent and deep training.
candidate.source_title: Layer Normalization

candidate.name: Adam optimizer
candidate.causal_claim: Adam is the optimizer family the GPT line trained with; a commodity component of the inherited training recipe, not a GPT-2-specific enabler.
candidate.definition: Optimizer (Kingma & Ba, 2014) with adaptive per-parameter rates from first/second moment estimates; became deep learning's default.
candidate.source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

candidate.name: GELU activation
candidate.causal_claim: GELU is the activation the GPT line adopted from GPT-1 onward; it reaches GPT-2 inside the inherited architecture.
candidate.definition: Activation (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016) weighting inputs by their Gaussian CDF, adopted across Transformer models.
candidate.source_title: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)

candidate.name: BooksCorpus
candidate.causal_claim: BooksCorpus was GPT-1's pretraining corpus - the data half of the recipe GPT-2 replaced with WebText; its channel runs through GPT-1.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Zhu et al., 2015) of 11,038 unpublished books (~74M sentences) used to train the original GPT.
candidate.source_title: Aligning Books and Movies: Towards Story-like Visual Explanations by Watching Movies and Reading Books

candidate.name: Common Crawl
candidate.causal_claim: Common Crawl is the web-scale corpus infrastructure of the era; GPT-2's WebText was deliberately NOT Common Crawl (Reddit-linked pages instead), so the channel is weak.
candidate.definition: Nonprofit web archive (founded 2007-08) providing petabytes of crawled web pages used to train many LMs.
candidate.source_title: Common Crawl

candidate.name: AlexNet
candidate.causal_claim: AlexNet opened the deep-learning era whose scaling logic GPT-2 extends to language; it reaches GPT-2 through the entire deep-learning succession, not directly.
candidate.definition: CNN (Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, 2012) winning ImageNet by a wide margin with GPU training, founding the deep-learning era.
candidate.source_title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

candidate.name: CUDA GPU computing
candidate.causal_claim: CUDA made the GPU training of every model in this lineage practical; it reaches GPT-2 as inherited infrastructure, two successions removed.
candidate.definition: Platform (NVIDIA, 2007) exposing GPU parallelism to general computation, the substrate of deep-learning training economics.
candidate.source_title: CUDA

candidate.name: Backpropagation
candidate.causal_claim: Backpropagation trained every network in the lineage; it reaches GPT-2 through the models and recipes that embody it.
candidate.definition: Algorithm (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986) computing gradients through layered networks by the chain rule.
candidate.source_title: Backpropagation

candidate.name: LSTM
candidate.causal_claim: LSTMs were the pre-Transformer LM substrate (ELMo, ULMFiT); GPT-2's lineage displaced them via the Transformer, which is the channel.
candidate.definition: Recurrent architecture (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) with gated memory cells for long-range sequence learning.
candidate.source_title: Long short-term memory

candidate.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
candidate.causal_claim: Seq2seq founded neural sequence transduction; it reaches GPT-2 through the Transformer that displaced it.
candidate.definition: Framework (Sutskever et al., 2014) mapping sequences to sequences with LSTM encoder-decoders.
candidate.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

candidate.name: Bahdanau attention
candidate.causal_claim: Bahdanau attention is the Transformer's own predecessor; it reaches GPT-2 inside self-attention, via the Transformer.
candidate.definition: Mechanism (Bahdanau et al., 2014) letting a decoder attend over encoder states in neural MT.
candidate.source_title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

candidate.name: Matching Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Matching Networks did one-shot classification by attention over support examples - a conditioning-flavored few-shot method, but embedding-based and never consumed by the GPT line.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Vinyals et al., 2016) for one-shot learning via attention over a support set in embedding space.
candidate.source_title: Matching Networks for One Shot Learning

candidate.name: Zero-shot learning via attributes
candidate.causal_claim: Attribute-based zero-shot classification in vision showed category transfer without examples a decade earlier - a conceptual sibling in another modality, with no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Method (Lampert, Nickisch & Harmeling, 2009) classifying unseen animal classes via human-specified attribute vectors.
candidate.source_title: Learning to detect unseen object classes by between-class attribute transfer

candidate.name: Kneser-Ney smoothing
candidate.causal_claim: Kneser-Ney was the statistical-LM state of the art the neural lineage displaced; ancestry of the task, not of the method.
candidate.definition: Smoothing technique (Kneser & Ney, 1995) for n-gram LMs, the best-performing backoff scheme of the statistical era.
candidate.source_title: Kneser-Ney smoothing

candidate.name: Perplexity as LM metric
candidate.causal_claim: Perplexity (Jelinek-era) is the yardstick GPT-2's log-linear scaling claim is stated in; a measurement convention, not an enabler of the capability.
candidate.definition: Metric from speech-recognition LM evaluation (Jelinek, 1970s): exponentiated cross-entropy of a test set under the model.
candidate.source_title: Perplexity

candidate.name: One Billion Word Benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: The 1B Word Benchmark standardized neural LM comparison in the pre-Transformer years; part of the evaluation lineage, not an input to GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Benchmark (Chelba et al., 2013) for statistical language modeling at billion-word scale.
candidate.source_title: One Billion Word Benchmark for Measuring Progress in Statistical Language Modeling

candidate.name: Penn Treebank LM benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: PTB was the small-data LM testbed of the neural-LM era (Mikolov's RNNLM results); evaluation ancestry only.
candidate.definition: Corpus (Marcus et al., 1993) whose LM split became the standard small benchmark for neural language models.
candidate.source_title: Penn Treebank

candidate.name: TensorFlow
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-1/GPT-2 were implemented in TensorFlow; commodity tooling any equivalent framework replaces, not a milestone in the method's causal chain.
candidate.definition: Google's open-source deep-learning framework (2015) for dataflow graph computation.
candidate.source_title: TensorFlow

candidate.name: PyTorch
candidate.causal_claim: PyTorch was the era's other framework; the GPT line's public code was TensorFlow-based, so even the tooling channel points elsewhere.

candidate.name: Distributed training (parameter servers)
candidate.causal_claim: Large-scale distributed training patterns underpin all big-model runs of the era; GPT-2's 1.5B training was modest by later standards and consumed no specific distributed-training milestone.

candidate.source_title: Scaling Distributed Machine Learning with the Parameter Server

candidate.name: Curriculum learning
candidate.causal_claim: Curriculum learning orders training examples easy-to-hard; GPT-2's training used no curriculum - a named idea in the training-methods space with no channel.

candidate.name: Generating sequences with RNNs (Graves)

candidate.source_title: Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks

candidate.name: GloVe

candidate.name: Fast weights (Schmidhuber)
candidate.causal_claim: Schmidhuber's fast-weight programmers proposed one network programming another via weight changes - a conceptual ancestor of conditioning, cited by later meta-learning, with no channel into GPT-2's work.
candidate.definition: Proposal (Schmidhuber, 1992) in which a slow network generates fast weights for another network, an early form of learned adaptation.
candidate.source_title: Learning to Control Fast-Weight Memories: An Alternative to Dynamic Recurrent Networks

candidate.name: Learning to learn (Thrun & Pratt)
candidate.causal_claim: The learning-to-learn literature framed transfer as meta-knowledge decades before; framing ancestry for few-shot claims, not a consumed component.

candidate.name: Neural Turing Machines
candidate.causal_claim: NTMs coupled networks to external memory; an alternative augmentation direction that the GPT lineage did not take.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2014) giving a neural controller differentiable read/write access to an external memory bank.

candidate.name: Memory Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Memory Networks answered questions over an explicit memory store; a sibling QA architecture with no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Weston, Chopra & Bordes, 2014) combining learned representations with a long-term memory component for QA.
candidate.source_title: Memory Networks

candidate.name: End-to-End Memory Networks
candidate.causal_claim: MemN2N made memory attention end-to-end differentiable; part of the attention-era QA landscape, not GPT-2's lineage.
candidate.definition: Model (Sukhbaatar et al., 2015) reading memory with multiple attention hops, trained end-to-end.
candidate.source_title: End-To-End Memory Networks

candidate.name: Differentiable Neural Computer
candidate.causal_claim: The DNC was DeepMind's flagship memory-augmented architecture; a parallel direction with no channel into the GPT line.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2016) coupling a neural controller to an external memory matrix with differentiable addressing.
candidate.source_title: Hybrid computing using a neural network with dynamic external memory

candidate.name: Residual networks (ResNet)
candidate.causal_claim: Residual connections are inside every Transformer block GPT-2 stacks; they arrive as part of the Transformer/GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
candidate.definition: Architecture (He et al., 2015) with skip connections enabling training of 100+ layer networks, winning ImageNet 2015.
candidate.source_title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

candidate.name: Dropout
candidate.causal_claim: Dropout is a standard regularizer inside the inherited training recipe; commodity component, not a GPT-2 enabler in the milestone sense.
candidate.definition: Regularization technique (Srivastava et al., 2014) randomly dropping units during training to prevent co-adaptation.
candidate.source_title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting

candidate.name: Batch normalization
candidate.causal_claim: BatchNorm normalized activations across batches; the Transformer line standardized on LayerNorm instead, so even the component channel points to its sibling.
candidate.definition: Method (Ioffe & Szegedy, 2015) normalizing layer inputs per mini-batch, accelerating deep training.
candidate.source_title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift

candidate.name: Weight initialization (Xavier/He)
candidate.causal_claim: Principled initialization is inside every training run of the era; background technique, not a milestone GPT-2 distinctively consumed (GPT-2's scaled residual init is its own tweak).
candidate.definition: Initialization schemes (Glorot & Bengio, 2010; He et al., 2015) keeping activation/gradient scales stable across layers.
candidate.source_title: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks

candidate.name: Stochastic gradient descent with momentum
candidate.causal_claim: SGD is the optimization substrate of all of it; it reaches GPT-2 through every intervening training run and belongs many levels deeper in the trace.
candidate.definition: Optimization method (stochastic approximation, Robbins-Monro 1951; momentum, Polyak 1964) training models by noisy gradient steps.
candidate.source_title: Stochastic gradient descent

candidate.name: Automatic differentiation (autodiff)
candidate.causal_claim: Autodiff (Linnainmaa 1970; framework-era reverse mode) is how gradients are computed in practice; deep infrastructure ancestry, mediated by every framework and model above it.
candidate.definition: Technique (Linnainmaa, 1970) computing derivatives of composite functions by the chain rule in reverse accumulation order.
candidate.source_title: Automatic differentiation

candidate.name: Theano
candidate.causal_claim: Theano pioneered symbolic autodiff frameworks for research; GPT-2's stack was TensorFlow, so even the tooling lineage is a sibling.
candidate.definition: Python library (Bergstra et al., 2007-2010) for symbolic tensor computation and GPU code generation, from MILA.
candidate.source_title: Theano (software)

candidate.name: cuDNN
candidate.causal_claim: cuDNN's GPU kernels underlie all framework training of the era; commodity plumbing beneath the recipe, not a consumed milestone.
candidate.definition: NVIDIA library (2014) of GPU-accelerated primitives for deep neural networks.
candidate.source_title: cuDNN

candidate.name: Data parallelism and model parallelism practice
candidate.causal_claim: Multi-GPU training practice (from AlexNet's two-GPU split onward) is the era's background capability; GPT-2's 1.5B run consumed the practice generically, not a named milestone.

candidate.source_title: One weird trick for parallelizing convolutional neural networks

candidate.name: Reddit as a curated data source
candidate.causal_claim: WebText's curation trick was scraping pages linked from Reddit with karma>=3 - a data choice inside GPT-2's own contribution, using a commodity platform; the platform is not a milestone predecessor.

candidate.source_title: Reddit

candidate.name: Wikipedia as training corpus
candidate.causal_claim: Wikipedia text trained half the models of the era; GPT-2's WebText notably drew on Reddit-linked pages broadly - corpus plumbing, not a milestone in the method's chain.
candidate.definition: Free encyclopedia (founded 2001) whose text became a standard LM training and evaluation corpus.
candidate.source_title: Wikipedia

candidate.name: Shannon's n-gram entropy studies
candidate.causal_claim: Shannon's prediction-and-entropy work founded language modeling as a measurable science; the remotest task ancestry, mediated by the entire statistical and neural LM succession.
candidate.definition: Studies (Shannon, 1951) estimating the entropy of English via human prediction experiments, founding statistical language modeling.
candidate.source_title: Prediction and Entropy of Printed English

candidate.name: Markov chains for text
candidate.causal_claim: Markov's letter-sequence analysis of Pushkin is the first statistical text model; ancestry of the task across a century of intermediaries.
candidate.definition: Analysis (Markov, 1913) of vowel/consonant sequences in Eugene Onegin, the first application of Markov chains to text.
candidate.source_title: Markov chain

candidate.name: Feedforward neural LM (Bengio follow-ups)
candidate.causal_claim: Duplicate-angle variant of the NPLM line (already scouted as the neural probabilistic LM); dedupe is expected to merge or drop it.

candidate.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

candidate.name: Hierarchical softmax and NCE
candidate.causal_claim: Output-layer approximations made large-vocabulary neural LMs trainable in the Mikolov era; GPT-2's full softmax at 50k vocab on modern hardware no longer needed them - a displaced enabling trick of the prior era.
candidate.definition: Techniques (Morin & Bengio, 2005; Mnih & Teh, 2012; Gutmann & Hyvarinen, 2010) approximating the softmax partition function for large vocabularies.
candidate.source_title: Noise-contrastive estimation

candidate.name: Character-aware LM (Kim et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: Character-CNN word models addressed open vocabularies compositionally; the GPT line solved the same problem with BPE instead - a sibling solution, not a channel.
candidate.definition: Model (Kim et al., 2015) composing word representations from character CNNs for language modeling.
candidate.source_title: Character-Aware Neural Language Models

candidate.name: Pointer-sentinel and variational LM advances
candidate.causal_claim: Mid-2010s PTB-era LM refinements (pointer sentinel, variational dropout) mark the RNN-LM era's ceiling that the Transformer succession displaced; no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Models (Merity et al., 2016; Gal & Ghahramani, 2016) pushing RNN LM perplexity via pointer mechanisms and variational dropout.
candidate.source_title: Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models

candidate.name: Semi-supervised sequence learning
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Dai & Le's sequence-autoencoding pretraining anticipated LM pretraining for classification in 2015; an early paradigm ancestor whose channel runs through the 2018 wave.
candidate.definition: Method (Dai & Le, 2015) pretraining sequence models by LM/autoencoding before supervised fine-tuning, improving classification.
candidate.source_title: Semi-supervised Sequence Learning

candidate.name: LAMBADA
candidate.causal_claim: LAMBADA was a headline zero-shot test in GPT-2's paper (accuracy jumping with scale); a testbed the result was measured on, not a component of the method.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Paperno et al., 2016) of narrative passages whose final word requires broad discourse context, designed to defeat local-context models.
candidate.source_title: The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context

candidate.name: Children's Book Test
candidate.causal_claim: CBT was among GPT-2's zero-shot evaluation suites; evaluation ancestry only.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Hill et al., 2015/2016) of children's-book sentences with a missing word to predict from context, for evaluating reading models.
candidate.source_title: The Goldilocks Principle: Reading Children's Books with Explicit Memory Representations

candidate.name: WikiText
candidate.causal_claim: WikiText-103 was a standard LM benchmark in GPT-2's zero-shot perplexity tables; a yardstick, not an enabler.
candidate.definition: Benchmark (Merity et al., 2016) of 103M tokens from verified Wikipedia articles for long-term LM evaluation.
candidate.source_title: Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models

candidate.name: CNN/Daily Mail summarization dataset
candidate.causal_claim: CNN/Daily Mail was the corpus for GPT-2's zero-shot summarization probe (TL;DR prompting); evaluation lineage only.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Hermann et al., 2015) of news articles with bullet summaries, repurposed as the standard abstractive summarization benchmark.
candidate.source_title: Teaching Machines to Read and Comprehend

candidate.name: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling
candidate.causal_claim: Jozefowicz et al. pushed LSTM LMs to their limits and catalogued what scale bought before Transformers - the immediate pre-history of the scaling question GPT-2 answered differently.
candidate.definition: Study (Jozefowicz et al., 2016) training very large LSTM LMs on the 1B Word Benchmark, analyzing architectures and output layers at scale.
candidate.source_title: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling

candidate.name: WaveNet
candidate.causal_claim: WaveNet showed autoregressive generation at unprecedented fidelity in audio - the generative-modeling era's emblem, in another modality; no channel into GPT-2's text result.

candidate.source_title: WaveNet: A Generative Model for Raw Audio

candidate.name: QRNN
candidate.causal_claim: QRNNs were the efficiency-focused RNN alternative of the PTB era; part of the displaced RNN-LM landscape, no channel into GPT-2.

candidate.name: Continuous cache and dynamic evaluation
candidate.causal_claim: Cache/dynamic-evaluation tricks squeezed RNN LMs by exploiting recency at test time; test-time adaptation ideas the GPT-2 demonstration did not use.

candidate.causal_claim: Winograd schemas defined the commonsense coreference challenge used to probe LM understanding of the era; evaluation ancestry for GPT-2's claims.

candidate.source_title: The Winograd Schema Challenge

candidate.name: Story Cloze and ROCStories

candidate.name: TRPO (trust region policy optimization)

candidate.name: REINFORCE (Williams)

candidate.name: Policy gradient theorem (Sutton et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: The mathematical foundation that makes policy-gradient methods (REINFORCE, actor-critic, TRPO, PPO) well-defined.

candidate.name: Actor-critic methods (Konda & Tsitsiklis)

candidate.name: Natural policy gradient (Kakade)

candidate.name: Conservative policy iteration (Kakade & Langford)

candidate.name: Generalized advantage estimation (GAE)

candidate.name: Deep Q-Network (DQN)
