candidate.name: Generative pretraining (GPT-1)
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-1 is GPT-2's literal predecessor in the same lab: the Transformer-decoder generative-pretraining recipe GPT-2 scaled 10x and pushed from fine-tuning to zero-shot conditioning.
candidate.definition: OpenAI model (Radford et al., 2018): a 117M Transformer decoder pretrained on BooksCorpus, then fine-tuned per task, beating purpose-built models on 9 of 12 language-understanding tasks.
candidate.source_title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

candidate.name: Transformer architecture
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-2 is a stack of Transformer decoder blocks; the architecture reaches it as part of the GPT-1 recipe it inherited and scaled.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017) replacing recurrence with self-attention; the substrate of all modern LLMs.
candidate.source_title: Attention Is All You Need

candidate.name: ULMFiT
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: ULMFiT proved pretrain-then-fine-tune for NLP months before GPT-1, defining the transfer paradigm GPT-2's zero-shot move reacted against and extended.
candidate.definition: Method (Howard & Ruder, 2018): LM pretraining, LM fine-tuning, classifier fine-tuning with discriminative rates and gradual unfreezing, large gains on text classification.
candidate.source_title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification

candidate.name: ELMo
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: ELMo showed contextualized representations from a pretrained LM transfer broadly; part of the 2018 pretraining wave GPT-2's lineage runs through GPT-1, not ELMo's biLSTM design.
candidate.definition: Representation model (Peters et al., 2018): deep contextualized word vectors from a bidirectional LSTM LM, improving six NLP benchmarks.
candidate.source_title: Deep contextualized word representations

candidate.name: BERT
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: BERT is the encoder sibling of the 2018 pretraining wave - the alternative branch (masked, fine-tuned) to GPT-2's decoder, zero-shot branch; not consumed by GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Bidirectionally pretrained encoder (Devlin et al., 2018) whose fine-tuned representations reset NLP benchmarks.
candidate.source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

candidate.name: Deep learning scaling predictability (Hestness)
candidate.causal_claim: Hestness et al. showed learning curves follow predictable power laws with scale - the empirical backdrop for GPT-2's log-linear scaling bet, though GPT-2's paper derives its claim from its own runs.
candidate.definition: Study (Hestness et al., 2017) demonstrating predictable power-law scaling of model performance with data and model size across applications.
candidate.source_title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically

candidate.name: MAML meta-learning
candidate.causal_claim: MAML learns initializations for fast few-shot adaptation by gradient steps - the meta-learning paradigm GPT-2's conditioning-based few-shot bypassed entirely; no channel, as with ICL's expansion.
candidate.definition: Meta-learning algorithm (Finn, Abbeel & Levine, 2017) learning parameter initializations adaptable to new tasks in a few gradient steps.
candidate.source_title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks

candidate.name: Prototypical Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Prototypical Networks learn metric spaces for few-shot classification; part of the meta-learning paradigm with no channel into GPT-2's demonstration.
candidate.definition: Method (Snell, Swersky & Zemel, 2017) classifying by distance to class prototypes in a learned embedding space.
candidate.source_title: Prototypical Networks for Few-shot Learning

candidate.name: CoVe contextual vectors
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: CoVe transferred MT-encoder representations to downstream tasks, an early transfer-representation result in the run-up to ELMo/GPT-1; its channel runs through that 2018 wave.
candidate.definition: Representations (McCann et al., 2017) from a machine-translation encoder, improving classification and QA when concatenated with GloVe.
candidate.source_title: Learned in Translation: Contextualized Word Vectors

candidate.name: Transformer-XL
candidate.causal_claim: Transformer-XL extended context via recurrence in Jan 2019 - coeval with GPT-2 (same year), listed to be dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Dai et al., 2019) adding segment-level recurrence and relative positions to the Transformer for longer contexts.
candidate.source_title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context

candidate.name: XLNet
candidate.causal_claim: XLNet's permutation LM was 2019's alternative pretraining objective - coeval with GPT-2, dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: Pretraining method (Yang et al., 2019) maximizing likelihood over permutation orders, combining autoregressive and autoencoding advantages.
candidate.source_title: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding

candidate.name: RoBERTa
candidate.causal_claim: RoBERTa showed BERT was undertrained - a coeval 2019 replication study, dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: Study (Liu et al., 2019) optimizing BERT's training recipe for substantially better results.
candidate.source_title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach

candidate.name: ERNIE
candidate.causal_claim: Baidu's ERNIE added knowledge masking to pretraining in 2019 - coeval, dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: Pretraining model (Sun et al., 2019) masking entities and phrases to inject knowledge into representations.
candidate.source_title: ERNIE: Enhanced Representation through Knowledge Integration

candidate.name: GPT-2 staged release and 'too dangerous to release' debate
candidate.causal_claim: The staged-release controversy is part of GPT-2's own 2019 story, not a predecessor - coeval, dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: OpenAI's staged release of GPT-2 (Feb-Nov 2019) over misuse concerns, a landmark in release-policy debates.
candidate.source_title: GPT-2

candidate.name: AWD-LSTM
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: AWD-LSTM was the strongest RNN LM recipe ULMFiT built on; it reaches GPT-2 through the ULMFiT/GPT-1 paradigm succession, as a SUBTYPE-relative of the LSTM line.
candidate.definition: Regularized LSTM LM (Merity, Keskar & Socher, 2017) whose recipe powered ULMFiT's transfer results.
candidate.source_title: Regularizing and Optimizing LSTM Language Models

candidate.name: Contextual pre-training via language modeling (Peters 2017 NAACL)
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: The tagLM work preceding ELMo showed LM states helping sequence labelers; ancestry inside the ELMo branch of the 2018 wave.
candidate.definition: Work (Peters et al., 2017) augmenting sequence labelers with pretrained LM representations (tagLM), the direct run-up to ELMo.
candidate.source_title: Semi-supervised sequence tagging with bidirectional language models

candidate.name: CoQA
candidate.causal_claim: CoQA supplied GPT-2's flagship zero-shot number (55 F1 without task training); the stage for the demonstration, not an input to it.
candidate.definition: Conversational QA dataset (Reddy, Chen & Manning, 2018) of 127k questions over dialogues about passages, with rationale spans.
candidate.source_title: CoQA: A Conversational Question Answering Challenge

candidate.name: RACE reading comprehension
candidate.causal_claim: RACE was part of the reading-comprehension evaluation landscape GPT-2's zero-shot claims were situated in; not an input.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Lai et al., 2017) of 100k English-exam questions for middle/high school students, for reading comprehension.
candidate.source_title: RACE: Large-scale ReAding Comprehension Dataset From Examinations

candidate.name: GLUE benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: GLUE defined the fine-tuning era's scoreboard that GPT-2's zero-shot stance implicitly argued against; the incumbent measurement regime, not an enabler.
candidate.definition: Benchmark (Wang et al., 2018) of nine sentence-level understanding tasks that standardized transfer evaluation for BERT-era models.
candidate.source_title: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark and Analysis Platform for Natural Language Understanding

candidate.name: ConvS2S
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Convolutional seq2seq was Facebook's parallel bet to the Transformer in 2017 - the sibling architecture line that lost; no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Gehring et al., 2017) using gated convolutions with attention for sequence-to-sequence tasks, matching RNN quality faster.
candidate.source_title: Convolutional Sequence to Sequence Learning

candidate.name: Sparsely-Gated MoE
candidate.causal_claim: Shazeer's MoE scaled capacity via conditional computation - the road GPT-2 did not take (dense scaling); a sibling scaling philosophy with no channel.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Shazeer et al., 2017) inserting sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layers to reach 137B parameters with conditional compute.
candidate.source_title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer

candidate.name: Relative position encodings
candidate.causal_claim: Shaw et al.'s relative positions improved Transformer self-attention; GPT-2 used learned absolute positions from the GPT-1 design, so the component channel does not reach it.
candidate.definition: Method (Shaw, Uszkoreit & Vaswani, 2018) representing relative positions in self-attention, improving translation quality.
candidate.source_title: Self-Attention with Relative Position Representations

candidate.name: Mixed-precision training
candidate.causal_claim: Mixed precision became standard large-training practice in this era; a generic technique GPT-2's run may have used but which no milestone claim attaches to.
candidate.definition: Technique (Micikevicius et al., 2017) training in FP16 with FP32 master weights, halving memory and speeding large runs.
candidate.source_title: Mixed Precision Training

candidate.name: AdamW and decoupled weight decay
candidate.causal_claim: AdamW fixed weight decay in adaptive optimizers; the GPT line's runs used Adam-family training generically - a sibling refinement, not a consumed milestone.
candidate.definition: Method (Loshchilov & Hutter, 2017) decoupling weight decay from gradient-based updates in Adam, improving generalization.
candidate.source_title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization

candidate.name: On the State of the Art of Evaluation in Neural Language Models
candidate.causal_claim: Melis et al. showed tuned LSTMs rivaling newer architectures - the evaluation-hygiene debate framing GPT-2's era; commentary, not a component.
candidate.definition: Study (Melis, Dyer & Blunsom, 2017) demonstrating standard LSTM LMs with tuned hyperparameters match or beat newer architectures.
candidate.source_title: On the State of the Art of Evaluation in Neural Language Models

candidate.name: MultiNLI
candidate.causal_claim: MultiNLI was a flagship transfer task of the GPT-1 fine-tuning demonstration; GPT-2's zero-shot stance bypassed the fine-tune eval regime it belongs to.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Williams, Nangia & Bowman, 2017) of 433k sentence pairs for natural language inference across genres.
candidate.source_title: A Broad-Coverage Challenge Corpus for Sentence Understanding through Inference

candidate.name: GPT-2
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3 is GPT-2 scaled ~100x: same decoder architecture, same BPE tokenizer, same conditioning-based task specification - the paper's model section is explicitly GPT-2's design at larger scale.
candidate.definition: OpenAI model (Radford et al., 2019): 1.5B Transformer decoder trained on WebText, demonstrating zero-shot task transfer by conditioning.
candidate.source_title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

candidate.name: Sparse Transformer
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3's paper states it uses 'alternating dense and locally banded sparse attention patterns in the layers of the transformer, similar to the Sparse Transformer' - a directly consumed architectural component.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Child et al., 2019, OpenAI): factorized strided+local attention patterns reducing self-attention complexity for long sequences.
candidate.source_title: Sparse attention - LLM Wiki

candidate.name: Megatron-LM
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3 required model parallelism at 175B; Megatron-LM is the prominent 2019 demonstration of tensor parallelism - but no record shows GPT-3's training consumed NVIDIA's implementation rather than OpenAI's own.
candidate.definition: NVIDIA framework (Shoeybi et al., 2019): intra-layer tensor model parallelism for training multi-billion-parameter Transformers.
candidate.source_title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism

candidate.name: Scaling laws for neural language models (Kaplan et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3's 175B size choice follows the Kaplan scaling-law analysis from the same lab months earlier - coeval at year granularity.
candidate.definition: Empirical study (Kaplan et al., Jan 2020, OpenAI): loss follows power laws in model size, data, and compute, prescribing much larger models.
candidate.source_title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

candidate.name: CTRL conditional language model
candidate.causal_claim: A parallel demonstration of steerable large LMs; not part of GPT-3's lineage.
candidate.definition: Model (Keskar et al., 2019, Salesforce): 1.6B LM steered by control codes.
candidate.source_title: CTRL: A Conditional Transformer Language Model for Controllable Generation

candidate.name: T5 text-to-text transfer Transformer
candidate.causal_claim: A parallel pretraining paradigm (fine-tune per task); GPT-3's paper contrasts its in-context approach rather than consuming T5.
candidate.definition: Model/framework (Raffel et al., 2019, Google): unified text-to-text format with encoder-decoder Transformer pretrained on C4.
candidate.source_title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

candidate.name: SuperGLUE benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3 was evaluated on SuperGLUE few-shot; an evaluation target, not an enabler of the leap.
candidate.definition: Benchmark suite (Wang et al., 2019) of hard language-understanding tasks.
candidate.source_title: SuperGLUE: A Stickier Benchmark for General-Purpose Language Understanding Systems

candidate.name: Natural Questions dataset
candidate.causal_claim: A GPT-3 few-shot evaluation set, not an enabler.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019, Google): real search queries with Wikipedia answers.
candidate.source_title: Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research

candidate.name: Winogrande dataset
candidate.causal_claim: A GPT-3 evaluation set, not an enabler.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Sakaguchi et al., 2019): large-scale Winograd-style commonsense benchmark.
candidate.source_title: Winogrande: An Adversarial Winograd Schema Challenge at Scale

candidate.name: WebText corpus
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3 trained on WebText2, an expanded version of GPT-2's WebText - the channel runs through GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Dataset (OpenAI, 2019): web pages from outbound Reddit links, built for GPT-2.
candidate.source_title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

candidate.name: Microsoft-OpenAI Azure supercomputing partnership
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3's training run executed on the Microsoft-built cluster - an institutional/compute precondition rather than a technical milestone in the lineage.
candidate.definition: Partnership (announced Jul 2019): Microsoft invested $1B in OpenAI to build Azure AI supercomputing for large-model training.
candidate.source_title: Microsoft invests in OpenAI (2019 announcement)

candidate.name: DeepSpeed ZeRO optimizer
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with GPT-3 (2020); not part of GPT-3's training stack on the record.
candidate.definition: Library (Rajbhandari et al., 2020, Microsoft): memory-optimization for distributed training.
candidate.source_title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models

candidate.name: ELECTRA
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with GPT-3 (2020) and a parallel paradigm.
candidate.definition: Model (Clark et al., 2020, Google): replaced-token-detection pretraining.
candidate.source_title: ELECTRA: Pre-training Text Encoders as Discriminators Rather Than Generators

candidate.name: Reformer
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with GPT-3 (2020); not consumed by it.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Kitaev et al., 2020): LSH attention and reversible layers for efficient Transformers.
candidate.source_title: Reformer: The Efficient Transformer

candidate.name: Deep RL from human preferences (Christiano et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: Christiano-style preference learning directly enabled the agent's leap as the first demonstration that human comparisons could train a reward model guiding behavior — the seed of RLHF.
candidate.source_title: Why is ChatGPT so good? (Scale AI)
candidate.definition: Method (Christiano et al., 2017) learning a reward model from human preferences over trajectory segments and optimizing it with RL.

candidate.name: PPO (proximal policy optimization)
candidate.causal_claim: PPO directly enabled the agent's leap as the optimization algorithm that ran the RLHF stage aligning the agent's engine.
candidate.source_title: The Day We Stopped Predicting the Next Word: How ChatGPT Was Actually Built
candidate.definition: Policy-gradient RL algorithm (Schulman et al., 2017) with clipped surrogate objective; the standard optimizer for RLHF.

candidate.name: Large-scale pretraining (GPT-3)
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3-scale pretraining directly enabled the agent's leap by producing a single model with enough world knowledge and few-shot adaptability to serve as a general task engine.
candidate.source_title: AI Paper Review: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
candidate.definition: Training very large autoregressive language models on web-scale text; GPT-3 (175B) showed few-shot in-context task performance without fine-tuning.

candidate.name: Fine-tuning language models from human preferences (Ziegler et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: The first application of preference-based reward learning to language models - the direct methodological bridge between Christiano et al. 2017 and Stiennon et al. 2020 / InstructGPT.
candidate.definition: Method (Ziegler et al., 2019, OpenAI): train a reward model from human comparisons and fine-tune a pretrained LM (GPT-2) with PPO under a KL penalty.
candidate.source_title: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences - ADS

candidate.name: Learning to summarize from human feedback (Stiennon et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: The immediate predecessor of InstructGPT: same recipe, same lab, six shared authors; proved RLHF beats supervised baselines and human reference summaries.
candidate.definition: Method (Stiennon et al., 2020, OpenAI): full RLHF recipe - human comparisons, Bradley-Terry reward model, PPO with reference-KL penalty - applied to summarization at 1.3B-6.7B scale.
candidate.source_title: Learning to summarize from human feedback

candidate.name: Preference-based reinforcement learning (Wirth et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: The formal backdrop Christiano et al. operationalized at deep-RL scale in the same year; the consumed artifact in the lineage is Christiano's method.
candidate.definition: Survey/formalization (Wirth et al., 2017) of RL from trajectory preferences rather than numeric rewards.
candidate.source_title: Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning: A Formal Framework and a Survey

candidate.name: WebGPT
candidate.causal_claim: A sibling application of human-feedback fine-tuning, not an enabler of the RLHF recipe itself.
candidate.definition: System (Nakano et al., 2021, OpenAI): GPT-3 fine-tuned with human feedback to answer questions using a text browser.
candidate.source_title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback

candidate.name: InstructGPT
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with the RLHF node itself (same year, same work) - cannot be its predecessor at year granularity.
candidate.definition: System (Ouyang et al., 2022, OpenAI): SFT + RLHF on GPT-3 - the very system this graph's RLHF node is drawn from.
candidate.source_title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

candidate.name: Constitutional AI
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with RLHF (2022) and a parallel branch, not a predecessor.
candidate.definition: Method (Bai et al., 2022, Anthropic): RL from AI feedback (RLAIF) using a written constitution.
candidate.source_title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

candidate.name: Sparrow dialogue agent
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with RLHF (2022); a parallel application.
candidate.definition: System (Glaese et al., 2022, DeepMind): dialogue agent trained with human judgements and rule-based rewards.
candidate.source_title: Improving alignment of dialogue agents via targeted human judgements

candidate.name: Direct preference optimization (DPO)
candidate.causal_claim: Postdates the RLHF node (2022) - a successor/simplification, not a predecessor.
candidate.definition: Method (Rafailov et al., 2023): optimize policies directly on preference data, bypassing an explicit reward model.
candidate.source_title: Direct Preference Optimization

candidate.name: COACH (convergent actor-critic by humans)
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with Christiano et al. (2017) - a parallel human-feedback formulation, not a predecessor.
candidate.definition: Method (MacGlashan et al., 2017): human feedback interpreted as policy-dependent advantage rather than reward.
candidate.source_title: Interactive Learning from Policy-Dependent Human Feedback

candidate.name: Deep TAMER
candidate.causal_claim: Postdates Christiano et al. (2017).
candidate.definition: Method (Warnell et al., 2018): TAMER with deep function approximation for high-dimensional state spaces.
candidate.source_title: Deep TAMER: Interactive Agent Shaping in High-Dimensional State Spaces

raw_candidates.name: RNN Encoder–Decoder (Cho et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bahdanau et al. directly extended Cho et al.'s RNN Encoder–Decoder: same lab, same gated unit, and the fixed-length summary vector c is exactly what the alignment model replaces.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Cho et al., EMNLP 2014): two RNNs jointly trained to map a variable-length source sequence to a fixed-length vector and decode a target sequence from it; introduced the gated recurrent unit (GRU).
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder–Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation

raw_candidates.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Sutskever et al.'s deep-LSTM encoder–decoder is the other fixed-vector template Bahdanau et al. name as a proposer of NMT and set out to fix.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Sutskever et al., 2014): a multilayer LSTM reads a source sequence into a fixed-length vector and a second LSTM decodes the target, with source reversal easing optimization.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Gated recurrent unit (GRU)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bahdanau et al. reused Cho et al.'s gated hidden unit (reset and update gates) verbatim in both encoder and decoder of RNNsearch.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent unit (Cho et al., 2014) with reset and update gates that adaptively capture dependencies at multiple time scales, simpler than LSTM.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder–Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation

raw_candidates.name: On the Properties of Neural Machine Translation: Encoder–Decoder Approaches
raw_candidates.causal_claim: This analysis by Cho, van Merriënboer, Bahdanau and Bengio documented that basic encoder–decoder quality deteriorates rapidly as sentence length grows — the documented bottleneck Bahdanau et al. cite as their motivation.
raw_candidates.definition: Empirical study (SSST-8, 2014) showing fixed-vector encoder–decoder translation quality collapses with sentence length and unknown-word count.
raw_candidates.source_title: On the Properties of Neural Machine Translation: Encoder-Decoder Approaches

raw_candidates.name: Recurrent models of visual attention
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Mnih et al.'s RAM showed an RNN could learn where to look next via REINFORCE in the same season — the hard-attention sibling of Bahdanau's soft alignment, not an input to it.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Mnih et al., 2014) that processes an image through a sequence of stochastically chosen glimpses, trained with reinforcement learning (hard attention).
raw_candidates.source_title: Recurrent Models of Visual Attention

raw_candidates.name: Neural Turing Machines
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Graves et al.'s content-based addressing over an external memory is a parallel differentiable-attention design from the same autumn; no channel into RNNsearch is documented.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Graves, Wayne & Danihelka, 2014) coupling a neural controller to an external memory matrix via soft content- and location-based addressing.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Turing Machines

raw_candidates.name: Memory Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Weston et al.'s memory-augmented QA model is a coeval attention-adjacent design; it addresses a different task and was not consumed by the Montréal MT group.
raw_candidates.definition: Model class (Weston, Chopra & Bordes, 2014) pairing a long-term memory component with learned read/write and reasoning over stored facts for question answering.
raw_candidates.source_title: Memory Networks

raw_candidates.name: Multiple object recognition with visual attention
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Ba, Mnih & Kavukcuoglu's sequential glimpse model is another coeval hard-attention system; parallel work, no documented input into RNNsearch.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Ba, Mnih & Kavukcuoglu, 2014) recognizing multiple objects by a recurrent controller that steers a retina-like sensor over an image.
raw_candidates.source_title: Multiple Object Recognition with Visual Attention

raw_candidates.name: Fast and robust neural network joint models for statistical machine translation
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Devlin et al.'s feedforward joint model was the strongest neural component inside 2014 SMT pipelines; RNNsearch replaced the whole pipeline rather than consuming it.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Devlin et al., ACL 2014): a feedforward neural joint source-target language model integrated into phrase-based SMT, worth about 1 BLEU.
raw_candidates.source_title: Fast and Robust Neural Network Joint Models for Statistical Machine Translation

raw_candidates.name: Multilingual models for compositional distributed semantics
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Hermann & Blunsom's language-specific encoders, compared in Bahdanau et al.'s introduction, are a parallel 2014 encoder design the paper positions against, not one it builds on.
raw_candidates.definition: Models (Hermann & Blunsom, ACL 2014) learning sentence representations in two languages with separate encoders whose outputs are compared for semantic equivalence.
raw_candidates.source_title: Multilingual Models for Compositional Distributed Semantics

raw_candidates.name: A convolutional neural network for modelling sentences
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Kalchbrenner et al.'s dynamic CNN sentence model is a coeval alternative sentence encoder; RNNsearch's encoder is recurrent, not convolutional.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Kalchbrenner, Grefenstette & Blunsom, ACL 2014): a convolutional network with dynamic k-max pooling producing sentence representations for classification tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Convolutional Neural Network for Modelling Sentences

raw_candidates.name: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GloVe is a coeval embedding method; RNNsearch trained its word representations jointly from scratch and did not consume pretrained vectors.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Pennington, Socher & Manning, 2014) factoring a global word co-occurrence matrix to produce word vectors with linear semantic structure.
raw_candidates.source_title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

raw_candidates.name: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Adam appeared in December 2014, after RNNsearch was posted; Bahdanau et al. trained with Adadelta, so no channel exists.
raw_candidates.definition: Optimizer (Kingma & Ba, 2014) combining per-parameter adaptive learning rates with bias-corrected moment estimates; became the default deep-learning optimizer.
raw_candidates.source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

raw_candidates.name: Generating sequences with recurrent neural networks (Graves soft window)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Graves built the first working differentiable alignment in sequence transduction — a soft Gaussian window the network slides over an input text so it learns which characters it is writing; Bahdanau et al. explicitly discuss it and generalize it into content-based soft search over encoder annotations, freed from the monotonic window.
raw_candidates.definition: Model and mechanism (Graves, 2013): deep LSTM sequence generation whose handwriting-synthesis network conditions on a text through a differentiable soft window (mixture of Gaussians) that learns the alignment between characters and pen strokes.
raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Recurrent continuous translation models
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Kalchbrenner & Blunsom founded the neural MT attempt and are named in Bahdanau et al.'s introduction as proposers of NMT; but the template Bahdanau extended was Cho et al.'s encoder–decoder, through which any RCTM influence is mediated.
raw_candidates.definition: Model class (Kalchbrenner & Blunsom, EMNLP 2013): translation probabilities computed purely from continuous representations, with a recurrent target language model conditioned on a convolutional source-sentence model.
raw_candidates.source_title: Recurrent Continuous Translation Models

raw_candidates.name: Joint language and translation modeling with recurrent neural networks
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Auli et al.'s RNN joint model rescored SMT lattices with source-conditioned recurrent predictions; RNNsearch is an end-to-end architecture that does not consume lattice rescoring.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Auli, Galley, Quirk & Zweig, EMNLP 2013): an RNN language model augmented with a continuous representation of the source sentence, used to rescore phrase-based SMT output lattices for about 1.1 BLEU.
raw_candidates.source_title: Joint Language and Translation Modeling with Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: On the difficulty of training recurrent neural networks (gradient clipping)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Pascanu et al. analyzed exploding gradients and proposed norm clipping, part of the standard RNN training toolkit of the Montréal group; a training aid, not the alignment mechanism.
raw_candidates.definition: Analysis and recipe (Pascanu, Mikolov & Bengio, ICML 2013): a dynamical-systems account of vanishing/exploding gradients in RNNs and the gradient-norm clipping heuristic that made deep RNN training routine.
raw_candidates.source_title: On the Difficulty of Training Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: word2vec
raw_candidates.causal_claim: word2vec made trained word vectors famous the year before, but RNNsearch learned its embeddings jointly inside the translation model; no pretrained word2vec vectors were an input.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Mikolov et al., 2013): efficient prediction-based training (CBOW/skip-gram) of word vectors exhibiting linear semantic regularities.
raw_candidates.source_title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

raw_candidates.name: Continuous space translation models for phrase-based SMT
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Schwenk's feedforward continuous-space translation model estimated phrase-pair probabilities inside SMT; it belongs to the pipeline tradition RNNsearch replaced, and Schwenk's channel into Bahdanau runs through his co-authorship of Cho et al. 2014.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Schwenk, COLING 2012): a feedforward neural network with bag-of-words phrase representations directly estimating translation probabilities for phrase-based SMT, able to score unseen phrase pairs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Continuous Space Translation Models for Phrase-Based Statistical Machine Translation

raw_candidates.name: Learning where to attend with deep architectures for image tracking
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Denil et al. learned fixation policies for image tracking with deep architectures — attention as sequential selection in vision, cited by later surveys as same-spirit prior work, with no documented channel into the Montréal MT model.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Denil, Bazzani, Larochelle & de Freitas, Neural Computation 2012): deep architectures that learn where to fixate in an image for tracking, an early neural attention system.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning Where to Attend with Deep Architectures for Image Tracking

raw_candidates.name: Adadelta: An Adaptive Learning Rate Method
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Adadelta is the optimizer Bahdanau et al. actually used to train RNNsearch; a substitutable training component rather than the mechanism of the leap.
raw_candidates.definition: Optimizer (Zeiler, 2012) adapting per-dimension learning rates from a running window of gradients, removing the need to set a global learning rate.
raw_candidates.source_title: Adadelta: An Adaptive Learning Rate Method

raw_candidates.name: ImageNet classification with deep convolutional neural networks (AlexNet)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: AlexNet's 2012 rout made deep networks the default bet across ML and is the ambient credibility wave behind the 2013–14 neural MT attempts; it contributes no mechanism to RNNsearch.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, NeurIPS 2012): a GPU-trained deep CNN that cut ImageNet error from 26% to 15.3%, igniting the deep-learning era.
raw_candidates.source_title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Improving the neural network acoustic model with dropout (2012 preprint)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Dropout was circulating as a general regularizer in 2012–14, but RNNsearch's published recipe does not rest on it; no specific channel into the alignment mechanism.
raw_candidates.definition: Regularization method (Hinton et al., 2012; Srivastava et al., JMLR 2014): randomly dropping units during training to prevent co-adaptation, approximating an ensemble at test time.
raw_candidates.source_title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting

raw_candidates.name: LSTM neural network language models for speech recognition (Sundermeyer et al.)
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Sundermeyer et al. put LSTM language models into production ASR, part of the recurrent substrate the Montréal group inherited; the channel into Bahdanau runs through the gated-unit lineage, not this system.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Sundermeyer, Schlüter & Ney, ICASSP 2012): LSTM recurrent language models outperforming feedforward and class-based models in a large-vocabulary speech recognizer.
raw_candidates.source_title: LSTM Neural Networks for Language Modeling

raw_candidates.name: Learning to combine foveal glimpses with a third-order Boltzmann machine
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Larochelle & Hinton's glimpse model is the canonical pre-2014 neural attention system — sequential, hard, vision-based; later attention surveys group it as same-spirit prior work, but RNNsearch's differentiable content-based scoring does not descend from it by any documented channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Larochelle & Hinton, NeurIPS 2010): a Boltzmann machine with third-order connections that learns to accumulate shape evidence over a sequence of foveal fixations, deciding where to look next.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to combine foveal glimpses with a third-order Boltzmann machine

raw_candidates.name: Recurrent neural network based language model (Mikolov)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Mikolov's RNNLM established the recurrent decoder-side language model that encoder–decoders condition on a source; its influence on Bahdanau arrives through Cho et al.'s encoder–decoder, whose decoder is an RNNLM variant.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Mikolov et al., Interspeech 2010): a simple recurrent network language model that beat n-gram and feedforward models and revived RNNs for language tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Recurrent Neural Network Based Language Model

raw_candidates.name: Theano: a CPU and GPU math expression compiler
raw_candidates.causal_claim: RNNsearch was implemented in Theano (the Montréal lab's own toolkit, via the GroundHog MT library); tooling that hosts the experiment, substitutable in principle.
raw_candidates.definition: Software system (Bergstra et al., SciPy 2010): a Python library defining symbolic math expressions and compiling them to CPU/GPU code, the substrate of the Montréal deep-learning group's research code.
raw_candidates.source_title: Theano: A CPU and GPU Math Expression Compiler

raw_candidates.name: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks (Xavier initialization)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Glorot & Bengio's initialization analysis is part of the era's general training toolkit; no specific channel into the alignment mechanism is documented.
raw_candidates.definition: Analysis and recipe (Glorot & Bengio, AISTATS 2010): variance-preserving weight initialization that made deep feedforward networks trainable without unsupervised pretraining.
raw_candidates.source_title: Understanding the Difficulty of Training Deep Feedforward Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Curriculum learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bengio et al.'s curriculum strategy is a same-lab training idea from 2009; RNNsearch's gains are architectural and do not rest on a curriculum.
raw_candidates.definition: Training strategy (Bengio, Louradour, Collobert & Weston, ICML 2009): presenting examples in a meaningful easy-to-hard order to speed and improve learning, formalized as a continuation method.
raw_candidates.source_title: Curriculum Learning

raw_candidates.name: Large-scale deep unsupervised learning using graphics processors (Raina et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPU deep learning demonstrations from 2009 made hundred-million-parameter training plausible; ambient infrastructure for the era, not a mechanism input to RNNsearch.
raw_candidates.definition: Demonstration (Raina, Madhavan & Ng, ICML 2009): DBNs and autoencoders trained on GPUs at 10–30x CPU speed, scaling deep unsupervised learning to a billion connections.
raw_candidates.source_title: Large-Scale Deep Unsupervised Learning Using Graphics Processors

raw_candidates.name: Moses: open source toolkit for statistical machine translation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Moses is the phrase-based baseline RNNsearch was benchmarked against and matched on no-unknown-word sentences — the incumbent, not an enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Toolkit (Koehn et al., ACL 2007 demos): the standard open-source phrase-based SMT pipeline (training, tuning, decoding) that defined the state of the art RNNsearch had to beat.
raw_candidates.source_title: Moses: Open Source Toolkit for Statistical Machine Translation

raw_candidates.name: Log-bilinear language model (Mnih & Hinton)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The log-bilinear model is an embedding-lineage relative of the neural LM tradition; RNNsearch's representations are learned inside an RNN encoder–decoder, not inherited from it.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Mnih & Hinton, NeurIPS 2007): a probabilistic language model scoring word sequences with bilinear interactions between distributed context representations.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Scalable Hierarchical Distributed Language Model

raw_candidates.name: CUDA parallel computing platform
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CUDA is the generic GPU substrate under all 2012–14 deep learning including the Montréal group's Theano code; a commodity input, not the leap's enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Platform (NVIDIA, 2007): general-purpose GPU programming that turned commodity graphics cards into the default deep-learning accelerator.
raw_candidates.source_title: CUDA: A Scalable Parallel Programming Model for Personal Supercomputing

raw_candidates.name: Europarl parallel corpus
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Europarl and the WMT'14 En–Fr collection (348M words) trained RNNsearch — but the identical corpus trained the fixed-vector baseline whose long-sentence failure is the paper's starting point, so the data is not the differentiator.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Koehn, EAMT 2005): sentence-aligned European Parliament proceedings in 11 languages, the foundational open parallel corpus for SMT and for the WMT shared tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Europarl: A Parallel Corpus for Statistical Machine Translation

raw_candidates.name: Bidirectional LSTM and dynamic time warping for phoneme classification (Graves & Schmidhuber)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BiLSTM instantiated the bidirectional idea with LSTM cells for sequence labeling; Bahdanau's encoder consumed the bidirectional-RNN architecture in its gated-unit (GRU) form, so BiLSTM's channel runs through the 1997 bidirectional formulation.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Graves & Schmidhuber, IJCNN 2005): bidirectional LSTM networks classifying phonemes frame-by-frame, establishing BiLSTM as a standard sequence-labeling architecture.
raw_candidates.source_title: Framewise Phoneme Classification with Bidirectional LSTM and Other Neural Network Architectures

raw_candidates.name: Hierarchical probabilistic neural network language model
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Morin & Bengio's hierarchical softmax made large-vocabulary neural LMs practical in the same lab; a vocabulary-scaling device, not part of RNNsearch's alignment mechanism.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Morin & Bengio, AISTATS 2005): organizing the vocabulary in a binary tree so neural language model inference costs log-vocabulary instead of vocabulary size.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Hierarchical Probabilistic Neural Network Language Model

raw_candidates.name: Pre-reordering for statistical machine translation (Collins et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Pre-reordering attacked SMT's word-order problem with parse-tree rules before translation; RNNsearch's learned soft alignment made such explicit reordering machinery unnecessary rather than building on it.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Collins, Koehn & Kucerova, ACL 2005): applying learned syntactic reordering rules to the source sentence before phrase-based translation, a standard fix for long-distance reordering.
raw_candidates.source_title: Clause Restructuring for Statistical Machine Translation

raw_candidates.name: Connectionist temporal classification
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CTC solved sequence transduction without pre-segmented alignment by marginalizing over blank-augmented paths — Graves' earlier alignment technology; Bahdanau's soft search is a different answer to the alignment problem and does not consume CTC.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Graves et al., ICML 2006): an RNN output layer that transduces between unaligned input and output sequences by summing over all valid alignments.
raw_candidates.source_title: Connectionist Temporal Classification: Labelling Unsegmented Sequence Data with Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Greedy layer-wise training of deep networks (deep belief nets)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Hinton et al.'s 2006 pretraining opened the deep-learning era, but by 2014 end-to-end backpropagation had displaced it; RNNsearch uses no layer-wise pretraining.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Hinton, Osindero & Teh, 2006): greedy layer-wise unsupervised pretraining of deep belief networks that made deep architectures trainable and launched modern deep learning.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Fast Learning Algorithm for Deep Belief Nets

raw_candidates.name: Workshop on Statistical Machine Translation (WMT)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: WMT supplied the shared task, data and BLEU yardstick for the En–Fr comparison; an institution that measured the leap, not a mechanism that enabled it.
raw_candidates.definition: Institution (Koehn & Monz, 2006–): the annual shared task and workshop whose standardized datasets and evaluations defined SMT progress, including WMT'14 English–French.
raw_candidates.source_title: Workshop on Statistical Machine Translation

raw_candidates.name: Phrase-based statistical machine translation (Koehn, Och & Marcu)
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Phrase-based SMT is the incumbent paradigm RNNsearch matched and began displacing; its alignment tables are the conceptual foil for learned soft alignment, not a consumed input.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Koehn, Och & Marcu, NAACL 2003): translation by segmenting the source into phrases, translating each from a learned phrase table, and reordering under a log-linear model.
raw_candidates.source_title: Statistical Phrase-Based Translation

raw_candidates.name: A systematic comparison of various statistical alignment models (Och & Ney)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Och & Ney systematized the IBM/HMM alignment models whose explicit word alignments Bahdanau's learned soft alignments are compared against in the paper's qualitative analysis — the classical alignment tradition, present as foil and vocabulary, not as mechanism.
raw_candidates.definition: Study (Och & Ney, Computational Linguistics 2003): the reference comparison of IBM Models 1–5 and the HMM alignment model, with the GIZA++ implementations that produced SMT's word alignments.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Systematic Comparison of Various Statistical Alignment Models

raw_candidates.name: Neural probabilistic language model
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bengio et al. founded neural language modeling with jointly learned word embeddings — the deep ancestor of every 2013–14 neural MT model, reaching Bahdanau only through the intervening RNNLM and encoder–decoder lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Bengio, Ducharme, Vincent & Jauvin, JMLR 2003): a feedforward network learning distributed word representations jointly with a probability model of word sequences, defeating the curse of dimensionality.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

raw_candidates.name: Minimum error rate training for SMT (Och)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MERT tuned the log-linear weights of the phrase-based baselines RNNsearch was compared against; part of the incumbent's machinery, not of the new model.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Och, ACL 2003): directly optimizing SMT feature weights against BLEU on a development set, the standard tuning procedure of the phrase-based era.
raw_candidates.source_title: Minimum Error Rate Training in Statistical Machine Translation

raw_candidates.name: BLEU: a method for automatic evaluation of machine translation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BLEU is the metric in which RNNsearch's improvement was stated (26.75 vs 17.82); measurement of the leap, not an enabler of it.
raw_candidates.definition: Metric (Papineni et al., ACL 2002): n-gram precision against reference translations with a brevity penalty, the standard automatic MT evaluation for two decades.
raw_candidates.source_title: BLEU: A Method for Automatic Evaluation of Machine Translation

raw_candidates.name: Learning to forget: continual prediction with LSTM (forget gate)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The forget gate completed the LSTM cell; Bahdanau's units were GRUs, so any forget-gate influence arrives through the gated-unit lineage whose proximate form is the coeval GRU.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Gers, Schmidhuber & Cummins, Neural Computation 2000): adding a forget gate to LSTM so continual streams can be reset, the final piece of the modern LSTM cell.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to Forget: Continual Prediction with LSTM

raw_candidates.name: Saliency-based visual attention (Itti, Koch & Niebur)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The saliency map is the classical computational model of bottom-up attention in vision; a conceptual relative with no channel into a 2014 translation model.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Itti, Koch & Niebur, IEEE TPAMI 2001): a biologically inspired system computing a topographic saliency map from multi-scale image features to guide covert visual attention.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Model of Saliency-Based Visual Attention for Rapid Scene Analysis

raw_candidates.name: Bidirectional recurrent neural networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bahdanau et al.'s encoder IS a bidirectional RNN: each annotation h_j concatenates the forward and backward hidden states around source word j, so the soft search attends over exactly the representations this 1997 architecture produces.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Schuster & Paliwal, IEEE Trans. Signal Processing 1997): two recurrent layers processing a sequence in opposite directions so each position's representation summarizes both past and future context.
raw_candidates.source_title: Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Long short-term memory (LSTM)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LSTM founded the gated recurrent unit family, but Bahdanau et al.'s encoder and decoder ran on Cho et al.'s GRU, so LSTM's influence on RNNsearch is mediated by the gated unit's proximate 2014 form.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, Neural Computation 1997): recurrent units with a constant-error carousel and multiplicative gates that learn long-term dependencies plain RNNs cannot.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long Short-Term Memory

raw_candidates.name: HMM-based word alignment model (Vogel, Ney & Tillmann)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The HMM alignment model made word alignment a first-order Markov process inside SMT; part of the classical alignment tradition Bahdanau's learned alignments supersede, not a mechanism it consumes.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Vogel, Ney & Tillmann, COLING 1996): word alignment in SMT as a hidden Markov model, improving on IBM Model 2 by modeling alignment positions as dependent on previous alignments.
raw_candidates.source_title: HMM-Based Word Alignment in Statistical Translation

raw_candidates.name: Biased competition theory of attention (Desimone & Duncan)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Biased competition framed attention as competition among representations resolved by top-down bias — a neuroscience framing with no computational channel into RNNsearch.
raw_candidates.definition: Theory (Desimone & Duncan, Annual Review of Neuroscience 1995): visual attention as biased competition between objects in the visual system, resolved by working-memory templates.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Mechanisms of Selective Visual Attention

raw_candidates.name: Learning long-term dependencies with gradient descent is difficult (Bengio et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: This analysis named the vanishing-gradient obstacle that gated units were invented to circumvent; its channel into Bahdanau runs through the LSTM-to-GRU gated-unit lineage it motivated.
raw_candidates.definition: Analysis (Bengio, Simard & Frasconi, IEEE Trans. Neural Networks 1994): dynamical-systems proof that gradient descent on recurrent networks faces a fundamental trade-off between robustness and long-term dependency learning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning Long-Term Dependencies with Gradient Descent is Difficult

raw_candidates.name: IBM Models of statistical machine translation (Brown et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: IBM Models 1–5 founded statistical MT and made 'alignment' a latent variable estimated by EM — the concept Bahdanau's alignment model inherits its name and problem from, while replacing the machinery wholesale with a differentiable network.
raw_candidates.definition: Model family (Brown, Della Pietra, Della Pietra & Mercer, Computational Linguistics 1993): five generative models of translation in which word alignment is a hidden variable, founding statistical machine translation.
raw_candidates.source_title: The Mathematics of Statistical Machine Translation: Parameter Estimation

raw_candidates.name: A program for aligning sentences in bilingual corpora (Gale & Church)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Sentence alignment made parallel corpora usable at scale — data plumbing two decades upstream of RNNsearch, shared by every SMT system of the era.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Gale & Church, Computational Linguistics 1993): aligning sentences in parallel texts by length statistics, the standard first step in building the bilingual corpora SMT trains on.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Program for Aligning Sentences in Bilingual Corpora

raw_candidates.name: A theory of visual attention (Bundesen's TVA)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: TVA formalized attentional selection and weighting mathematically in psychology; a formal relative of attention weighting with no channel into neural MT.
raw_candidates.definition: Theory (Bundesen, Psychological Review 1990): a computational account of visual attention in which elements compete for representation with attentional weights determined by pertinence and bias.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Theory of Visual Attention

raw_candidates.name: Finding structure in time (Elman recurrent network)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Elman's simple recurrent network founded the RNN family Bahdanau's encoder belongs to; the influence is mediated by two decades of recurrent architecture development, proximately by the gated bidirectional encoder actually used.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Elman, Cognitive Science 1990): a recurrent network whose context layer copies hidden states, letting it discover temporal structure such as word categories from prediction alone.
raw_candidates.source_title: Finding Structure in Time

raw_candidates.name: Probabilistic interpretation of feedforward networks (softmax, Bridle)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The softmax that turns Bahdanau's alignment scores into weights descends from Bridle's probabilistic reading of network outputs; a generic mathematical primitive used everywhere, not the leap's specific enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Formulation (Bridle, 1990): interpreting feedforward network outputs via the softmax as posterior class probabilities, the normalization that later turns attention scores into weights.
raw_candidates.source_title: Probabilistic Interpretation of Feedforward Classification Network Outputs

raw_candidates.name: A tutorial on hidden Markov models (Rabiner)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Rabiner's tutorial canonized HMMs, the sequence-alignment machinery of the speech era from which SMT alignment models descend; two removes from RNNsearch.
raw_candidates.definition: Synthesis (Rabiner, Proceedings of the IEEE 1989): the canonical exposition of hidden Markov models and their forward-backward, Viterbi and Baum–Welch algorithms for speech recognition.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Tutorial on Hidden Markov Models and Selected Applications in Speech Recognition

raw_candidates.name: A statistical approach to machine translation (Brown et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The 1990 Candide paper proposed translation as a noisy-channel statistical problem; its influence on Bahdanau is entirely mediated by the IBM Models and the SMT tradition it founded.
raw_candidates.definition: Proposal (Brown, Cocke, Della Pietra et al., Computational Linguistics 1990): machine translation by statistical parameter estimation from parallel corpora, the founding document of SMT.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Statistical Approach to Machine Translation

raw_candidates.name: Sequential network construction (Jordan recurrent network)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Jordan's output-feedback recurrent network is the other founding RNN design; its lineage into Bahdanau runs through Elman's formulation and the recurrent architectures that followed.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Jordan, 1986): a recurrent network feeding its outputs back as inputs through decaying state units, designed for learning sequences of actions.
raw_candidates.source_title: Serial Order: A Parallel Distributed Processing Approach

raw_candidates.name: Learning representations by back-propagating errors
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Backpropagation is the generic training algorithm for every network in this graph, RNNsearch included; the universal substrate, not a proximate enabler of the alignment leap.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, Nature 1986): gradient descent through layered networks via the chain rule, making multilayer representation learning practical.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning Representations by Back-Propagating Errors

raw_candidates.name: Feature integration theory of attention (Treisman & Gelade)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Feature integration theory founded the psychology of attention that the field's vocabulary echoes; no computational channel into a 2014 neural MT model exists.
raw_candidates.definition: Theory (Treisman & Gelade, Cognitive Psychology 1980): visual attention as the serial spotlight that binds separately registered features into coherent objects.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Feature-Integration Theory of Attention

raw_candidates.name: Dynamic time warping for speech recognition (Sakoe & Chiba)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: DTW aligned speech signals to templates by dynamic programming — the classical alignment technology of the pre-statistical era, a conceptual ancestor of alignment with no channel into RNNsearch.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Sakoe & Chiba, IEEE Trans. ASSP 1978): aligning two time series of different speeds by dynamic programming, the standard speech-recognition alignment technique of its era.
raw_candidates.source_title: Dynamic Programming Algorithm Optimization for Spoken Word Recognition

raw_candidates.name: Maximum likelihood from incomplete data via the EM algorithm
raw_candidates.causal_claim: EM is the estimation engine of the IBM alignment models; any influence on Bahdanau is mediated by that SMT alignment tradition, and RNNsearch itself is trained by backpropagation, not EM.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Dempster, Laird & Rubin, JRSS-B 1977): iterative maximum-likelihood estimation with latent variables, the algorithm that trained HMMs and IBM alignment models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Maximum Likelihood from Incomplete Data via the EM Algorithm

raw_candidates.name: Selective attention and the cocktail party problem (Cherry; Broadbent filter model)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Cherry's dichotic-listening experiments founded the scientific study of selective attention; the shared word is where the connection ends — no channel into neural machine translation.
raw_candidates.definition: Finding and theory (Cherry, JASA 1953; Broadbent, 1958): listeners can shadow one of two simultaneous speech streams, founding selective-attention research and the filter model of attention.
raw_candidates.source_title: Some Experiments on the Recognition of Speech, with One and with Two Ears

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Forcada & Ñeco proposed an RNN encoder–decoder for translation in 1997 — the architecture in embryo, seventeen years early and without the training scale or gated units to work; a forgotten anticipation, not a consumed input.
raw_candidates.definition: Proposal (Forcada & Ñeco, 1997): recursive hetero-associative memories — recurrent encoder and decoder networks — for translating short sentences, an early encoder–decoder MT design that went largely uncited by the 2014 revival.
raw_candidates.name: Recursive hetero-associative memories for translation (Forcada & Ñeco)
raw_candidates.source_title: Recursive Hetero-Associative Memories for Translation

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The 2012 ASR consensus paper certified deep networks as production-grade sequence models; ambient evidence for the era's neural turn, no mechanism channel into RNNsearch.
raw_candidates.definition: Consensus account (Hinton et al., IEEE Signal Processing Magazine 2012): deep neural networks replacing GMMs in hybrid HMM speech recognizers across four industrial labs.
raw_candidates.name: Deep neural networks for acoustic modeling in speech recognition
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Neural Networks for Acoustic Modeling in Speech Recognition

raw_candidates.causal_claim: DistBelief is Google's distributed training stack, part of seq2seq's home infrastructure; the Montréal group's models trained on Theano clusters, not DistBelief.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Dean et al., NeurIPS 2012): Google's framework for training very large neural networks across thousands of machines with model and data parallelism.
raw_candidates.name: Large-scale distributed deep networks (DistBelief)
raw_candidates.source_title: Large Scale Distributed Deep Networks

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Sutskever et al.'s initialization-and-momentum study is Google-side training craft from seq2seq's first author; RNNsearch's training recipe (Adadelta) does not descend from it.
raw_candidates.definition: Study (Sutskever, Martens, Dahl & Hinton, ICML 2013): careful initialization plus classical momentum lets SGD rival Hessian-free optimization on deep and recurrent networks.
raw_candidates.name: On the importance of initialization and momentum in deep learning
raw_candidates.source_title: On the Importance of Initialization and Momentum in Deep Learning

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Martens & Sutskever showed RNNs could be trained on long-dependency problems with second-order methods; RNNsearch trained by first-order Adadelta, so the channel is thematic, not consumed.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Martens & Sutskever, ICML 2011): Hessian-free optimization training recurrent networks to solve long-term dependency tasks previously considered untrainable.
raw_candidates.name: Learning recurrent neural networks with Hessian-free optimization
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning Recurrent Neural Networks with Hessian-Free Optimization

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Sutskever, Martens & Hinton's character-level generation is the Google lineage's prior step toward seq2seq; for Bahdanau it is a parallel lab's work with no consumed channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Sutskever, Martens & Hinton, ICML 2011): a multilayer RNN with multiplicative connections generating coherent character-level text, an early demonstration of neural sequence generation.
raw_candidates.name: Generating text with multilayer recurrent neural networks
raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Text with Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Graves' RNN transducer maps input to output sequences of different lengths with a joint network — the closest pre-2014 transduction formulation; Bahdanau's encoder–decoder with soft search is a different decomposition and does not consume the transducer's blank-free alignment lattice.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Graves, 2012): a transcription network and prediction network combined to transduce between unaligned sequences, generalizing CTC to output sequences.
raw_candidates.name: Sequence transduction with recurrent neural networks (RNN transducer)
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence Transduction with Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The Google Brain 'cat neuron' system demonstrated thousand-machine unsupervised deep learning; scale-culture context for seq2seq's lab, no mechanism channel into the Montréal model.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Le et al., ICML 2012): a 1-billion-parameter network trained on unlabeled YouTube frames across 16,000 cores that learned face- and cat-selective neurons.
raw_candidates.name: Building high-level features using large-scale unsupervised learning
raw_candidates.source_title: Building High-Level Features Using Large Scale Unsupervised Learning

raw_candidates.causal_claim: CRFs were the discriminative sequence-labeling standard of the 2000s; a neighboring paradigm for structured prediction, not an input to end-to-end neural MT.
raw_candidates.definition: Model family (Lafferty, McCallum & Pereira, ICML 2001): discriminative undirected graphical models for labeling sequences, fixing label bias in HMM-style models.
raw_candidates.name: Conditional random fields
raw_candidates.source_title: Conditional Random Fields: Probabilistic Models for Segmenting and Labeling Sequence Data

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Berger et al.'s maximum-entropy framework became SMT's log-linear combination of feature scores — the incumbent's mathematics, displaced rather than consumed by end-to-end neural models.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Berger, Della Pietra & Della Pietra, Computational Linguistics 1996): exponential (log-linear) models combining arbitrary features, the modeling form of phrase-based SMT systems.
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.name: A maximum entropy approach to natural language processing (log-linear models)
raw_candidates.source_title: A Maximum Entropy Approach to Natural Language Processing

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Viterbi decoding is the dynamic-programming backbone of the HMM era; RNNsearch decodes by beam search over a neural distribution, inheriting the search idea only at several removes.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Viterbi, IEEE Trans. Information Theory 1967): dynamic-programming decoding of convolutional codes and, by extension, most-likely state paths in hidden Markov models.
raw_candidates.name: The Viterbi algorithm
raw_candidates.source_title: Error Bounds for Convolutional Codes and an Asymptotically Optimum Decoding Algorithm

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Beam search is the decoding heuristic RNNsearch used (beam width 12 in the long-trained model) — a generic search standard inherited from 1970s speech systems, substitutable and not specific to the alignment leap.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Lowerre, 1976, HARPY system): breadth-limited heuristic search keeping only the best partial hypotheses, the standard decoder for speech and later neural sequence models.
raw_candidates.name: Beam search decoding for speech recognition (Lowerre)
raw_candidates.source_title: The HARPY Speech Recognition System

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Martens' Hessian-free result proved very deep networks trainable by second-order methods; a Toronto training-craft landmark with no channel into Montréal's first-order RNNsearch recipe.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Martens, ICML 2010): Hessian-free optimization training deep autoencoders and RNNs that first-order methods of the time could not.
raw_candidates.name: Deep learning via Hessian-free optimization
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Learning via Hessian-Free Optimization

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Collobert et al.'s unified network showed jointly learned embeddings could serve many NLP tasks at once; part of the embedding-era backdrop, not an input to RNNsearch.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Collobert et al., JMLR 2011): a single convolutional neural architecture with embeddings learned from raw text performing POS tagging, chunking, NER and SRL near state of the art.
raw_candidates.name: Natural language processing (almost) from scratch (SENNA)
raw_candidates.source_title: Natural Language Processing (Almost) from Scratch

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Adagrad founded the adaptive-optimizer family Adadelta belongs to; the family resemblance runs through the optimizer Bahdanau actually used, making Adagrad at best a mediated relative.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Duchi, Hazan & Singer, JMLR 2011): per-coordinate adaptive learning rates from accumulated squared gradients, the ancestor of Adadelta, RMSProp and Adam.
raw_candidates.name: Adaptive subgradient methods for online learning (Adagrad)
raw_candidates.source_title: Adaptive Subgradient Methods for Online Learning and Stochastic Optimization

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Glorot et al.'s rectifier study is Montréal training craft of the era; RNNsearch's recurrent units are tanh/gated, so rectifiers are not part of its mechanism.
raw_candidates.definition: Study (Glorot, Bordes & Bengio, AISTATS 2011): rectified linear units enabling supervised training of very deep networks without unsupervised pretraining.
raw_candidates.name: Deep sparse rectifier neural networks
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Sparse Rectifier Neural Networks

raw_candidates.causal_claim: NCE made unnormalized models (including neural LMs) trainable by classification against noise; a vocabulary-scaling technique in the extended family, not part of RNNsearch's training as published.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Gutmann & Hyvärinen, AISTATS 2010): estimating unnormalized statistical models by discriminating data from known noise, later used to train word embeddings and neural LMs.
raw_candidates.name: Noise-contrastive estimation
raw_candidates.source_title: Noise-Contrastive Estimation: A New Estimation Principle for Unnormalized Statistical Models

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Hierarchical phrase-based SMT learned synchronous grammar rules for reordering — the incumbent's most sophisticated answer to the reordering problem that learned soft alignment dissolved; displaced, not consumed.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Chiang, Computational Linguistics 2007): phrase-based translation with automatically learned hierarchical rules (a weighted synchronous CFG), the strongest SMT variant of its era.
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.name: Hierarchical phrase-based translation (Chiang)
raw_candidates.source_title: Hierarchical Phrase-Based Translation

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Yamada & Knight's tree-to-string model was SMT's syntax turn; part of the incumbent tradition RNNsearch bypassed with learned continuous representations.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Yamada & Knight, ACL 2001): translation as probabilistic operations over parse trees, founding syntax-based statistical machine translation.
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.name: A syntax-based statistical translation model (Yamada & Knight)
raw_candidates.source_title: A Syntax-Based Statistical Translation Model

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Schwenk's CSLM put neural language models inside production SMT and ASR years before NMT; its lineage into Bahdanau runs through Schwenk's continuous-space translation models and the Cho et al. collaboration, not directly.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Schwenk, Computer Speech & Language 2007): feedforward neural language models with continuous word representations integrated into large-vocabulary speech recognition and SMT systems.
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.name: Continuous space language models (Schwenk)
raw_candidates.source_title: Continuous Space Language Models

raw_candidates.causal_claim: NETtalk was the 1980s demonstration that a network could learn text-to-speech mappings from examples; a cultural ancestor of neural sequence learning with no mechanism channel into 2014 MT.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Sejnowski & Rosenberg, 1987): a backpropagation network learning to pronounce English text, the era's emblematic demonstration of learned sequence transduction.
raw_candidates.name: NETtalk: parallel networks that learn to read aloud
raw_candidates.source_title: Parallel Networks That Learn to Read Aloud

raw_candidates.causal_claim: TDNNs introduced weight-shared temporal convolution for speech; an early sequence architecture whose lineage into RNNsearch is generic deep-learning ancestry.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Waibel, Hanazawa, Hinton, Shikano & Lang, IEEE Trans. ASSP 1989): neural networks with time-shifted weight sharing recognizing phonemes regardless of position.
raw_candidates.name: Time-delay neural network for phoneme recognition (Waibel et al.)
raw_candidates.source_title: Phoneme Recognition Using Time-Delay Neural Networks

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Posner's cueing paradigm operationalized covert attention shifts in psychology experiments; shared vocabulary only, no channel into neural MT.
raw_candidates.definition: Paradigm and theory (Posner, Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology 1980): measuring covert shifts of visual attention with spatial cues, founding the experimental study of attentional orienting.
raw_candidates.name: Orienting of attention: spatial cueing paradigm (Posner)
raw_candidates.source_title: Orienting of Attention

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Torch7 was the NYU/IDIAP Lua deep-learning framework; the Montréal group worked in Theano, so Torch is a parallel toolkit, not the substrate of RNNsearch.
raw_candidates.definition: Software system (Collobert, Kavukcuoglu & Farabet, 2011): a LuaJIT-based scientific computing framework that became a major deep-learning research platform.
raw_candidates.name: Torch7: a Matlab-like environment for machine learning
raw_candidates.source_title: Torch7: A Matlab-like Environment for Machine Learning

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Chorowski, Bahdanau et al. applied the new attention mechanism to speech within months — a child of RNNsearch (December 2014), not a parent; included to mark the boundary.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Chorowski, Bahdanau, Serdyuk, Cho & Bengio, 2014): attention-based encoder–decoder for large-vocabulary speech recognition, the first transfer of Bahdanau attention to audio.
raw_candidates.name: Attention-based models for speech recognition (Chorowski et al.)
raw_candidates.source_title: Attention-Based Models for Speech Recognition

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Vinyals et al.'s caption generator (November 2014) is a coeval child of the encoder–decoder wave; its attention extension came in 2015, after and from Bahdanau.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Vinyals, Toshev, Bengio & Erhan, 2014): a CNN encoder and LSTM decoder generating image captions end-to-end, transferring the seq2seq template to vision.
raw_candidates.name: Show and Tell: a neural image caption generator
raw_candidates.source_title: Show and Tell: A Neural Image Caption Generator

raw_candidates.causal_claim: cuDNN shipped in 2014 as NVIDIA's deep-learning primitives library; RNNsearch's Theano implementation predates any dependence on it.
raw_candidates.definition: Library (Chetlur et al., 2014): GPU-accelerated primitives (convolution, pooling, normalization) that became the standard backend of deep-learning frameworks.
raw_candidates.name: cuDNN: efficient primitives for deep learning
raw_candidates.source_title: cuDNN: Efficient Primitives for Deep Learning

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coates et al. showed commodity GPU clusters could train billion-parameter networks; part of the era's scale infrastructure story, centered at Stanford/Google rather than Montréal.
raw_candidates.definition: Demonstration (Coates et al., ICML 2013): training deep networks with billions of parameters on 16 commodity GPU servers using model parallelism.
raw_candidates.name: Deep learning with COTS high-performance computing (Coates et al.)
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Learning with COTS High-Performance Computing

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Cireșan et al.'s GPU MLPs reset MNIST records in 2010 and helped restart the deep-learning wave; ambient evidence, no channel into RNNsearch.
raw_candidates.definition: Demonstration (Cireșan, Meier, Gambardella & Schmidhuber, Neural Computation 2010): plain deep MLPs on GPUs reaching 0.35% MNIST error, reviving supervised deep learning.
raw_candidates.name: Deep, big, simple neural nets for handwritten digit recognition (Cireșan et al.)
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Big Simple Neural Nets for Handwritten Digit Recognition

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Shannon's information theory underlies the noisy-channel framing of SMT; its distance from RNNsearch is the whole history of the field — ancestry, not enablement.
raw_candidates.definition: Theory (Shannon, Bell System Technical Journal 1948): the mathematical foundation of information, entropy and channel coding from which the noisy-channel model of translation descends.
raw_candidates.name: A mathematical theory of communication (Shannon)
raw_candidates.source_title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Weaver's 1949 memo proposed treating translation as a cryptographic/statistical problem — the founding vision of MT, separated from RNNsearch by 65 years of intervening milestones.
raw_candidates.definition: Memorandum (Weaver, 1949): the Rockefeller Foundation memo proposing computers translate language using cryptography, information theory and statistical semantics — the founding document of machine translation research.
raw_candidates.name: Weaver memorandum: Translation
raw_candidates.source_title: Translation (Weaver Memorandum)

candidate.name: Generating sequences with recurrent neural networks (Graves soft window)
candidate.causal_claim: Graves built the first working differentiable alignment in sequence transduction — a soft Gaussian window the network slides over an input text so it learns which characters it is writing; Bahdanau et al. explicitly discuss it and generalize it into content-based soft search over encoder annotations, freed from the monotonic window.
candidate.definition: Model and mechanism (Graves, 2013): deep LSTM sequence generation whose handwriting-synthesis network conditions on a text through a differentiable soft window (mixture of Gaussians) that learns the alignment between characters and pen strokes.
