candidate.name: Recurrent continuous translation models
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Kalchbrenner & Blunsom founded the neural MT attempt and are named in Bahdanau et al.'s introduction as proposers of NMT; but the template Bahdanau extended was Cho et al.'s encoder–decoder, through which any RCTM influence is mediated.
candidate.definition: Model class (Kalchbrenner & Blunsom, EMNLP 2013): translation probabilities computed purely from continuous representations, with a recurrent target language model conditioned on a convolutional source-sentence model.

candidate.name: Joint language and translation modeling with recurrent neural networks
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Auli et al.'s RNN joint model rescored SMT lattices with source-conditioned recurrent predictions; RNNsearch is an end-to-end architecture that does not consume lattice rescoring.
candidate.definition: Model (Auli, Galley, Quirk & Zweig, EMNLP 2013): an RNN language model augmented with a continuous representation of the source sentence, used to rescore phrase-based SMT output lattices for about 1.1 BLEU.

candidate.name: On the difficulty of training recurrent neural networks (gradient clipping)
candidate.causal_claim: Pascanu et al. analyzed exploding gradients and proposed norm clipping, part of the standard RNN training toolkit of the Montréal group; a training aid, not the alignment mechanism.
candidate.definition: Analysis and recipe (Pascanu, Mikolov & Bengio, ICML 2013): a dynamical-systems account of vanishing/exploding gradients in RNNs and the gradient-norm clipping heuristic that made deep RNN training routine.

candidate.name: word2vec

candidate.name: Continuous space translation models for phrase-based SMT
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Schwenk's feedforward continuous-space translation model estimated phrase-pair probabilities inside SMT; it belongs to the pipeline tradition RNNsearch replaced, and Schwenk's channel into Bahdanau runs through his co-authorship of Cho et al. 2014.
candidate.definition: Model (Schwenk, COLING 2012): a feedforward neural network with bag-of-words phrase representations directly estimating translation probabilities for phrase-based SMT, able to score unseen phrase pairs.

candidate.name: Learning where to attend with deep architectures for image tracking
candidate.causal_claim: Denil et al. learned fixation policies for image tracking with deep architectures — attention as sequential selection in vision, cited by later surveys as same-spirit prior work, with no documented channel into the Montréal MT model.
candidate.definition: Model (Denil, Bazzani, Larochelle & de Freitas, Neural Computation 2012): deep architectures that learn where to fixate in an image for tracking, an early neural attention system.

candidate.causal_claim: Adadelta is the optimizer Bahdanau et al. actually used to train RNNsearch; a substitutable training component rather than the mechanism of the leap.

candidate.causal_claim: AlexNet's 2012 rout made deep networks the default bet across ML and is the ambient credibility wave behind the 2013–14 neural MT attempts; it contributes no mechanism to RNNsearch.

candidate.definition: Demonstration (Cireșan, Meier, Gambardella & Schmidhuber, Neural Computation 2010): plain deep MLPs on GPUs reaching 0.35% MNIST error, reviving supervised deep learning.

candidate.causal_claim: Shannon's information theory underlies the noisy-channel framing of SMT; its distance from RNNsearch is the whole history of the field — ancestry, not enablement.
candidate.definition: Theory (Shannon, Bell System Technical Journal 1948): the mathematical foundation of information, entropy and channel coding from which the noisy-channel model of translation descends.
candidate.name: A mathematical theory of communication (Shannon)

candidate.causal_claim: Weaver's 1949 memo proposed treating translation as a cryptographic/statistical problem — the founding vision of MT, separated from RNNsearch by 65 years of intervening milestones.
candidate.definition: Memorandum (Weaver, 1949): the Rockefeller Foundation memo proposing computers translate language using cryptography, information theory and statistical semantics — the founding document of machine translation research.
candidate.name: Weaver memorandum: Translation
candidate.source_title: Translation (Weaver Memorandum)

card.name: Hierarchical probabilistic neural network language model
card.definition: Method (Morin & Bengio, AISTATS 2005): organizing the vocabulary in a binary tree so neural language model inference costs log-vocabulary instead of vocabulary size.

card.name: Neural probabilistic language model
card.definition: Model (Bengio, Ducharme, Vincent & Jauvin, JMLR 2003): a feedforward network learning distributed word representations jointly with a probability model of word sequences, defeating the curse of dimensionality.

card.name: A systematic comparison of various statistical alignment models (Och & Ney)
card.definition: Study (Och & Ney, Computational Linguistics 2003): the reference comparison of IBM Models 1–5 and the HMM alignment model, with the GIZA++ implementations that produced SMT's word alignments.

card.name: HMM-based word alignment model (Vogel, Ney & Tillmann)
card.definition: Model (Vogel, Ney & Tillmann, COLING 1996): word alignment in SMT as a hidden Markov model, improving on IBM Model 2 by modeling alignment positions as dependent on previous alignments.

candidate.name: RNN Encoder–Decoder (Cho et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: Bahdanau et al. directly extended Cho et al.'s RNN Encoder–Decoder: same lab, same gated unit, and the fixed-length summary vector c is exactly what the alignment model replaces.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Cho et al., EMNLP 2014): two RNNs jointly trained to map a variable-length source sequence to a fixed-length vector and decode a target sequence from it; introduced the gated recurrent unit (GRU).
candidate.source_title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder–Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation

candidate.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
candidate.causal_claim: Sutskever et al.'s deep-LSTM encoder–decoder is the other fixed-vector template Bahdanau et al. name as a proposer of NMT and set out to fix.
candidate.definition: Method (Sutskever et al., 2014): a multilayer LSTM reads a source sequence into a fixed-length vector and a second LSTM decodes the target, with source reversal easing optimization.
candidate.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

candidate.name: Gated recurrent unit (GRU)
candidate.causal_claim: Bahdanau et al. reused Cho et al.'s gated hidden unit (reset and update gates) verbatim in both encoder and decoder of RNNsearch.
candidate.definition: Recurrent unit (Cho et al., 2014) with reset and update gates that adaptively capture dependencies at multiple time scales, simpler than LSTM.
candidate.source_title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder–Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation

candidate.name: On the Properties of Neural Machine Translation: Encoder–Decoder Approaches
candidate.causal_claim: This analysis by Cho, van Merriënboer, Bahdanau and Bengio documented that basic encoder–decoder quality deteriorates rapidly as sentence length grows — the documented bottleneck Bahdanau et al. cite as their motivation.
candidate.definition: Empirical study (SSST-8, 2014) showing fixed-vector encoder–decoder translation quality collapses with sentence length and unknown-word count.
candidate.source_title: On the Properties of Neural Machine Translation: Encoder-Decoder Approaches

candidate.name: Recurrent models of visual attention
candidate.causal_claim: Mnih et al.'s RAM showed an RNN could learn where to look next via REINFORCE in the same season — the hard-attention sibling of Bahdanau's soft alignment, not an input to it.
candidate.definition: Model (Mnih et al., 2014) that processes an image through a sequence of stochastically chosen glimpses, trained with reinforcement learning (hard attention).
candidate.source_title: Recurrent Models of Visual Attention

candidate.name: Neural Turing Machines
candidate.causal_claim: Graves et al.'s content-based addressing over an external memory is a parallel differentiable-attention design from the same autumn; no channel into RNNsearch is documented.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Graves, Wayne & Danihelka, 2014) coupling a neural controller to an external memory matrix via soft content- and location-based addressing.
candidate.source_title: Neural Turing Machines

candidate.name: Memory Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Weston et al.'s memory-augmented QA model is a coeval attention-adjacent design; it addresses a different task and was not consumed by the Montréal MT group.
candidate.definition: Model class (Weston, Chopra & Bordes, 2014) pairing a long-term memory component with learned read/write and reasoning over stored facts for question answering.
candidate.source_title: Memory Networks

candidate.name: Multiple object recognition with visual attention
candidate.causal_claim: Ba, Mnih & Kavukcuoglu's sequential glimpse model is another coeval hard-attention system; parallel work, no documented input into RNNsearch.
candidate.definition: Model (Ba, Mnih & Kavukcuoglu, 2014) recognizing multiple objects by a recurrent controller that steers a retina-like sensor over an image.
candidate.source_title: Multiple Object Recognition with Visual Attention

candidate.name: Fast and robust neural network joint models for statistical machine translation
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Devlin et al.'s feedforward joint model was the strongest neural component inside 2014 SMT pipelines; RNNsearch replaced the whole pipeline rather than consuming it.
candidate.definition: Model (Devlin et al., ACL 2014): a feedforward neural joint source-target language model integrated into phrase-based SMT, worth about 1 BLEU.
candidate.source_title: Fast and Robust Neural Network Joint Models for Statistical Machine Translation

candidate.name: Multilingual models for compositional distributed semantics
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Hermann & Blunsom's language-specific encoders, compared in Bahdanau et al.'s introduction, are a parallel 2014 encoder design the paper positions against, not one it builds on.
candidate.definition: Models (Hermann & Blunsom, ACL 2014) learning sentence representations in two languages with separate encoders whose outputs are compared for semantic equivalence.
candidate.source_title: Multilingual Models for Compositional Distributed Semantics

candidate.name: A convolutional neural network for modelling sentences
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Kalchbrenner et al.'s dynamic CNN sentence model is a coeval alternative sentence encoder; RNNsearch's encoder is recurrent, not convolutional.
candidate.definition: Model (Kalchbrenner, Grefenstette & Blunsom, ACL 2014): a convolutional network with dynamic k-max pooling producing sentence representations for classification tasks.
candidate.source_title: A Convolutional Neural Network for Modelling Sentences

candidate.name: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
candidate.causal_claim: GloVe is a coeval embedding method; RNNsearch trained its word representations jointly from scratch and did not consume pretrained vectors.
candidate.definition: Method (Pennington, Socher & Manning, 2014) factoring a global word co-occurrence matrix to produce word vectors with linear semantic structure.
candidate.source_title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

candidate.name: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
candidate.causal_claim: Adam appeared in December 2014, after RNNsearch was posted; Bahdanau et al. trained with Adadelta, so no channel exists.
candidate.definition: Optimizer (Kingma & Ba, 2014) combining per-parameter adaptive learning rates with bias-corrected moment estimates; became the default deep-learning optimizer.
candidate.source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

candidate.causal_claim: Chorowski, Bahdanau et al. applied the new attention mechanism to speech within months — a child of RNNsearch (December 2014), not a parent; included to mark the boundary.
candidate.definition: Model (Chorowski, Bahdanau, Serdyuk, Cho & Bengio, 2014): attention-based encoder–decoder for large-vocabulary speech recognition, the first transfer of Bahdanau attention to audio.
candidate.name: Attention-based models for speech recognition (Chorowski et al.)
candidate.source_title: Attention-Based Models for Speech Recognition

candidate.causal_claim: Vinyals et al.'s caption generator (November 2014) is a coeval child of the encoder–decoder wave; its attention extension came in 2015, after and from Bahdanau.
candidate.definition: System (Vinyals, Toshev, Bengio & Erhan, 2014): a CNN encoder and LSTM decoder generating image captions end-to-end, transferring the seq2seq template to vision.
candidate.name: Show and Tell: a neural image caption generator
candidate.source_title: Show and Tell: A Neural Image Caption Generator

candidate.causal_claim: cuDNN shipped in 2014 as NVIDIA's deep-learning primitives library; RNNsearch's Theano implementation predates any dependence on it.
candidate.definition: Library (Chetlur et al., 2014): GPU-accelerated primitives (convolution, pooling, normalization) that became the standard backend of deep-learning frameworks.
candidate.name: cuDNN: efficient primitives for deep learning
candidate.source_title: cuDNN: Efficient Primitives for Deep Learning

card.name: Neural probabilistic language model
card.definition: Model (Bengio, Ducharme, Vincent & Jauvin, JMLR 2003): a feedforward network learning distributed word representations jointly with a probability model of word sequences, defeating the curse of dimensionality.

raw_candidates.name: Long short-term memory (LSTM)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LSTM directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by being the consumed cell of both its encoder and decoder: Sutskever et al. built the whole model from multilayer LSTMs, citing LSTM's ability to learn long-range temporal dependencies as the reason for the choice.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long short-term memory (Wikipedia)
raw_candidates.definition: Gated recurrent unit (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) whose constant error carousel carries information and gradients across long time lags without vanishing.

raw_candidates.name: Recurrent neural network language model (Mikolov)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The RNN language model directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by supplying its decoder: the paper defines the decoder as 'essentially a recurrent neural network language model except that it is conditioned on the input sequence', citing Mikolov's RNNLM line.
raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Text with Recurrent Neural Networks (Sutskever et al. 2011)
raw_candidates.definition: A recurrent network trained to predict the next word from the previous words (Mikolov et al., 2010), which made variable-length conditional text generation a trainable objective.

raw_candidates.name: RNN Encoder-Decoder (Cho et al.)
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The RNN Encoder-Decoder directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by publishing the two-RNN encode-to-fixed-vector / decode-from-vector template months earlier; Sutskever et al. scaled the same template from phrase scoring inside SMT to standalone sentence translation with deep LSTMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Cho et al., arXiv June 2014) of two jointly trained RNNs, one encoding a variable-length sequence into a fixed vector and one decoding it back, introduced with the GRU unit.

raw_candidates.name: Recurrent continuous translation models (Kalchbrenner & Blunsom)
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Recurrent continuous translation models directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by demonstrating a recurrent encoder (convolutional) feeding a recurrent decoder for translation a year earlier, the closest published template for end-to-end recurrent transduction.
raw_candidates.source_title: Encoding Source Language with Convolutional Neural Network for Machine Translation
raw_candidates.definition: Translation model (Kalchbrenner & Blunsom, 2013) pairing a convolutional sentence encoder with an RNN decoder, evaluated by rescoring and perplexity.

raw_candidates.name: Generating text with recurrent neural networks (Sutskever, Martens & Hinton)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Sutskever's 2011 text-generation work directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by proving, in the first author's own prior work, that a large RNN trained well could generate coherent sequences as a conditional generator - the decoder half of seq2seq, demonstrated three years early.
raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Text with Recurrent Neural Networks
raw_candidates.definition: Character-level text generation with multiplicative RNNs trained by Hessian-free optimization (Sutskever, Martens & Hinton, ICML 2011), then the largest RNN application reported.

raw_candidates.name: Hessian-free optimization (Martens)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Hessian-free optimization directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by being the training breakthrough that made large RNNs trainable in Sutskever's own research line, establishing that recurrent sequence models could be optimized at scale before he moved to deep LSTMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Text with Recurrent Neural Networks
raw_candidates.definition: Second-order optimizer (Martens, 2010; Martens & Sutskever, 2011) that trains very deep and recurrent networks from random initializations by exploiting curvature.

raw_candidates.name: DistBelief (large-scale distributed deep networks)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: DistBelief directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by being Google's production framework for training very large deep networks across machines - the infrastructure culture and tooling (co-authored by seq2seq's own Quoc Le) in which a 380M-parameter ensemble was a routine training job.
raw_candidates.source_title: Large Scale Distributed Deep Networks (NIPS 2012)
raw_candidates.definition: Google's software framework (Dean et al., 2012) for training deep networks with billions of parameters across thousands of machines, with Downpour SGD and Sandblaster L-BFGS.

raw_candidates.name: AlexNet (deep convolutional networks on GPUs)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: AlexNet directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by proving, in work co-authored by Sutskever himself, that very deep networks trained on GPUs beat engineered pipelines by a wide margin - the template of confidence behind betting on a 4-layer LSTM against the SMT pipeline.
raw_candidates.source_title: Large Scale Distributed Deep Networks (TellWorld papers index)
raw_candidates.definition: Deep convolutional network (Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, 2012) trained on two GPUs that won ILSVRC-2012 by a large margin and ignited the deep-learning era.

raw_candidates.name: Joint language and translation modeling with RNNs (Auli et al.)
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Auli et al.'s joint model directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by showing an RNNLM extended with source-language inputs could predict target words from an unbounded bilingual history - the decoder-conditioning idea, published a year before seq2seq removed the SMT lattice around it.
raw_candidates.source_title: Joint Language and Translation Modeling with Recurrent Neural Networks
raw_candidates.definition: Joint language/translation model (Auli, Galley, Quirk & Zweig, EMNLP 2013) extending the RNNLM with a source-input layer, used to rescore SMT lattices for up to +1.5 BLEU.

raw_candidates.name: Neural network joint model (Devlin et al.)
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The neural network joint model directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by marking the high-water mark of the competing paradigm the same year: a feedforward joint model inside the SMT decoder gained +3.0 BLEU, showing both the appetite for neural translation modeling and the ceiling of keeping the pipeline.
raw_candidates.source_title: Fast and Robust Neural Network Joint Models for Statistical Machine Translation
raw_candidates.definition: Feedforward neural joint model (Devlin et al., ACL 2014) augmenting an n-gram LM with an 11-word source window as a feature inside an SMT decoder.

raw_candidates.name: BLEU metric
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BLEU directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by making the leap legible: a single automatic score on a fixed test set is what let a 34.8-vs-33.3 comparison against the phrase-based baseline count as a breakthrough rather than an anecdote.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks (paper)
raw_candidates.definition: Automatic translation metric (Papineni et al., 2002) scoring n-gram overlap with reference translations; the standard yardstick of MT progress.

raw_candidates.name: WMT'14 English-French dataset (Europarl and web corpora)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The WMT'14 dataset directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by supplying the 12M-sentence (348M-word) parallel corpus and the shared test set on which an end-to-end model could be trained and compared against the best SMT systems at all.
raw_candidates.source_title: GRU explained - the RNN Encoder-Decoder paper (2014)
raw_candidates.definition: The Workshop on Machine Translation 2014 English-French training and test data, assembled from Europarl and large web-crawled parallel corpora.

raw_candidates.name: Neural probabilistic language model (Bengio et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The neural probabilistic language model directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by establishing the two ingredients the decoder is built from - learned word embeddings and a neural next-word distribution - a decade before they were assembled into a conditional generator.
raw_candidates.source_title: Fast and Robust Neural Network Joint Models for Statistical Machine Translation
raw_candidates.definition: Feedforward neural language model (Bengio et al., 2003) that learns distributed word representations jointly with next-word prediction, beating n-gram models.

raw_candidates.name: Gradient clipping (Pascanu, Mikolov & Bengio)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Gradient clipping directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by being part of its published training recipe: the seq2seq models were trained with SGD plus a hard gradient-norm threshold, the Pascanu et al. prescription that keeps deep recurrent training from exploding.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long Short-Term Memory, from First Principles
raw_candidates.definition: Training rule (Pascanu, Mikolov & Bengio, 2013) that rescales the gradient whenever its norm exceeds a threshold, taming exploding gradients in RNNs.

raw_candidates.name: word2vec (efficient estimation of word representations)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: word2vec directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by demonstrating at Google, one year earlier and in the same lab, that learned continuous word vectors trained on huge corpora carry syntactic and semantic structure - the representational bet seq2seq's jointly learned embeddings rely on.
raw_candidates.source_title: Joint Language and Translation Modeling with Recurrent Neural Networks
raw_candidates.definition: Efficient embedding training (Mikolov et al., 2013) producing word vectors whose arithmetic encodes linguistic regularities, trained on billions of words.

raw_candidates.name: Continuous space language models for SMT (Schwenk)
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Schwenk's continuous space language models directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by being the established channel through which neural models first entered production MT - neural scores inside the SMT log-linear model - the incremental path seq2seq's end-to-end break was measured against.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
raw_candidates.definition: Neural language models (Schwenk, 2007; Schwenk et al., 2012) integrated as features in phrase-based SMT, the standard pre-2014 way neural nets improved translation.

raw_candidates.name: Phrase-based statistical machine translation (Koehn et al.)
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Phrase-based SMT directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by constituting the incumbent it had to beat and the comparison harness it beat it in: the paper's headline is a BLEU comparison against a phrase-based system, and its reranking result is computed over that system's 1000-best lists.
raw_candidates.source_title: A review of Sequence to sequence learning with neural networks
raw_candidates.definition: Translation paradigm (Koehn, Och & Marcu, 2003) translating phrase pairs with a log-linear model; the dominant MT approach of 2003-2014.

raw_candidates.name: Backpropagation through time
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Backpropagation through time directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by being the training algorithm that makes 'end-to-end' more than a slogan: one differentiable encoder-decoder trained by BPTT on translation pairs is the paper's entire method.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long Short-Term Memory (Dive into Deep Learning)
raw_candidates.definition: Training method that unrolls a recurrent network over time and applies backpropagation (formalized by Werbos; Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986).

raw_candidates.name: Teacher forcing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Teacher forcing directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by being the decoder's training regime: the decoder is fed the true previous target word at every step, which is what makes conditional language-model training on parallel sentences stable and fast.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks (alphaxiv audio page)
raw_candidates.definition: Training scheme (Williams & Zipser, 1989) for recurrent sequence generators that feeds ground-truth outputs back as inputs during training.

raw_candidates.name: Beam search decoding
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Beam search directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by being its decoding procedure: the reported BLEU scores come from a left-to-right beam search (beam 12) over the decoder's distributions, without which the model's probabilities do not become translations.
raw_candidates.source_title: A review of Sequence to sequence learning with neural networks
raw_candidates.definition: Heuristic search (Lowerre, 1976; standard in speech decoding) that keeps the B most probable partial hypotheses at each step of sequence generation.

raw_candidates.name: Bidirectional recurrent neural networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bidirectional RNNs directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by completing the 1997 recurrent toolkit (with LSTM) that made encoding a whole sentence as state a known technique - though Sutskever's encoder read the source in reverse with a unidirectional LSTM, the bidirectional formulation is the sibling design the encoder-decoder family standardized on within the year.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long short-term memory (Wikipedia)
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent architecture (Schuster & Paliwal, 1997) running separate forward and backward passes so each position sees both past and future context.

raw_candidates.name: Connectionist temporal classification (CTC)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CTC directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by having posed, eight years earlier, the alignment-free sequence transduction problem in trainable form - Graves's CTC showed an RNN could map input sequences to output sequences without pre-segmented alignments, the problem class seq2seq generalized to different alphabets and lengths.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long Short-Term Memory, from First Principles
raw_candidates.definition: Objective (Graves et al., 2006) that trains RNNs to label unsegmented sequences by marginalizing over all alignments, first proven on speech.

raw_candidates.name: Generating sequences with recurrent neural networks (Graves)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Graves's 2013 sequence generation work directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by demonstrating LSTM generation of long structured sequences (handwriting, with a soft attention-like window) a year earlier - the public proof that LSTM decoders could produce extended coherent output, from the same research conversation seq2seq emerged in.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long Short-Term Memory, from First Principles
raw_candidates.definition: LSTM sequence generation (Graves, 2013) for handwriting synthesis, introducing a differentiable soft window over the input - a precursor of attention.

raw_candidates.name: Vanishing gradient analysis (Hochreiter 1991; Bengio et al. 1994)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The vanishing-gradient analyses directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by naming the obstacle the whole design routes around: they are why the field knew a plain RNN encoder would fail on long sentences and why LSTM's constant error carousel was the required component.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence Memory (On Language Modeling notes)
raw_candidates.definition: Formal analyses (Hochreiter, 1991; Bengio, Simard & Frasconi, 1994) proving gradient descent cannot learn long-term dependencies in standard RNNs.

raw_candidates.name: Forget gate (Gers, Schmidhuber & Cummins)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The forget gate directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by completing the LSTM variant that became standard: the ability to reset the cell state is part of the LSTM formulation the seq2seq implementation and all its successors use.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long short-term memory (Wikipedia)
raw_candidates.definition: LSTM extension (Gers, Schmidhuber & Cummins, 2000) adding a learnable forget gate so memory cells can flush stale state.

raw_candidates.name: Elman recurrent network
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The Elman network directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by originating the architecture class the whole lineage descends from: a recurrent hidden state summarizing a sequence so far, the design LSTM encoder-decoders inherit.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long Short-Term Memory (Dive into Deep Learning)
raw_candidates.definition: Simple recurrent network (Elman, 1990) with context units copying the hidden state, the founding RNN design for sequence learning.

raw_candidates.name: Deep belief nets and layer-wise pretraining (Hinton et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Deep belief nets directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by restarting trainable deep learning in Hinton's lab in 2006 - the research program, and the advisor lineage (Hinton supervised Sutskever), inside which deep recurrent sequence models became a plausible bet.
raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Text with Recurrent Neural Networks
raw_candidates.definition: Greedy layer-wise pretraining of deep belief nets (Hinton, Osindero & Teh, 2006) that made deep networks trainable and relaunched deep learning.

raw_candidates.name: IBM statistical machine translation models (Brown et al.)
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The IBM models directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by defining the probabilistic framing it inherited: translation as maximizing P(target|source) over word alignments - seq2seq kept the objective and replaced the alignment machinery with a learned vector.

candidate.name: RNN transducer (Graves)

candidate.definition: Input-output hidden Markov models (Bengio & Frasconi, 1995) modeling conditional distributions over output sequences given input sequences.

candidate.causal_claim: Collobert & Weston's unified architecture directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by normalizing learned embeddings as the input layer of every NLP network by 2008-2011 - the representational default the seq2seq encoder starts from.

candidate.definition: Unified neural architecture (Collobert & Weston, 2008) learning word embeddings jointly across NLP tasks.

candidate.name: Latent semantic analysis (Deerwester et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: LSA directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by originating continuous semantic spaces from co-occurrence statistics - the intellectual ancestor of every learned representation the encoder-decoder manipulates.

candidate.name: Principal component / factor models of language

candidate.name: Machine translation evaluation campaigns (DARPA/NIST OpenMT)
candidate.causal_claim: OpenMT evaluation campaigns directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by building the shared-task culture - common data, blind test sets, one number - that made WMT'14 the arena in which a neural system could publicly dethrone the pipeline.

candidate.definition: Government-run MT evaluation campaigns (NIST OpenMT, from 2002) standardizing datasets and metrics for machine translation.

candidate.name: Workshop on Machine Translation shared tasks (WMT)

candidate.source_title: A review of Sequence to sequence learning with neural networks

candidate.name: Adaptive resonance / sequence chunking psychology (Grossberg)

candidate.name: Shannon information theory

candidate.definition: Shannon's mathematical theory of communication (1948) defining entropy and the channel model underlying MT's noisy-channel framing.

candidate.name: Rule-based machine translation (SYSTRAN)

candidate.name: Hopfield networks

candidate.name: TDNN (time-delay neural network, Waibel)

candidate.source_title: Sequence Memory (On Language Modeling notes)
candidate.definition: Time-delay neural networks (Waibel et al., 1989) applying shared-weight temporal convolutions to speech recognition.

candidate.name: LeNet convolutional networks (LeCun)

candidate.definition: Convolutional networks (LeCun et al., 1998) trained by backpropagation for document recognition.

candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art

candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: The neural network joint model directly enabled Sequence-to-sequence learning's leap by marking the high-water mark of the competing paradigm the same year: a feedforward joint model inside the SMT decoder gained +3.0 BLEU, showing both the appetite for neural translation modeling and the ceiling of keeping the pipeline.

candidate.source_title: GRU explained - the RNN Encoder-Decoder paper (2014)

candidate.source_title: What is sequence-to-sequence learning (guidetoartificialintelligence)

candidate.name: Gated recurrent unit (GRU)

candidate.source_title: GRU explained - the RNN Encoder-Decoder paper (2014)

candidate.source_title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
candidate.definition: Two-layer feedforward model (Chandar et al., 2014) mapping a bag-of-words source representation to a target phrase distribution inside SMT.

raw_candidates.name: Elman recurrent network
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The Elman network directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by being the 'regular recurrent neural network' the paper explicitly extends: Schuster & Paliwal take the standard RNN and run it in both time directions - the base architecture is consumed whole, twice.
raw_candidates.source_title: Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks (Schuster & Paliwal 1997, paper)
raw_candidates.definition: Simple recurrent network (Elman, 1990) with context units copying the hidden state, the standard RNN design BRNN extends.

raw_candidates.name: Forward-backward algorithm (Baum et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The forward-backward algorithm directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by supplying the two-pass template: a forward summary of the past and a backward summary of the future combined at every position is exactly HMM smoothing, the dominant speech tradition in which the BRNN authors worked.
raw_candidates.source_title: Hidden Markov model (knowledge base)
raw_candidates.definition: Dynamic-programming procedure (Baum et al.) computing smoothed state posteriors by combining a forward pass over past observations with a backward pass over future ones.

raw_candidates.name: Backpropagation through time
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Backpropagation through time directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by being its training procedure: the paper's training runs BPTT in both the positive and negative time directions, which is what makes the two-layer design learnable at all.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long Short-Term Memory (Dive into Deep Learning)
raw_candidates.definition: Training method that unrolls a recurrent network over time and applies backpropagation (Werbos; Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986).

raw_candidates.name: Time-delay neural network (Waibel)
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The TDNN directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by defining the limitation it removes: the paper's abstract states the BRNN 'can be trained without the limitation of using input information just up to a preset future frame' - the preset window is the TDNN/MLP design the paper surveys and supersedes.
raw_candidates.source_title: Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks (Schuster & Paliwal 1997, paper)
raw_candidates.definition: Time-delay neural network (Waibel et al., 1989) applying shared-weight temporal convolutions over a fixed input window for speech recognition.

raw_candidates.name: TIMIT database
raw_candidates.causal_claim: TIMIT directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by being the real-data testbed of the paper: the phoneme classification experiments on TIMIT are the evidence that bidirectionality helps on actual speech, not only on artificial data.
raw_candidates.source_title: Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks (Schuster & Paliwal 1997, paper)
raw_candidates.definition: Standard phoneme-labeled speech corpus (Garofolo et al., DARPA TIMIT, 1988-1993) used across speech recognition research.

raw_candidates.name: Hidden Markov models for speech recognition
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: HMMs directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by constituting the speech framework the BRNN was built to serve: the paper's second part estimates conditional posteriors of symbol sequences - the quantities hybrid HMM/ANN recognizers consume.
raw_candidates.source_title: Hidden Markov model (knowledge base)
raw_candidates.definition: Hidden Markov models (Baum et al., 1966-1972), the era-defining probabilistic framework for speech recognition.

raw_candidates.name: Long short-term memory (LSTM)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LSTM directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap only as a coeval sibling: both appeared in 1997, and the BRNN paper uses conventional RNNs throughout - the famous combination (bidirectional LSTM) waited until Graves & Schmidhuber 2005.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long short-term memory (Wikipedia)
raw_candidates.definition: Gated recurrent cell (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) addressing the vanishing gradient problem.

raw_candidates.name: Jordan recurrent network
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The Jordan network directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by being the other founding recurrent design: output-feedback recurrence is part of the 'regular RNN' design space Schuster & Paliwal's extension operates over.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence Memory (On Language Modeling notes)
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent architecture (Jordan, 1986) feeding output units back into the state layer.

raw_candidates.name: Backpropagation algorithm (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Backpropagation directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by being the gradient engine under BPTT, the procedure the paper uses to train both directional layers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long Short-Term Memory (Dive into Deep Learning)
raw_candidates.definition: Gradient-based learning algorithm (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986) computing derivatives through layered networks by the chain rule.

raw_candidates.name: Hybrid HMM/ANN speech recognition (Bourlard & Morgan)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The hybrid HMM/ANN approach directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by defining the job its second half performs: frame-level posterior estimation for HMM decoding is the application frame Graves & Schmidhuber cite (Bourlard & Morgan, 1994) when situating bidirectional phoneme classification.
raw_candidates.source_title: Framewise Phoneme Classification with Bidirectional LSTM Networks (Graves & Schmidhuber 2005)
raw_candidates.definition: Hybrid speech recognition (Bourlard & Morgan, 1994) using neural networks to estimate phoneme posteriors consumed by HMM decoders.

raw_candidates.name: Kalman smoothing (Rauch-Tung-Striebel)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Kalman smoothing directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by originating two-pass estimation: a forward filter pass and a backward smoother pass combined at each time step is the classical form of using past and future evidence jointly, decades before its neural version.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence Memory (On Language Modeling notes)
raw_candidates.definition: Fixed-interval smoother (Rauch, Tung & Striebel, 1965) combining a forward Kalman filter pass with a backward correction pass.

raw_candidates.name: Bidirectional associative memory (Kosko)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bidirectional associative memory directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap only by name and loose analogy: BAMs flow information in two directions between two layers, but store static patterns rather than process sequences - included so the evaluator can separate name resemblance from channel.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence Memory (On Language Modeling notes)
raw_candidates.definition: Two-layer associative memory (Kosko, 1988) with bidirectional connections for pattern recall.

raw_candidates.name: Recurrent neural networks for speech recognition (Robinson)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Robinson's recurrent speech work directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by establishing the immediate practice it extends: RNNs as phoneme classifiers inside hybrid recognizers on TIMIT-style tasks, the exact experimental frame of the BRNN paper.
raw_candidates.source_title: Framewise Phoneme Classification with Bidirectional LSTM Networks (Graves & Schmidhuber 2005)
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent network phoneme classification for hybrid speech recognition (Robinson, 1994), a reference point in the bidirectional LSTM literature.

raw_candidates.name: Multilayer perceptron with fixed input windows
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Windowed MLPs directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by being the baseline structure whose fixed-window limitation the paper's introduction names first: MLPs 'require definition of the size of the input window in advance', the constraint both TDNNs and BRNNs attack.
raw_candidates.source_title: Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks (Schuster & Paliwal 1997, paper)
raw_candidates.definition: Feedforward networks applied to sequences by presenting a fixed-size window of frames as input.

raw_candidates.name: Output delay trick for future context
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The output-delay trick directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by being the partial solution it replaces: Graves & Schmidhuber's retrospective notes that delaying outputs gives a unidirectional net some future context 'but these do not usually make full use of backwards dependencies' - the gap the BRNN closes.
raw_candidates.source_title: Framewise Phoneme Classification with Bidirectional LSTM Networks (Graves & Schmidhuber 2005)
raw_candidates.definition: Practice of delaying target outputs by a few frames so a causal network can peek at near-future inputs.

raw_candidates.name: Viterbi algorithm
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The Viterbi algorithm directly enabled Bidirectional recurrent neural networks' leap by founding the decoding tradition of the speech systems BRNNs feed: posterior sequences are only useful inside a decoder that searches over symbol sequences.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence Memory (On Language Modeling notes)
raw_candidates.definition: Dynamic-programming decoder (Viterbi, 1967) finding the most probable path through a sequence model.

raw_candidates.name: Baum-Welch algorithm

raw_candidates.name: Long short-term memory (LSTM)

raw_candidates.definition: The gated recurrent architecture (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) whose constant error carousel lets a network store information over long lags.

raw_candidates.source_title: Mixture Density Networks (Bishop, 1994)
raw_candidates.definition: Bishop's scheme (1994) in which a neural network outputs the weights, means and variances of a mixture distribution instead of a point prediction.

raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks (Graves, 2013)
raw_candidates.definition: Schuster's 1999 model class combining bidirectional RNNs with mixture density outputs for generative modelling of sequential data.

raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks (Graves, 2013)
raw_candidates.definition: Gers, Schraudolph & Schmidhuber's addition of diagonal connections from the LSTM cell state to its gates, letting gates time their actions precisely.

raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to Forget: Continual Prediction with LSTM (Gers, Schmidhuber & Cummins, 2000)
raw_candidates.definition: The 2000 addition of a learned forget gate to LSTM, allowing memory cells to reset themselves on continual input streams.

raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks (Graves, 2013)
raw_candidates.definition: Tieleman & Hinton's 2012 stochastic gradient method that rescales each gradient by a running average of its recent magnitude.
